title: Tensorflow NPM Packages are shipping TypeScript sources instead of just the distrubtion files [URGENT]
body: This is in my package.json```    "@tensorflow/tfjs": "^2.0.1",```I'm getting this error:```/path/to/project/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/environment.tsTypeScript error in /path/to/project/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/environment.ts(45,3):Property 'platformName' has no initializer and is not definitely assigned in the constructor.  TS2564    43 |   private urlFlags: Flags = {},    44 |   > 45 |   platformName: string,       |   ^    46 |   platform: Platform,    47 |     48 |   // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any```I also tried ` "skipLibCheck": true` in `tsconfig.json` but that didn't work either.> In the case of tfjs, there are actual .ts files (e.g. `node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/environment.ts`) which cause the failure.> Generally npm modules should ship compiled files and their public APIs, so anything happening internally (in js files) should not be reported.Related https://www.reddit.com/r/typescript/comments/hjgd30/skiplibcheck_but_for_ts_files/
comments: ['@jbis9051 can you please provide steps to reproduce above error ?=====', '@rthadur The linked reddit post describes why it\'s an issue better.# Reproduce```shell$ mkdir test$ cd test$ npm init$ npm install --save @tensorflow/tfjs```In `test/node_modules/@tensorflow` there is a bunch of packages:```shell.├── tfjs├── tfjs-backend-cpu├── tfjs-backend-webgl├── tfjs-converter├── tfjs-core├── tfjs-data└── tfjs-layers```Inside all of these packages is something similar to the following:```shell├── tfjs-core│\xa0\xa0 ├── BUILD.bazel│\xa0\xa0 ├── README.md│\xa0\xa0 ├── cloudbuild.yml│\xa0\xa0 ├── development│\xa0\xa0 ├── dist│\xa0\xa0 ├── package.json│\xa0\xa0 ├── scripts│\xa0\xa0 ├── src│\xa0\xa0 ├── test.html│\xa0\xa0 └── tsconfig.test.json```Instead, only the `dist` folder should be there. # Why this is an issue?For starters, including the source files (used for developing) increases package sizes tremendously and unnecessarily. Additionally, and more importantly, if you are using typescript in a project TypeScript will do type checks on the tensorflow source despite excluding `node_modules` and `"skipLibCheck": true` being included in your own `tsconfig.json`. Since most typescript configs don\'t line up with tensorflow\'s typescript config, the compilation will fail. The only workaround is to manually delete the src folders in every folder in `@tensorflow/`.# How do you guys fix it?For TypeScript based packages you should only publish the built (`dist`) files with the deceleration [*.d.ts] files. This will allow `"skipLibCheck": true` to work properly.If you look at bodyPix, that package is setup properly:```test/node_modules/@tensorflow-models└── body-pix ├── README-v1.md ├── README.md ├── cloudbuild.yml ├── diff ├── dist ├── package.json └── run_tests.ts```Despite BodyPix having a `src` directory (https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/tree/master/body-pix/src), only the `dist` folder is published and therefore installed, not the `src` folder.If we go into the dist folder then we can see all the compiled source and deceleration files.=====', 'Same issue here=====', '@tylerzhu-github can you please help with above request ?=====', 'same here=====', "@jbis9051 What version of typescript are you using? Could you post your tsconfig (or a similar tsconfig that reproduces the error), we've been shipping those up to NPM for a while and it would be nice to know why skipLibCheck/exclude does not work in this instance.=====", '@tafsiri Sure. `skipLibCheck` doesn\'t work because, again, those are source Typescript files (`*.ts`) not declaration files (`*.d.ts`). See here https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/compiler-options.html> `--skipLibCheck` | `boolean` | `false` | Skip type checking of all declaration files (`*.d.ts`).Not sure about why exclude doesn\'t work.Version: ` "typescript": { "version": "3.7.5",`Here\'s a TSConfig:```json{ "compilerOptions": { "target": "es5", "lib": [ "dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext" ], "allowJs": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true, "strict": true, "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true, "module": "esnext", "moduleResolution": "node", "resolveJsonModule": true, "isolatedModules": true, "noEmit": true, "jsx": "react", "experimentalDecorators": true }, "include": [ "src" ], "exclude": [ "node_modules" ]}```It isn\'t compatible because `"strict": true,` isn\'t compatible with tensorflow\'s tsconfig. =====', 'Found the bug, it was an errant import path in our source. Should be resolved in the next release goes out.=====', '\\o/=====', 'Yeah, i independently found the problem (using `tsc --traceResolution`), and my workaround right now is to use https://npm.im/patch-package with the following patch:`patches/@tensorflow+tfjs-core+2.0.1.patch````patchdiff --git a/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/kernel_names.d.ts b/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/kernel_names.d.tsindex 126a329..b287921 100644--- a/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/kernel_names.d.ts+++ b/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/kernel_names.d.ts@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@ * limitations under the License. * ============================================================================= */-import { ExplicitPadding } from \'../src/ops/conv_util\',+import { ExplicitPadding } from \'./ops/conv_util\', import { NamedTensorInfoMap, TensorInfo } from \'./kernel_registry\', import { DataType, PixelData } from \'./types\', export declare const Add = "Add",diff --git a/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/kernel_names.ts b/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/kernel_names.tsindex 4e9a822..c998fdb 100644--- a/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/kernel_names.ts+++ b/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/kernel_names.ts@@ -18,7 +18,7 @@ // tslint:disable: variable-name // Unfortunately just enabling PascalCase per file (tslint:enable: // allow-pascal-case) doesn\'t work.-import {ExplicitPadding} from \'../src/ops/conv_util\',+import {ExplicitPadding} from \'./ops/conv_util\', import {NamedTensorInfoMap, TensorInfo} from \'./kernel_registry\', import {DataType, PixelData} from \'./types\',```=====', 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: Set the weight file location of tf.loadLayersModel
body: #### TensorFlow.js version1.3.2#### Describe the problem or feature requestHello. As I tried to create and use a simple model, it seems that the location of the weight file can be set automatically or only the prefix of the path can be set. In the case of me, I want to set the position of the weight like setting the position of the model, but I wonder if there is a reason not to set it.The API I am expecting is as follows.```jsconst loadModel = await tf.loadLayersModel(model.default,{weightPath:weight.default}),```
comments: ["Yes that isn't something we support. The expectation is that the weight file(s) (note there may be multiple files) are stored in the same location to the json file. Is that particularly prohibitive for your use case?=====", "Hi. @tafsiri. Thank you for your response.There are currently two usecases for me.- I am creating and running a model locally. When I load the model and weight files in the build tool (parcel), Build Tool changed the file name, but the file name of the weight also changed, so I felt uncomfortable to do any work.- Only specific extensions are available for cdn, but there is a problem in that we have to use the name of weigth.bin unconditionally because we want to change and use the extension.Of course, I can solve both problems, but it's inconvenient and I was wondering why I didn't specify the file path of the weight. Thanks=====", "Thanks for the info! The renaming of weight files would be an issue because they are specifically referred to by name in the model.json (and have an ordering that is important to maintain—they aren't always in one weights.bin file). You can pass a [weightsPathPrefix](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#loadLayersModel) to loadLayersModel to set a path to a folder containing weights, but it doesn't support arbitrary names for weight files. If you really wanted to get around that you would have to implement a custom IOHandler that supported your renaming conventions, here is the [default HTTP one](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-core/src/io/http.ts#L145)=====", 'Ah ha. Thanks. I think that I can solve this problem because of your info.=====', '**Tensorflow.js version: 2.0.1**I\'m having an issue during this process. The queries on their own, and the `model.json` query in the program, yield `200` status code responses and the correct results.I\'ve tried loading the model in two ways.**Method 1:**```const loadhttp = (url, dir2, dir3) =>  tf.io.http(url, {    weightPathPrefix: `directory_1%2F${dir2}%2F${dir3}%2F`,  }),...let http = loadhttp(model_url, dir2, dir3),tf.loadLayersModel(http).then((model) => {    console.log("Loaded model."),    console.log(model),})```[An example](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#loadGraphModel) from the docs specifies the entire path, so I when do that by adjusting the function to:```const loadhttp = (url) =>  tf.io.http(url, {    weightPathPrefix: before(url, \'model.json\'),  }),const before = (str, sub) => str.substring(0, str.indexOf(sub))```I still get the same result of:```<APP_URL>/o/group1-shard1of1.bin?<Query Params>          => 404 Not Found```**Method 2:**I\'ve adjusted the `model.json` file\'s `weightsManifest` from:```"weightsManifest": [{"paths": [group1-shard1of1.bin"] ...```to```"weightsManifest": [{"paths": ["directory_1%2Fdirectory_2%2Fdirectory_3%2Fgroup1-shard1of1.bin"] ...```(and the JS code to)```const loadhttp = (url) =>  tf.io.http(url),```And it was surprisingly unsuccessful (same incorrect `404` weights URL). My assumption was this directed the second query,  and my only explanation is that this value is being overridden in some way. Although this is the less ideal method, I was fairly certain it would work.=====', 'This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. title: webgpu: batchNorm* related cases fail due to 'The number of storage buffers exceeds the maximum per-stage limit'
body: The number of storage buffers exceeds the maximum per-stage limit.    at ValidateBindingCounts (..<URL>)    at CreateDefault (..<URL>)    at CreateComputePipelineInternal (..<URL>)14Object is an error.    at ValidateObject (..<URL>)    at ValidateGetBindGroupLayout (..<URL>)17Object is an error.    at ValidateObject (..<URL>)    at ValidateBindGroupDescriptor (..<URL>)    at CreateBindGroupInternal (..<URL>)17Object is an error.    at Finish (..<URL>)17Object is an error.    at ValidateObject (..<URL>)    at ValidateSubmit (..<URL>)debug.js:15 FAILED batchNorm4D test-webgpu {"WEBGPU_CPU_FORWARD":false} simple batchnorm4D, no offset, 2x1x1x2Above failure is due to the change https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/24481/6/src/common/Constants.h#42. In those shaders, we used more than 4 storage buffers. It seems that we should use uniform buffer or constant value instead of storage buffer to reduce the binding storage buffer count.
comments: ["@annxingyuan @kainino0x From https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-backend-webgpu/src/kernels/FusedBatchNorm.ts#L43, we can see that FusedBatchNorm has 5 inputs tensors [x as Tensor, mean as Tensor, variance as Tensor, offset as Tensor, scale as Tensor]. If all of them use storage buffer, it will exceed the limitation of webgpu which's max value is 4. However, if we use uniform buffer, it must follow the std140 layout which needs to padding the value in tensor. If the tensor is too big, constant value is also not a good option. Maybe we should consider to use texture to store the last tensor if no storage buffer can be used? =====", 'Hi @Kangz, in the latest Dawn there is a newly-added limitation on the maximum number of storage buffers inside one shader stage (4), while in the current version of TFJS we actually need 5 storage buffers. Some other cases also have the similar issue. For example, fused-conv2d.```    layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 0) writeonly buffer ssbOut {      float result[],    },      layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 1) readonly buffer ssbx {        float x[],      },      layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 2) readonly buffer ssbW {        float W[],      },      layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 3) readonly buffer ssbbias {        float bias[],      },      layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 4) readonly buffer ssbpreluActivationWeights {        float preluActivationWeights[],      },```>Another possible approach would be to use copies to merge some of the inputs into a single input storage buffer that you address at offsets.Well, it looks like a doable method. We can merge some parameters weights into one buffer, for example, the bias, the preluActivation. Or we use readonly texture for each of those parameters. I will take a look.>If this op has 5 inputs, do you need 6 storage buffers (5, plus one for the output)?Oh, yes. It should need 6 storage buffers if op has 5 inputs. =====", "One thing we could do is add support for `GPULimits` in Chromium so TF.js can ask for increased limits (but not work on devices with the bare minimum). And in the meantime we can set the minimum to 6 in Dawn so that TF.js isn't block on it. WDYT? @austinEng @kainino0x ?=====", "Temporary limit change sounds okay with me since we're not testing or shipping on mobile platforms yet. We'll start failing CTS tests that test the limits though.=====", 'sgtm=====', 'fyi: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/25840 should be in Chrome Canary in the next couple of days=====']

title: It should be possible to specify custom paths for multiple WASM binaries.
body: Currently `setWasmPath` accepts a full path to the vanilla WASM binary. Now that we are shipping multiple WASM binaries to support experimental features, users need the ability to specify multiple custom paths. One way to do this would be to change `setWasmPath` to something like `setWasmPrefix`, which would specify a custom directory with multiple WASM binaries.

title: Load a model from url of a .zip / .gz file
body: #### Describe the problem or feature requestAfter pruning/quantization and subsequent conversion to tf js model, it is ideal to host the model files as .zip / .gz fomat in order to make use of the pruned weights. This often leads results in serving smaller files. Is there any feature that loads a model directly from a path or url of the compressed file?  Do you intend to plan on supporting such a feature in the future?How would one go about this way of serving the models currently ?TIA
comments: ['@alokwhitewolf That is a good idea, I believe you are right if you quantize the weights into 8bit/16bit integer, the weight can probably further compressed using zip format. To host all files as a single .gz would be non-trivial, since the model loader has logic that loads the model.json and bin files in order. But you can zip the individual bin file, and create a custom ioHandler to support decompressing.Contributions are welcome, I think this addition would benefit many tfjs users. thanks!=====', '@pyu10055 Thanks for responseI ended up using a version of your second approach to make it work for now. * Changed the `paths` in `weightsManifest` of model.json to ensure that they end with ".bin.gz" rather than ".bin"* I gzippped all the .bin filesSince I was using Google Cloud for hosting the weights, I looked at the [transcoding docs](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/transcoding) and did the followiing -* set `content-type` to \'application/json\' for the gzipped json file and \'application/octet-stream\' for the weights. * set `content-encoding` to "gzip"* Set the `Cache-Control` metadata field for the object to `no-transform`, then the object is served as a compressed object in all subsequent requests, regardless of any `Accept-Encoding` request headers.This makes it work for now.But yeah, it would be good to have this as a feature. I will try to contribute a ioHandler for this. =====', '@alokwhitewolf Cool, basically you are letting browser to handle the decompression. That is very nice. Can you share what level of compression you are getting for the bin files with this approach?=====', 'Roughly around ~3.6x. title: Feature Request: Using Javascript to convert a TensorflowJS model to a TensorflowLite model.
body: Please make the ability to convert TensorflowJS models into TensorflowLite (flatbuffers?) so that they can be used on micro-controllers such as the $100 [Dual Core Arduino Portenta H7 ](https://www.arduino.cc/pro/hardware/product/portenta-h7).I have a working sine function model that loads onto both cores [here](https://github.com/hpssjellis/my-examples-for-the-arduino-portentaH7/blob/master/m09-Tensoflow/a02-EloquentTinyML-to-M4.ino) and runs much faster than TensorflowLite on most boards (I needed to add a delay of 3 microseconds per loop for it even to be visible).TensorflowJS is easier to work with than other forms of Tensorflow. Micro-controllers have a huge hobby and professional following. The ability to convert directly between TensorflowJS and TensorflowLite would dramatically simplify the process of using smaller specific machine learning models.**Note:** The output should be in a ready made model.h file not the regular .tflite file see the explanation [here](https://www.digikey.ca/en/maker/projects/intro-to-tinyml-part-1-training-a-model-for-arduino-in-tensorflow/8f1fc8c0b83d417ab521c48864d2a8ec). Look for:  _I will save everything in just a .h file._ That way the file is ready to upload immediately to a micro-controller. (Probably a good idea to give the user the option to also save as a .tflite file)Reasons to have TensorflowJS convert directly to TensorflowLite:1. Tensorflowjs on a webpage is very similar to a mobileApp. Testing your models on TensorflowJS would be the fastest way to test and make changes before converting the model to a mobile device. 2. TensorflowJS to TensorflowLite for micro-controllers allows programming without learning Java or Python. Micro-controller C++ is reasonably simple.3. The dual core PortentaH7 has C-USB out to video, connections for WebCams and Bluetooth to keyboard or mouse. This makes it similar to how TensorflowJs interacts with ML models.4. As TensorflowLite only has a subset of the functions of Tensorflow, being able to quickly test if your TensorflowJS model can be converted to TensorflowLite would be an asset.Can anyone think of any other reasons?P.S. I have done a fair bit of making TensorflowJS simpler for High School students by converting examples and demos into single file vanilla Javascript [here](https://hpssjellis.github.io/beginner-tensorflowjs-examples-in-javascript/).

title: Error loading exported Keras MobileNetV2
body: #### TensorFlow.js versionTested on 2.0.0 and 2.1.0#### Browser versionChrome 84.0.4147.105#### Describe the problem or feature requestI am trying to export a fine-tuned model from Keras, but I see the error "Unknown layer: Functional". I tried using MobileNetV2 without any modifications and I still get the error.I followed the instructions from [Importing a Keras model into TensorFlow.js](https://www.tensorflow.org/js/tutorials/conversion/import_keras)#### Code to reproduce the bugCreate these two files:`convert.py````pythonimport tensorflow as tfimport tensorflowjs as tfjsmodel = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(include_top=False)tfjs.converters.save_keras_model(model, 'mobilenetv2-tfjs')````index.html````html<html><head><script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tensorflow/tfjs@2.1.0/dist/tf.min.js"></script></head><body><script>tf.loadLayersModel('mobilenetv2-tfjs/model.json')</script></body></html>```Then after installing Anaconda, run:```conda create -n tfjs python=3.7pip install tensorflowjs==2.1.0python convert.pypython -m http.server```Then open `http://localhost:8000` in your browser. The console should display:```Uncaught (in promise) Error: Unknown layer: Functional. This may be due to one of the following reasons:1. The layer is defined in Python, in which case it needs to be ported to TensorFlow.js or your JavaScript code.2. The custom layer is defined in JavaScript, but is not registered properly with tf.serialization.registerClass().```I also tested a simple model, just to make sure it isn't a broad bug:```pythonmodel = tf.keras.models.Sequential([tf.keras.layers.Dense(8)])model.build(input_shape=(1,8,))```And this model loads without any trouble. So I can only assume that there is an unsupported layer inside `MobileNetV2`. But when I print out all the layer types, I do not see anything called "Functional", or anything out of the ordinary:```pythonimport tensorflow as tfmodel = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(include_top=False)print(set([layer.__class__.__name__ for layer in model.layers]))``````{'Conv2D', 'BatchNormalization', 'InputLayer', 'DepthwiseConv2D', 'ZeroPadding2D', 'ReLU', 'Add'}```I also tested the SavedModel converter, exporting the same network with the SavedModel format taking notes from the tutorial [Using the SavedModel format](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/saved_model):```pythonimport tensorflow as tfmodel = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(include_top=False)tf.saved_model.save(model, 'mobilenetv2-savedmodel')```Then running the converter:```tensorflowjs_converter --input_format tf_saved_model mobilenetv2-savedmodel mobilenetv2-tfjs```But this gives a different error (for both 2.0.0 and 2.1.0), which I've pasted here slightly abridged:```Uncaught (in promise) Error: layer: Improper config format: {"node":[{"name":"StatefulPartitionedCall/mobilenetv2_1.00_224/Conv1_pad/Pad/paddings","op":"Const","attr":{"value":{"tensor":{"dtype":"DTINT32","tensorShape":{"dim":[{"size":"4"},{"size":"2"}]}}},"dtype":{"type":"DTINT32"}}}, [...] {"name":"StatefulPartitionedCall/mobilenetv2_1.00_224/block_2_expand/Conv2D_weights","op":"Const","attr":{"value":{"tensor":{"dtype":"DTFLOAT","tensorShape":{"dim":[{"size":"1"},{"size":"generic_utils.js:227)    at CT (serialization.js:31)    at models.js:295    at u (runtime.js:45)    at Generator._invoke (runtime.js:274)    at Generator.forEach.t.<computed> [as next] (runtime.js:97)    at Wm (runtime.js:728)    at o (runtime.js:728)```
comments: ['Solved... I think.It looks like `tfjs.converters.save_keras_model()` does not support functional models. Despite what the error message says, it\'s not really about a specific layer in the original Keras model.The process for saving functional models should look like this:```pythonimport tensorflow as tfimport tensorflowjs as tfjsmodel = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(include_top=False)model.save(\'mobilenetv2.h5\')```Followed by conversion:```tensorflowjs_converter --input_format keras --output_format tfjs_graph_model mobilenetv2.h5 mobilenetv2-tfjs```And using `loadGraphModel()` instead of `loadLayersModel()`:```<html><head><script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tensorflow/tfjs@2.1.0/dist/tf.min.js"></script></head><body><script>tf.loadGraphModel(\'mobilenetv2-tfjs/model.json\')</script></body></html>```I figured this out while looking at the options for `tensorflowjs_converter` and found `tfjs_graph_model`. After Googling that, I found [Importing a TensorFlow GraphDef based Models into TensorFlow.js](https://www.tensorflow.org/js/tutorials/conversion/import_saved_model) which lead me to `loadGraphModel()`.If you see `Improper config format` it might mean that your model was successfully exported, but you need to use `loadGraphModel()`. For the other error `Unknown layer: Functional`, this seems like the kind of error that could have been caught earlier when calling `tfjs.converters.save_keras_model()`.=====', "One more aside, it looks like with tfjs 2 the loadGraphModel method has moved:```javascriptimport { loadGraphModel } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-converter',let model,const setupPage = async () => {    model = await loadGraphModel('mobilenetv2-tfjs/model.json'),}setupPage(),```I couldn't find this in the documentation... maybe this is obvious to folks who are more experienced with modern JavaScript :) I found a hint in the tests [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/e2e/integration_tests/load_predict_test.ts).=====", "One more note, the help for `tensorflowjs_converter` says `--output_format tfjs_graph_model` is the default, but I don't think this is actually true.If you don't specify `tfjs_graph_model` manually, and then try to `loadGraphModel` you will get an error `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read property 'producer' of undefined`.=====", '@kylemcdonald thank you for try it out, if the input type is keras, the default output is tfjs_layers_model.The functional layers has been supported with this PR https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3863=====']

title: SOFT_ONE in tfjs-examples/mnist-acgan/gan.js should be scalar tensor instead of number.
body: #### TensorFlow.js versionv2.0+#### Browser versionGoogle chrome v84.0.4147.125#### Describe the problem or feature requestProblem is located in [gan.js](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-examples/blob/master/mnist-acgan/gan.js) file in tfjs example project demonstrating usage of GANNs. Variable **SOFT_ONE** is declared and defined as `const SOFT_ONE = 0.95`.This variable is used incorrectly in given circumstances. For example: `tf.ones([batchSize, 1]).mul(SOFT_ONE)`.This assumption is based on [following documentation](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#mul) which states that parameter of 'mul' method is tensor - not a number.Incorrect usage also throws following exception: _**Argument 'b' passed to 'mul' must be a Tensor, but got number.**_#### Code to reproduce the bug / link to feature request`const SOFT_ONE = 0.95,tf.ones([2, 2]).mul(SOFT_ONE),`.I have also proposed a solution to this issue in following[ pull request](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-examples/pull/351).

title: Threaded build of WASM backend should support Node.
body: Currently we exclude Node from the threaded build of the WASM backend (https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3829). The threaded build fails in Node for several reasons:- In Emscripten SDK v.1.39.15 (this is what we're using), the web worker code includes the line `Worker = nodeWorkerThreads.Worker`, which is problematic because `Worker` is undefined. Emscripten v.1.39.16 contains a fix for this: https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/commit/cccf9bf53671a4d6e865420922295b556b292b59. We need to update to 1.39.16 (which means addressing several compile errors). - We are currently using the `Blob` API for the threaded build in order to narrow down the `wasm.mainScript` to just the Emscripten-generated WASM module, rather than our entire `tf-backend-wasm.js` bundle (which contains the Emscripten-generated WASM module). We need to narrow it down because the worker ingests `wasm.mainScript` through `importScripts`, and the worker can't ingest our whole bundle because it contains TFJS code that the worker doesn't know anything about (hence it immediately throws an error if attempting to ingest the whole bundle because `runKernel` is undefined). We need to polyfill `Blob` for Node, the way we do for `fetch`. - Launching a simple node program with the necessary experimental flags to ask for the threaded + SIMD build (e.g. `node index.js --experimental-wasm-simd --experimental-wasm-threads --experimental-wasm-bulk-memory`) fails with the following message: > requested a shared WebAssembly.Memory but the returned buffer is not a SharedArrayBuffer, indicating that while the browser has SharedArrayBuffer it does not have WebAssembly threads support - you may need to set a flag (on node you may need: --experimental-wasm-threads --experimental-wasm-bulk-memory and also use a recent version)` (from Emscripten).

Reduces input along the dimensions given in reduction_indices. Unless keep_dims is true, the rank of the tensor is reduced by 1 for each entry in reduction_indices. If keep_dims is true, the reduced dimensions are retained with length 1."And this structure belongs to the function tf.reduce_sum() and tf.reduce_max() that I used in the Tensorflow model. I converted the Tensorflow as Saved_model format (*.pb) and then converted it to TFJS. Any help is appreciated, thank you. #### Code to reproduce the bug / link to feature requestIf you would like to get help from the community, we encourage using Stack Overflow and the [`tensorflow.js`](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/tensorflow.js) tag.GitHub issues for this repository are tracked in the [tfjs union repository](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues).Please file your issue there, following the guidance in [that issue template](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md).

I tried with 2.1.0, 2.0.1, 1.7.4. I tried to downgrade my angular version to ^8. I tried ^10. Angular uses es5 and webpack. Can it be related? =====", 'I also have this issue, you found a way to handle this issue?=====', '@jinjingforever gentle ping if you got chance to look in to this issue, thank you =====', 'One way to fix this is to add `"@types/emscripten"` to the `compilerOptions.types` field in `tsconfig.app.json`. Here is what mine looks like:```{ "extends": "./tsconfig.json", "compilerOptions": { "outDir": "./out-tsc/app", "types": [ "@types/emscripten" ] }, "files": [ "src/main.ts", "src/polyfills.ts" ], "include": [ "src/**/*.d.ts" ]}```(if you don\'t have `tsconfig.app.json`, just edit the same field in `tsconfig.json`)The reason is that: `EmscriptenModule` is defined in the `emscriptem` types package in the global namespace. By default, when an angular app is generated, the `compilerOptions.types` field is set to an empty array, which means the compiler will not automatically add these "globals" to your app.Another fix would be to remove the empty `compilerOptions.types` field from `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.app.json`.Please give it a try, and let me know any problems. I will also add this to our README file.=====', 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: [webgl] allow direct WebGL tensor creation/retrieval using texture handle
body: Please make sure that this is a feature request. As per our [GitHub Policy](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/ISSUES.md), we only address code/doc bugs, performance issues, feature requests and build/installation issues on GitHub. tag:feature_template**System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): 2.4.0- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No):**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**For ML models that involve media processing (i.e. bodypix model), there are couple places where expensive data copying could happen: 1. Creating tensor from result of video processing pipeline. Although TFJS has fromPixels API, but it requires a html element (video/image), for data that is processed on GPU it will need some work-around (download to cpu or create html element)2. tensors from the ML execution can not be executed on GPU after the inference, unless using TFJS op APIs. If you have post-processing steps after the ML model execution that need to be executed on GPU, you will end up downloading the tensors and re-upload again.Proposing two new tensor APIs to solve above problems, these APIs target tensors that are located on WebGL backend:1. create tensor using WebGL texture handle, this allows data from GPU pre-processing steps to be converted to tensor.2. retrieve texture handle for tensor, this would prevent downloading the tensor from GPU and enable continue post-processing on GPU.**Will this change the current api? How?**This would not change any of the current APIs, and the proposed APIs shall throw exception for tensors that are not on WebGL backend.**Who will benefit with this feature?**Media processing pipeline that utilize TFJS for model execution with WebGL acceleration. **Any Other info.**

title: [Question] How to best time-profile a TFJS workflow?
body:
This template is for miscellaneous issues not covered by the other issue categories.For questions on how to work with TensorFlow.js, or support for problems that are not verified bugs in TensorFlow.js, please go to [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/tags/tensorflow.js).### Question DescriptionHey, I have a TFJS webapp that takes in frames from a Video, does some pre-processing, passes it into a TFJS Model (converted from a TF Frozen Model), post-processes output and renders that back to a canvas using custom code written in WebGL.
I am unable to get proper timing splits between Preprocessing (which includes fromPixels), Model Inference Time and Post Processing. Here are the things that I tried to time the application:- console.time- performance.now- tf.Profile (which gives kernelTimeMs)None of the above methods gave representative numbers. One thing I noticed is that the Datasync (downloading/uploading of buffers to and from GPU, correct me if I am wrong) call is taking about 90% of the time as compared to the Kernel Operations. I've read in some of the issues that the execute function just assembles/prepares the Kernel according to the TF graph along with the weights and doesn't actually execute them until a Datasync operation is called? Does this lead to the timing discrepancy that I'm noticing? Kindly help me clarify, thank you!
comments: ["Hello, this sort of question is better suited for StackOverflow. This issues list is for bugs and feature requests. Thanks and please use the tag 'tensorflow.js' on your StackOverflow question to makes sure it's discoverable.=====", "Hey, I noticed a lot of timing discrepancy in the [TFJS Benchmarking Tool](https://tensorflow.github.io/tfjs/e2e/benchmarks/local-benchmark/index.html) while testing my custom models as well as the ones provided in the list.The aggregate kernel-wise timings don't add up. They always exceeded in the case of 'USE - Batch Size 30' (but still relatively close to the Average Inference Time over 50 runs) and they are always very low compared to the Average for the 'USE - Batch Size 1' model. I thought it was to do with the batch size, so tested all the listed models which had batch size 1, and indeed they all had timing discrepancies => Aggregate Kernel-wise timings didn't add up to the average inference time. Can you tell me what could be happening? When I used to test using the same tool (about 2 months back) the timings always added up (or very close to the average) which is not happening now. @rthadur, request to reopen the issue=====", 'Hey, any leads as to why this is happening?=====', "Hi @sacredvoid, the numbers in the kernel-wise timings don't add up because they run in debugMode, which is much slower. But the ratio between these kernel-wise timings hold. So if you use the model inference time multiply by the ratio, you will get the actual time spent for the kernel. Regarding GPU downloading and uploading time, when kernel code finishes, it doesn't know whether computation is done on GPU. When trying to downloading data from GPU, it will wait till data is ready and download it. So when you benchmark, record the time after data sync, which will reflect the actual time taken to compute.=====", "@lina128 thanks for your time, a couple more questions> So if you use the model inference time multiply by the ratio, you will get the actual time spent for the kernelAttaching a PDF to Facedetector Kernel Timings (which don't add up). Can you tell me with the help of the benchmark below of what you meant by multiplying with ratio?[issue_benchmark.pdf](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/files/5284356/issue_benchmark.pdf)> when kernel code finishesThis means when it's done compiling the webgl kernel for that operation? So it doesn't actually do the computation till after a datasync is called?=====", "So you add up all the time in the kernel time(ms) column. Then for each row, you take the kernel time and divided by the total time. I use expo-camera takePictureAsync function : https://docs.expo.io/versions/latest/sdk/camera/#takepictureasync.However, I looked for a functional example of tfjs-react-native use with a local model, and so a call of https://js.tensorflow.org/api_react_native/latest/#bundleResourceIO like in https://blog.tensorflow.org/2020/02/tensorflowjs-for-react-native-is-here.html (with burger_not_burger.json and burger_not_burger_weights.bin) but I didn't find anything (except theses burgers but without the model files so... The model.json / model_weights.bin is always big and we can't use any other format such as SavedModel, frozenModel or tflite. I false do you any idea what could go wrong here ?On the other hand I tried to use a local classification model too : https://tfhub.dev/google/tfjs-model/imagenet/mobilenet_v2_035_224/classification/3/default/1I did the same : - Downloaded the file and extract it- Got the model.json file- Used the command "cat" to concatenate group1-shard1of2 to group1-shard2of2 into a 6 529ko model_weights.binAnd into my app :- Loaded my model with tf.loadGraphModel(bundleResourceIO(modelJson, modelWeightsId)) **It works**- Trying to classify the image returned by expo-camera with this code : `        const imageAssetPath = Image.resolveAssetSource({ uri })        const imgB64 = await FileSystem.readAsStringAsync(imageAssetPath.uri, {            encoding: FileSystem.EncodingType.Base64,        })        const imgBuffer = tf.util.encodeString(imgB64, 'base64').buffer,        const raw = new Uint8Array(imgBuffer)        const imageTensor = decodeJpeg(raw)        const predictions = model.classify(imageTensor)`And got the following error :_Error: The shape of dict['images'] provided in model.execute(dict) must be [-1,224,224,3], but was [300,300,3]_It seems pretty classic, I've seen this error on numerous posts and I did try a lot of things : to reshape or resize my tensor but I never successed to make it work... **Could you tell me how to make it work ?****Am I doing something wrong ?** I start to think only pre-trained models (https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models ) work with tfjs react-native ^^'That's pretty sad because I wanted to train my own models and use it into my app.I also saw this post but there was not really an answer : https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/3070Thank you in advance for your answer, and have a good day.
comments: ["Hi thanks for the details in your issue, I'll split my response into two parts:### Error loading model / app crashHaving more debug information here would be helpful, if the app crashes before the javascript catch block gets to run, I would suggest looking at the device logs between the app starting and the attempt to load a model/crash. More info on device logs are [available here](https://reactnative.dev/docs/debugging#native-debugging) on the react native docs (in particular see the accessing console logs section). There should be some error message given in those logs for the crash.### Shape error on classificationThis part demonstrates that you can indeed load local models (which is great!). However when you try and run a prediction you get an error. Let me try and explain `shape of dict['images'] provided in model.execute(dict)[-1,224,224,3], but was [300,300,3]`.- Your image dimensions are 300 px * 300 px * 3 channels.- The model expects images of are 224 px * 224 px * 3 channels. So you need to [resize your image](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#image.resizeBilinear).- Further more the model expects inputs to be 'batched'. The -1 means it can take an arbitrary number of 224x224x3 images (constrained by on-device memory). So once you have an imageTensor of the correct size you can turn into into a 'batch of 1' by calling [tf.expandDims](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#expandDims) on the imageTensor. This will give you a shape of [1,224,224,3] which you should be able to pass to the model.---Btw interesting approach to unsharding model weights by using `cat`, hadn't thought of that before. But I wouldn't expect that to work without editing the model.json since the model.json references the different shards. I'm surprised that the second example loads (and is certainly something I will look into if I get some time). We do [plan on adding support](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/3197#issuecomment-631137219) to the tfjs-converter to unshard tfjs graph models using that tool. title: Cannot use addWeight with constraint in CustomLayer
body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js 2.4.0- This issue occurs both on Node.js and in the browserThanks for this wonderful library :-)**Scenario**See fiddle https://jsfiddle.net/fj2d6Luw/8/ (inspired from [this gist](https://gist.github.com/caisq/33ed021e0c7b9d0e728cb1dce399527d))* Creating a custom layer* Adding a constraint in the build method, while using `getWeight` function```js    this.x = this.addWeight('x', shape, 'float32', tf.initializers.ones(), null, true, tf.constraints.minMaxNorm({minValue: 0.95, maxValue: 1.05}) ),```* Logging the value of the variable in `call````js call(input) {    return tf.tidy(() => {    	const xRead = this.x.read(),      const k = tf.pow(xRead, this.alpha),      xRead.print(),      return tf.add(input[0], k),    }),  }```**Describe the current behavior**The variable is not impacted by the constrained during training : ```"Tensor    1""Epoch 0: loss = 3.0572354793548584""Tensor    0.947640061378479""Epoch 1: loss = 2.5550408363342285""Tensor    0.9010470509529114""Epoch 2: loss = 2.146026611328125""Tensor    0.8594121932983398""Epoch 3: loss = 1.8105026483535767""Tensor    0.8220672011375427""Epoch 4: loss = 1.5334960222244263""Model saved."```**Conclusion** :  the variable is going under the constraint of minValue: 0.95**Describe the expected behavior**The variable should be impacted by the constraint and stay in the minValue-maxValue range### Other consideration* By looking in the code, it seems that the [LayerVariable.write](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-layers/src/variables.ts#L95) method is never called* I faced this issue with different constraint and i'm just using `tf.constraints.minMaxNorm`for the example* Might be related to #3345

title: Tensorflowjs expects 3 Dimensions, even though I trained it with 2 in Python
body: I am trying to test a Model which I trained using XOR-Operator values in Python:```x_train = [[1,0],[0,1],[0,0],[1,1]]x_label = [1,1,0,0]model = keras.Sequential([    keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(2,1)),    keras.layers.Dense(8, activation="relu"),    keras.layers.Dense(2, activation="softmax")])model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",metrics=["accuracy"])model.fit(x_train, x_label, epochs=15)prediction = model.predict([[5,5]])print("Prediction: ", np.argmax(prediction[0]))```It works great in Python, but when I transform it into a Tensorflow JS file (model.json), it doesn't work anymore:```tfjs.converters.save_keras_model(model, "test_model")```As you can see above, I trained it with `input_shape=(2,1)`. But when I try it in Nodejs, I get the Error: ```ValueError: Error when checking : expected flatten_input to have 3 dimension(s), but got array with shape [2,1]```My JS Code:```tf.loadLayersModel(model_url).then((model)=>{        const input = tf.tensor([1,1],[2,1], "int32"),        const prediciton = model.predict(input)        console.log(prediciton),        response.send(prediciton),        return null,    }).catch((e)=>{        console.log(e),    }),```Thank you!**System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): Yes- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): Firebase Function- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): 2.4.0

Try```const input = tf.tensor([[5,5]], "int32"),```To make sure its working. And then try```const input = tf.tensor([[1,1],[2,1]], "int32"),```Note the extra square brackets around your input arrays. =====', '@tafsiri When I try `const input = tf.tensor([[5,5]], "int32"),` it stops because the second parameter should be the Shape,When I try `const input = tf.tensor([[1,1],[2,1]], "int32"),`, it gives me the same error:`ValueError: Error when checking : expected flatten_input to have 3 dimension(s), but got array with shape [1,2]`=====', 'Ah yes I think misread one part of your original snippet, yes you need to create a tensor of the appropriate shape (2,1) and then expand it into a batch (i think this is the step that is missing).You can call [tf.expandDims](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#expandDims) on your input tensor to convert it to a batch of one. title: Allow user to insert custom metadata into the model.json file
body: Please make sure that this is a feature request. As per our [GitHub Policy](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/ISSUES.md), we only address code/doc bugs, performance issues, feature requests and build/installation issues on GitHub. tag:feature_template**System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): 2.4.0- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No):**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**User would like to insert custom defined metadata information into the model, currently the [model definition](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/c891e3b70c907ba09481af4d429fcc75c0c8055f/tfjs-core/src/io/types.ts#L228) contains the userDefinedMetadata field that can be used for this purpose.potentially user can specify an external file that contains the metadata information, which allow user to include metadata that is not json compatible.**Will this change the current api? How?**1. The python converter command line should provide a new parameter to inserting user defined metadata. 2. The graph model class should expose the field.**Who will benefit with this feature?****Any Other info.**
comments: ['A common need for any classifier model is a mapping between classifier outputs and class names. E.g., for our YAMNet model on TF-Hub, the TF2 SavedModel includes the "class map" as an asset and this can be looked up to annotate predictions, as shown in the usage https://tfhub.dev/google/yamnet/1 and we would like to do the same for the TF-JS version https://tfhub.dev/google/tfjs-model/yamnet/tfjs/1Related issues: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/762 https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/1596One thought about using userDefinedMetadata: Inspecting model.json shows that this field is currently being used to hold a "signature". Is this only for informational purposes or does anything in TF-JS rely on the signature being present here? If we want to transport additional metadata through this field, we would need to merge whatever the user supplies with whatever is already present. I assume we want userDefinedMetadata to be a mapping from string keys to arbitrary json values, and the user can supply an arbitrary number of json files to include?=====', '@plakal Thank you for pointing out that signature is currently in the userDefinedMetadata. Signature is used by the GraphModel class, it would be better moved out of userDefinedMetadata field, and leave the userDefinedMetadata open.=====', 'Hi @plakal Thank you for providing the YAMNET use case, I think it definitely fits the purpose of this proposal. A bit of more detail of what we are imagining to support: 1. During conversion, user can provide an arbitrary number of json files, which converter can digest and store in userDefinedMetadata field, each json object keyed by a user provided name. 2. In client side, during graph load, tfjs library will load the field in memory and return as part of the model. Then user can access the object through the model. Also thank you for pointing out the signature field, as Ping said, the signature is converted from SavedModel and is used to distill the inference graph for execution. And this field is not supposed to be accessible or mutated, so we should move this out.=====', 'Sounds great, thanks!=====', "Thanks for the fast work! Is there any documentation for the new feature and how to use it when converting a model to TF-JS? I'd like to try this with YAMNet.=====", "Hi @plakal, we just merged it to master, it will be released with version 2.8.0, we are targeting a release next week. For the time being, if you want to try it out, you can check out master, and use the python converter from your local directory. I will update the readme once the 2.8.0 is released. For local testing for now, you can append this flag to the converter: `--metadata=key:path/metadata.json`. To provide multiple metadata files, separate each key/filepath pair with comma. And then after you load the model, you can access the metadata from `model.metadata` using the key, such as `model.metadata['key']`.====="]

How?**It could be a new function, perhaps`tf.image.gaussianBlur(image, params...)`?It could also be done as a layer. A layer would be more efficient for repeated invocations, because a layer could build its internal kernel just once, when `.build` is called.```const gaussianFilter = tf.layers.gaussianFilter(params)gaussianFilter.apply(image)```I have a 2-dimensional implementation in mind for images, but it could be useful in n-dimensions for general signal processing.**Who will benefit with this feature?**This would benefit myself, and other developers who work on vision and image processing systems in the browser.**Any Other info.**I already solved this for use in my own work, and am volunteering to contribute my code to the greater community. I can make the API conform to whatever the maintainers think best, and would like a consensus on the API before getting started on that. If this feature is undesirable to this project, feel free to close this feature request and I'll publish it as an independent package on NPM. Thanks!

title: TensorFlow.js cannot be bundled because it imports a module `seedrandom` which is actually a CommonJS module
body: **System information**:- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): No- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): macOS 10.15.6- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): `2.4.0`- Browser version: recent Chrome**Describe the current behavior**: ES module bundler complains when bundling TensorFlow.js, because it imports a module `seedrandom` which is actually a CommonJS module.**Describe the expected behavior**: Running TensorFlow.js through an ES module bundler should not generate errors.**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**: https://github.com/jameshfisher/tfjs-seedrandom-es-module-bug**Context:** I want to use [TensorFlow.js](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs) in the browser. I'm using [rollup](https://rollupjs.org/) to bundle my app for the browser.The TensorFlow.js source [imports from `seedrandom` in several places](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/69dfce1f988d516b148f7e961490cc6acf0880ba/tfjs-core/src/ops/rand_util.ts#L18). This [comes through in the ES modules distributed via npm](https://unpkg.com/browse/@tensorflow/tfjs-core@2.4.0/dist/ops/rand_util.js).To find the module `seedrandom` imported by TensorFlow, I'm using the plugin `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve`. This does find the `node_modules/seedrandom` package.Unfortunately, `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve` does not find an ECMAScript module in the seedrandom package. So instead, it decides to bundle [the seedrandom `index.js`](https://unpkg.com/browse/seedrandom@2.4.3/index.js). But this is a CommonJS module, not an ES module.As a result, rollup gives me errors like `alea is not exported by node_modules/seedrandom/index.js`, and the browser gives me errors like `require is not defined`.I think the _right_ solution is for the seedrandom package to provide an ES module. [I noted this here.](https://github.com/davidbau/seedrandom/issues/72) The alternative is for TensorFlow to stop importing from a package that doesn't provide an ES module.(You might say "well you just need to use a CommonJS->ES transpiler, like @rollup/plugin-commonjs". I'm reluctant to do so, because this transformation is gross, and in general, impossible.)

comments: ["AFAIK mobilenet is usually trained with at most 224x224 pixels with other common sizes being 128, 160, and 192 pixels.This means that inputs shouldn't be significantly larger than that. You may want to consider doing it once (possibly on node) and saving the embeddings so that you can re-use them.=====", "The [splice](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/splice) takes slice of array each time it's called, so similar to batching.> here is a link to my codepen, I tried your [codepen](https://codepen.io/tafsiri/pen/zYBOwVB?editors=1111), even that has the same issue, I will share a gif and that would probably explain the issue, it seems to be a memory leakage issue, observe the GPU memory used(Dedicated):![Mem Leak](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20347013/95144050-4db28a00-0795-11eb-8373-9e88138eacd9.gif)I had to close the browser tab, otherwise the screen would have gone blank and I couldn't have recorded it.> You may want to consider doing it once (possibly on node) and saving the embeddings so that you can re-use them.I want to use this model on frontend side, so that might not be possible. With the two steps above you should save a bunch of GPU memory. Try the two steps above and let us know if that helps.I\'ve [updated the codepen](https://codepen.io/tafsiri/pen/zYBOwVB?editors=1011) to include the steps above.cc @annxingyuan who suggested using the flag mentioned in step 2.=====', "For your node example, I didn't look closely but I think you should also do the embedding in batches and dispose the output tensors periodically if that is possible. =====", 'Thanks @tafsiri @annxingyuan ,the key was `tf.env().set("WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD", 0)` to solve the issue for me, dispose() function rather slows down the whole embedding process for me, so I had to remove it.Thanks=====', 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: [webgl] Debug mode errors out for modularized matMul.
body: Failing test: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/e2e-custom-dense/tfjs-core/src/debug_mode_test.ts#L102In WebGL when we read an output texture we "decode" it by copying its values densely to a new texture in order to ultimately download the smallest possible texture from the GPU (e.g., a 2x2 texture with 4 values is copied to a 1x1 texture with all 4 values stuffed into the RGBA channels). This means the WebGL backend temporarily registers an extra dataId during decoding. So this test fails because in WebGL2 we read from the GPU asynchronously and the profiler catches the WebGL backend before it has had a chance to clean up after its decoder. This errors out because in debug mode, with the `IS_TEST` flag enabled we check each kernel for memory leaks. To address this we could either explicitly exclude decode textures from numDataIds count, or we could make the profiler asynchronous so we wait for decoding to complete before counting dataIds.

title: tfjs-node does not implement kernel FlipLeftRight
body: Both [BlazeFace](https://tfhub.dev/tensorflow/tfjs-model/blazeface/1/default/1) and [HandDetector](https://tfhub.dev/mediapipe/tfjs-model/handdetector/1/default/1) models work just fine in NodeJS using tensorflow backend  The issue is in how post-processing is done in JS code which uses `FlipLeftRight` kernel func to reorient input for better second-pass detection.So if you use tfjs examples, you'll run into this issue> Error: Kernel 'FlipLeftRight' not registered for backend 'tensorflow'Unfortunately, those models are internally used by several others as well such as `FaceMesh` and `HandSkeleton` which makes list of affected models quite long.Request is to implement `FlipLeftRight` in tfjs-node - expectation is to have feature parity between main backends. Also, is there a matrix of implemented features per backend?Environment: TFJS 3.6.0 on Ubuntu 20.04
comments: ['@vladmandic can you please check for a similar issue [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/2329) =====', "There is no version conflict and I'm running latest TFJS 2.6.0. Just to confirm, I created a simple test that only has `tfjs-node` listed in `package.json`, zero other libraries so there is nothing to have conflict with.And I did note the issue <https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/3883> that clearly lists that forwardFunc is not implemented in `tensorflow` kernel  And it's easy to check:```shellnm -D node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-node/deps/lib/libtensorflow.so | grep forwardFunc```function is not present in tensorflow.so shared library which is the backend for `tfjs-node` (unless it's supposed to use a fallback defined in `@tensorflow/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts`).=====", "I'm going to rename this issue, because the underlying issue is that as mentioned in #3883 blazeface and handpose run kernels that are not implemented in the node.js backend. The error message is a bit confusing to that can be improved as well. I'll file a separate issue for that.=====", 'i understand the need for better error message, but will this feature request to actually implement kernel function stay open and eventually be completed?=====', "I'll try and get an update on this.=====", "I get`(node:15556) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Error: Backend name 'webgl' not found in registry`with node-gpu on Windows 10=====", "i've tested with tfjs 3.0.0 and error message is improved:```Error: Kernel 'FlipLeftRight' not registered for backend 'tensorflow'```now the remaining part is to actually implement function `FlipLeftRight` for NodeJS (backend: tensorflow).@rthadur @tafsiri and plans for implementing this? the issue is open and not even assigned.=====", 'Usually feature request are prioritized by the team and are assigned later , hopefully it will get picked up soon. I am tagging this for contributions welcome if any one interested. cc @pyu10055 @lina128 @mattsoulanille @jinjingforever =====', "@rthadur I am interested in implementing this if you're still accepting external contributors.=====", '@DCtheTall please go-ahead , thanks for your interest.=====', "@rthadur you're welcome! I was wondering if there is a place in tfjs-node which would be a good example of how you typically implement new kernel functions for Node.JS. Just an example of what to go off of should be enough for me to hack something together for a PR=====", 'Thank you @DCtheTall! This [PR](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/4348) might be a good example of adding missing ops to node JS, and this [doc](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING_MISSING_OP.md) might also be helpful. Really appreciate it! =====', '@jinjingforever thank you for the links. This should be all I need to get started!=====', '@rthadur @jinjingforever I have opened a [#5261](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/5261) which implements this function for Node.JS. Lmk if anything else needs to be done.=====', 'Thank you @DCtheTall for the PR! =====', 'This change will be available in next release , thank you so much @DCtheTall for your contribution.=====', "Sorry, thanks to @mattsoulanille, looks like the underlying TF C API (1.15) doesn't support this op. It is not supported in the latest version (2.5) either.What is the right approach to support this kind of ops? (@pyu10055 @lina128 @mattsoulanille). Thanks!=====", "Hi @jinjingforever, I see that there's a ScaleAndTranslate in the c API: https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/cc/class/tensorflow/ops/scale-and-translateCan we use that for FlipLeftAndRight?=====", "If ImageProjectiveTransformV3 is available in the c API, it's even better, it's easier to express flip with an Affine transformation matrix: https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/ImageProjectiveTransformV3=====", 'Thank you @lina128! Maybe we could use "reverse" to do the flip, i.e. reverse on the \'H\' dimension: `tf.reverse(image, [2])`?Also, there might be a bug in the current tfjs flipLeftRight implementations that might need to be fixed first. Will discuss with @lina128 offline. =====', 'reverse sounds good to me.=====', "@lina128 thanks for the reply. I'd be happy to assist if I can with any other work needed to reland my original PR=====", 'Thanks @DCtheTall! After that is merged, it would be great if you could help refactor your PR to use "reverse" to implement flipLeftRight in node. Really appreciate it! =====', '@jinjingforever SGTM. Really appreciate your help!=====", '@jinjingforever @lina128 I just uploaded a PR that implements the kernel using reverse. Let me know if this is what you had in mind 😄 =====']

title: VRAM hosting of convolution output
body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): Experimental only- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): Yes**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**Current behaviour, as I understand it, is that TF treats each of its back end components as a selection of bulk operator implementations running on different substrates. The substrate I'm interested in particular is the GPU, more specifically GLSL math bindings.For certain computer vision related applications, it is desirable to have the operation (e.g. 2d or 3d convolution) collect data from one or more VRAM buffers, and retain the output in VRAM buffers also. This facilitates bridging operators against large pools of data without having to round-trip that data across the bus, and also facilitates building non-AI output processing whose goal is to use the output as vertex, texture, colours, etc. in a render pipeline.Caveat: I am not an expert at TensorFlow, and although I've read the code and partially understand it, I don't have a full and deep understanding of what it's capable of.**Will this change the current api? How?**This would extend the current API. I am not specific in exactly how. I think it would suffice to be able to pass a GL buffer reference as an input, and receive one as an output, and then skip whatever parts of the CPU-GPU bandwidth utilization doing so makes redundant. I would leave the responsibility for getting data into and out of the GPU in the appropriate format outside of Tensorflow as a preprocessing step, since there are potentially lots of different ways to do that.**Who will benefit with this feature?**Anyone whose goal is to synthesize or augment still or video images using AI. Video encode/decode/edit/transcode pipelines. Advanced upsampling, modification or XR features implemented in the client. Probably other people too.**Any Other info.**My personal goal is to make it possible to deliver higher resolution video without increasing bandwidth and hosting costs, or else to deliver the same quality video for less bandwidth, by taking advantage of idle client GPU.

title: Floor kernel for the wasm backend
body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): 2.6.0- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): I can certainly try to help, but I'm a complete newbie with tensorflow.**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**Currently the `cpu` and `webgl` backends support the floor kernel, but the `wasm` backend doesn't.**Any Other info.**The `tfjs-node` backend seems to be several hundred times faster then the browser `cpu` backend when training the [mnist-acgan](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-examples/tree/master/mnist-acgan) in the `tfjs-examples` repo. This is at least partly due to the `tfjs-node` backend being multi-threaded, but I'm guessing it's also due to its use of SIMD operations.After seeing the [blazeface benchmarks](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/tree/master/tfjs-backend-wasm#face-detector) showing the SIMD + multi-threading performance of the `wasm` backend, I thought that maybe it would get closer to node's and webgl's performance, and that's what led me to posting this feature request. I'm not sure if there are other kernels missing from the `wasm` backend that would prevent the `mnist-acgan` example from running, but here's the code for the generator and discriminator, copied from [`mnist-acgan/gan.js`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-examples/blob/master/mnist-acgan/gan.js):```jsfunction buildGenerator(latentSize) {  const cnn = tf.sequential(),  cnn.add(tf.layers.dense({units: 3 * 3 * 384, inputShape: [latentSize], activation: 'relu'})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.reshape({targetShape: [3, 3, 384]})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2dTranspose({filters: 192,kernelSize: 5,strides: 1,padding: 'valid',activation: 'relu',kernelInitializer: 'glorotNormal'})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.batchNormalization()),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2dTranspose({filters: 96, kernelSize: 5, strides: 2, padding: 'same', activation: 'relu', kernelInitializer: 'glorotNormal'})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.batchNormalization()),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2dTranspose({filters: 1, kernelSize: 5, strides: 2, padding: 'same', activation: 'tanh', kernelInitializer: 'glorotNormal'})),  const latent = tf.input({shape: [latentSize]}),  const imageClass = tf.input({shape: [1]}),  const classEmbedding = tf.layers.embedding({inputDim: NUM_CLASSES, outputDim: latentSize, embeddingsInitializer: 'glorotNormal'}).apply(imageClass),  const h = tf.layers.multiply().apply([latent, classEmbedding]),  const fakeImage = cnn.apply(h),  return tf.model({inputs: [latent, imageClass], outputs: fakeImage}),}function buildDiscriminator() {  const cnn = tf.sequential(),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2d({filters: 32, kernelSize: 3, padding: 'same', strides: 2, inputShape: [IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE, 1]})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.leakyReLU({alpha: 0.2})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.dropout({rate: 0.3})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2d({filters: 64, kernelSize: 3, padding: 'same', strides: 1})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.leakyReLU({alpha: 0.2})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.dropout({rate: 0.3})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2d({filters: 128, kernelSize: 3, padding: 'same', strides: 2})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.leakyReLU({alpha: 0.2})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.dropout({rate: 0.3})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.conv2d({filters: 256, kernelSize: 3, padding: 'same', strides: 1})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.leakyReLU({alpha: 0.2})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.dropout({rate: 0.3})),  cnn.add(tf.layers.flatten()),  const image = tf.input({shape: [IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE, 1]}),  const features = cnn.apply(image),  const realnessScore = tf.layers.dense({units: 1, activation: 'sigmoid'}).apply(features),  const aux = tf.layers.dense({units: NUM_CLASSES, activation: 'softmax'}).apply(features),  return tf.model({inputs: image, outputs: [realnessScore, aux]}),}function buildCombinedModel(latentSize, generator, discriminator, optimizer) {  const latent = tf.input({shape: [latentSize]}),  const imageClass = tf.input({shape: [1]}),  let fake = generator.apply([latent, imageClass]),  let aux,  discriminator.trainable = false,  [fake, aux] = discriminator.apply(fake),  const combined = tf.model({inputs: [latent, imageClass], outputs: [fake, aux]}),  combined.compile({optimizer, loss: ['binaryCrossentropy', 'sparseCategoricalCrossentropy']}),  combined.summary(),  return combined,}```

title: implement support for saved_models in browser environment
body: tensorflow/js introduced new model type compared to tensorflow/python - `graph_model`  unfortunately, very few of new models are published in `graph_model` format and require a conversion from `saved_mode` to `graph_model` (just check <tfhub.dev> - less than a third of models are available in `graph_model` format - and none of the models published in the last half a year)  however, this leads to many issues as `tensorflowjs_converter` is really not up to par - and big divergence from tensorflow itself  (as an example of issues, see #4125, #3903, #3942, #3930, etc...)  `tfjs-node` introduced direct loading of `saved_model` using `tf.node.loadSavedModel`  this allows many more models to be fully functional than relying on just `graph_model` support  however, that feature is `tfjs-node` specific and cannot be used in browser  there are valid use-cases to run tfjs in browser even for non-trivial items (and availability of webgl-acceleration on desktop is much easier than getting cuda-acceleration to run)i also understand the reasoning for `graph_model` on small and/or mobile platforms (especially chunking which allows for parallel loading) - but when working on high speed local network, those reasons are not critical  environment: tfjs 2.6.0 on ubuntu 20.10

title: [webgl] Investigate how to reduce memory usage from texture allocation with minimal performance impact.
body: Hi,I've been using the Universal Sentence Encoders model and had a hard to track memory leak. I eventually found [this comment](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4015#issuecomment-704335135)  which suggested setting ```jstf.env().set("WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD", 0),```Which solved the issue. I don't know what it did but it worked and I suggest documenting it more prominently. I'd volunteer to do so myself but don't understand what this does so leaving it as a suggestionThanks !
comments: ['```// set this flag so that textures are deleted when tensors are disposed.tf.env().set("WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD", 0),```=====', '> ```> // set this flag so that textures are deleted when tensors are disposed.> tf.env().set("WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD", 0),> ```I\'m not sure of that was for my sake, but if it was I (and similar users) don\'t understand it. I\'m just a simple NLP guy, I know some tensorflow and am fighting my way in the JS world to make things works. I (and people like me), want to use this lib, but have no idea what a texture is.More practically, it would be cool if it said somewhere: "Hey, if you see your script using 10G of ram, you might have a memory leak. Try this because WebGL allocates textures but doesn\'t release them by default ... " Hope that\'s helpful=====', 'I think a goo place to do this would be in the README for Universal Sentence Encoder. @talolard if you were interested in making a PR for that that would be great. Else we can do that. =====', 'cc @annxingyuan =====', "> I think a goo place to do this would be in the README for Universal Sentence Encoder. @talolard if you were interested in making a PR for that that would be great. Else we can do that.I'd be happy to. To make the thing compelte, can you point me to why it's a universal encoders thing and a general tf.js issue ? e.g. If I was building my own model it wouldn't be an issue ? =====", "@talolard Changing the default behavior of `WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD` is hopefully more of a last resort for our users, so I think that's why we'd want to document this closer to the specific use cases. =====", "Thanks @annxingyuan Can you shed some light on what it does and why it's specifc to Universal Sentence Encoders. I'd love to submit a PR with the relevant information but don't feel like I know what I'm talking about yet. Tnx=====", 'not intending to hijack this thread, but `WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD` is pretty much required for execution of any complex model due to TFJS extremely high WebGL memory usage. On the other hand, it has a really bad performance impact - it slows down subsequent inferences by 2-3x.The goal should be to optimize TFJS not to use 10x memory with `backend-webgl` compared to other backends.See this one for more details: <https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4166>=====', "@vladmandic Yes you're right - adjusting `WEBGL_DELETE_TEXTURE_THRESHOLD` does not address the underlying issue, which is why I'm hesitant to encourage people to rely on it, although I understand that it can improve performance in certain cases. body: **System information**- Have I written custom code: Yes- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): iOS ~13- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device: yes, iPhone X- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): script link- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): 2.7.0- Browser version: Safari - Tensorflow.js Converter Version: N/A**Describe the current behavior**I'm trying to fine-tune a complex computer vision neural net on the mobile browser, specifically iOS's Safari. The model architecture is really long and I don't think it's the problem, but basically it takes in two 128x128x3 images and an 8 vector, runs each input through some hidden layers, concats them and then runs them through some more hidden layers, and then outputs two numbers representing two normalized coordinates. My backend is webgl, and it's set before any other operations happen. I'm loading in the model (it was converted from a keras model using the python tfjs converter), then freezing every layer except the last few (everything here before the dense_3 has their trainable set to false): ![Screen Shot 2020-10-28 at 12 04 37 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29759597/97389833-baf79d80-18b1-11eb-981a-5a2a2a245325.png)I then try to fit it using this code. It just compiles the model using sgd and runs fit, and at the end of every epoch evaluates it on random inputs and prints the current loss, :```javascriptnaturemodel.predict([tf.randomNormal([1,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([1,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([1,8])]).print()var epochCount = 0// Compile the modelnaturemodel.compile({  optimizer: tf.train.sgd(0.0000268),  loss: 'meanSquaredError',  metrics: ['mae', 'mse']}),var n = 2,console.log(tf.memory())naturemodel.fit([tf.randomNormal([n,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([n,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([n,8])], [tf.randomNormal([n,2])], {       epochs: 3,       callbacks: {          onEpochEnd: async (batch, logs) => {                console.log('in batch predict ', naturemodel.predict([tf.randomNormal([1,128,128,3]),                                                tf.randomNormal([1,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([1,8])]).arraySync())                console.log(epochCount++, 'Loss: ' + logs.loss.toFixed(5)),}                }     })naturemodel.predict([tf.randomNormal([1,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([1,128,128,3]), tf.randomNormal([1,8])]).print()```So, originally, the losses, weights, and biases were all NaN after training no matter how small the learning rate was: ![naturemodel.fit attempt with WEBGL_CPU_FORWARD left default, true](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29759597/97389970-1e81cb00-18b2-11eb-89d6-6c56c2486df1.png)I then turned off the WEBGL_CPU_FORWARD flag with tf.ENV.set('WEBGL_CPU_FORWARD', false),. title: Making separable Convolutions more efficient

title: FaceMesh memory Leak when covering the face partially
body: Please make sure that this is a bug. As per our[GitHub Policy](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/ISSUES.md),we only address code/doc bugs, performance issues, feature requests andbuild/installation issues on GitHub. tag:bug_template**System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): No- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): Windows 10- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device: No- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): 2.1- Browser version: Chrome 86.0.4240.111- Tensorflow.js Converter Version: 2.1**Describe the current behavior**When I run the demo of the FaceMesh model and I cover my face partially, the gpu memory demand is steadily increasing with each frame. When the whole face is visible or the face isn't visible at all, the allocated memory remains the same. All this is only an issue with the webgl backend.**Describe the expected behavior**The memory demand should not increase in any case.**Code to reproduce the issue**The line following line can be added to the renderPrediction function to monitor gpu demand:`console.log(tf.backend().memory())`![facemesh](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69153609/97991946-5a50ef00-1de2-11eb-9406-aaab6d54ddf8.gif)
comments: ["For context: the facemesh pipeline includes two models:1) Bounding box detection model2) Geometry detection modelIf the face remains in view, we only run (2). If there is no face in view, we only run (1). if the face moves in and out of view, we run (1) followed by (2) over and over. So there is more opportunity for leaks in this case. I'm not sure where the leak occurs exactly, but this is the most likely scenario for creating a leak.For additional context, we are dataSyncing the bounding box detection model output to the CPU because we are doing many small postprocessing transformations on the output of the bounding box detection model that are slower to carry out on the GPU according to our experiments. ====="]
