title: fromPixels() must be an HTMLVideoElement but was HTMLVideoElement
body: > Uncaught (in promise) Error: pixels passed to tf.browser.fromPixels() must be either an HTMLVideoElement, HTMLImageElement, HTMLCanvasElement, ImageData in browser, or OffscreenCanvas, ImageData in webworker or {data: Uint32Array, width: number, height: number}, but was HTMLVideoElementThis error is showing up in the console.log of a node.js + nw.js project.It is triggered by this js code:```const tf = require('@tensorflow/tfjs'),const webcam = document.getElementById("webcam"),let new_tensor = tf.browser.fromPixels(webcam),```webcam refers to this HTML element:```<video id="webcam" autoplay muted></video>```The js code is executed after the video element is loaded and it's working if I print a video screenshot into a canvas and then I use that as input for the `fromPixels` method:```const tf = require('@tensorflow/tfjs'),const canvas = document.getElementById("canvas"),let ctx = canvas.getContext('2d'),ctx.drawImage(video, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height),let new_tensor = tf.browser.fromPixels(canvas),```canvas refers to this HTML element:```<canvas id="canvas"></canvas>```- Node.js: 14.6.0- nwVersion: 0.48.3- nwjs-builder-phoenix: 1.15.0- Windows 10 Home: 20H2- TensorFlow.js installed from: npm- TensorFlow.js version: 2.7.0
comments: ['Could you provide a minimal reproduction that we could run to see the error? Something like https://codepen.io/tafsiri/pen/qBNyMxP?editors=1111 but in the environment that you are experiencing the issue in.Also could you post the result of the following in your app.```jsconst webcam = document.getElementById("webcam"),console.log(\'webcam\', webcam)console.log(\'webcam instanceof HTMLVideoElement\', webcam instanceof HTMLVideoElement)```=====', 'The code you provided generate this output in console:> webcam <video id=\u200b"webcam" autoplay muted>\u200b</video>\u200b> webcam instanceof HTMLVideoElement trueI also tryied to run `tf.browser.fromPixels(webcam),` inside a if statement like so:```if (video instanceof HTMLVideoElement) {        const input_tensor = tf.browser.fromPixels(video),} else {        console.log("not an HTMLVideoElement"),}```And the if condition is satisfied so the error occurThe problem comes from a node.js + nwjs project so I don\'t know if there\'s an online platform that allows to reproduce this issue so easily.For the moment I uploaded a repo with all the testing code and the steps to reproduce it at this [link](https://github.com/Fantantonio/tfjs_issue_4189_test), if someone knows a better way just let me know.=====', 'After digging around a bit, it looks like your project is running in [separate context mode](http://docs.nwjs.io/en/latest/For%20Users/Advanced/JavaScript%20Contexts%20in%20NW.js/#separate-context-mode) and there are two JS contexts in which code is run. Your code is being run in the browser context and the tfjs library code is being run in the node context. In the node context `video instanceof HTMLVideoElement` returns false. The nw.js docs suggest that browser api\'s aren\'t usable in the node context so there may be incompatibility there. Their docs suggest you can switch to [mixed context mode](http://docs.nwjs.io/en/latest/For%20Users/Advanced/JavaScript%20Contexts%20in%20NW.js/#mixed-context-mode), I tried that by adding the following entry to the package.json and then it worked.```"chromium-args": "--mixed-context",```If you want to stay in separate context mode (and I don\'t know enough about nw.js to know the advantages and disadvantages of each) you would need to not use any of the browser specific apis of tfjs.=====', "Thanks for your time and for linking the documentation!That's the way to get it to work====="]

title: browser packaging for `tfjs-backend-wasm` module is broken
body: browser packaging for `tfjs-backend-wasm` modules is broken  it can be loaded as a script tag, but not as a modul bundletried 3 different imports:```jsimport { setWasmPaths } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm',import { setWasmPaths } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.js',import { setWasmPaths } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js',```and it tries to load `perf_hooks` and fails  also, **browser** module should not require **nodejs** specific requires such as `path` and `fs`  compare generated output of `tfjs-backend-webgl` and `tfjs-backend-wasm` modules headers:`@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-webgl/dist/tf-backend-webgl.es2017.js`:```js(function (global, factory) {  typeof exports === 'object' && typeof module !== 'undefined' ? factory(exports, require('@tensorflow/tfjs-core')) :  typeof define === 'function' && define.amd ? define(['exports', '@tensorflow/tfjs-core'], factory) :  (global = global || self, factory(global.tf = global.tf || {}, global.tf)),}(this, (function (exports, tf) { 'use strict',````@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js`:```js(function (global, factory) {  typeof exports === 'object' && typeof module !== 'undefined' ? factory(exports, require('@tensorflow/tfjs-core'), require('path'), require('fs'), require('worker_threads'), require('perf_hooks')) :  typeof define === 'function' && define.amd ? define(['exports', '@tensorflow/tfjs-core', 'path', 'fs', 'worker_threads', 'perf_hooks'], factory) :  (global = global || self, factory((global.tf = global.tf || {}, global.tf.wasm = global.tf.wasm || {}), global.tf, global.path, global.fs, global.worker_threads, global.perf_hooks)),}(this, (function (exports, tfjsCore, path, fs, worker_threads, perf_hooks) { 'use strict',```workaround is to import to compiled sources entry point instead and not use bundles at all - this works!:```jsimport { setWasmPaths } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js',```also, module rebuild should not require full recompilation of binary wasm files by default  for example, rebuild of `tfjs-node` downloads latest tensorflow binary and compiles typescript to module with bindings to downloaded binary  but rebuild of `tfjs-backend-wasm` attempts to rebuild .wasm files using `bazel` each time - this is not inline with the rest of tfjs  environment: tfjs 2.7.0 with chrome 86
comments: ['Can you tell us more about what environment you are seeing this in. Are you importing the module in a browser or running this through a bundler/build tools?=====', "i've tried both - running in browser directly and running through the bundler.header of `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js` is clearly wrong - that is supposed to be a browser bundle and yet it includes requires for `fs, `path`, `perf_hooks`. no other esm bundle (tfjs-core, tfjs-backend-webgl, tfjs-backend-cpu, etc.) has that.=====", 'For the bundler options, the first import `import {setWasmPaths} from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm\',` is similar to what [we have here in our webpack example](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/tree/master/tfjs-backend-wasm/starter/webpack) and I updated that to 2.7.0 and could build and serve the page without an error. Would you be able to share a small repo with a reproduction of the error you are seeing?For the browser case neither, `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.js` nor `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js` provide ESM modules. So they generally won\'t work with `import` (without something that can do pre-processing). We are planning on providing pre-bundled esm module builds in upcoming releases. This will probably be the suggested path for using esm modules directly in browser (but isn\'t something we explicitly support at the moment).As you may have seen `import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js\',` does provide an es module, though i\'m surprised it worked directly in your browser since it doesn\'t include the file extensions when importing. Note this is the file that a bundler that handle esm modules should resolve the package to (it is the path used in our "module" entry in our package.json).cc @annxingyuan=====', 'Sorry, when I said it works with no bundler, that\'s one level removed - my library uses tf and it creates bundle. Then I can use it inside html+js and that doesn\'t need to be bundled anymore. Ignore all notes on \'no bundler\'. (and yes, you are correct on not using extensions causing http 404s) Now, when it comes to bundlers, different bundlers generate different code - and some just strip unresolved extra requires.In my case, I use `esbuild` which does as little processing as possible and is about 10x faster than webpack/.1. `import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm\',`Loads correctly, but fails on first usage. Error: `\'cast\' not yet implemented or not found in the registry. This kernel may not be supported by the tfjs backend you have chosen` It just happens that `cast` is the first tfjs function called - basically, `tfjs-backend-wasm` loaded this way does not register kernel functions on its own. Basically, some bundlers don\'t look at `package.json` `modules` property so this ends up in the wrong place Using non-univeral `package.json` is not great, but not uncommon, so let\'s skip this 2. `import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.js\',`Does not load because of erroneous requires in header. Error `ReferenceError: require is not defined at empty:perf_hooks:1` 3. `import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js\',`Does not load because of erroneous requires in header. Error `ReferenceError: require is not defined at empty:perf_hooks:1` 4. `import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js\',`Works end-to-end. Now, some bundlers may "survive" mistakes, but I don\'t see how this can be valid for a Browser usage:`require(\'path\'), require(\'fs\'), require(\'worker_threads\'), require(\'perf_hooks\')`And that is in the header of generated `tf-backend-wasm.js` and `tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js` while no other part of TFJS intended for browser usage has that.=====', 'UPDATE:I just noticed that even when I\'m importing:`import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js\',`and everything works fine, there is a ghost request towards web server:`GET/2.0 404 /dist/empty:perf_hooks`This is because `dist/index.js` still uses a bundled `dist/miniprogram/index.js` which has the silly header with excessive requires!I think it all comes down to errors in `package.json`.(which i cannot verify right now because `tfjs-backend-wasm` cannot be rebuild without binary rebuild using `bazel`)note that both `tfjs-backend-webgl/package.json` and `tjfs-backend-cpu/package.json` contain:```json "browser": { "util": false, "crypto": false },```while `tfjs-backend-wasm/package.json` contains:```json "browser": { "fs": false, "path": false, "worker_threads": false, "perf_hooks": false },```=====', 'UPDATE: there is a related pending pull request: #3816 =====', 'I think this basically boils down to how the bundler you are using handles different kinds of modules. > import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js\',Works end-to-end.- If your bundler isn\'t following the module entry, but you do want to consume es modules as part of your build, `import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js\',` is a fine way to go (that is what the module entry points to). Though you may want to file a bug with your bundler on \'module\' entry support.> import { setWasmPaths } from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm\',Loads correctly, but fails on first usage.Error: \'cast\' not yet implemented or not found in the registry. This kernel may not be supported by the tfjs backend you have chosen- This makes me think that your bundler is following the module entry correctly. If you are seeing errors with kernels not being registered it means the bundler is also pretty aggressively tree shaking the import and thus kernels are not being registered. This should be fixable by adding an side-effect oriented import `import \'@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js\',````"browser": {\t"fs": false, "path": false, "worker_threads": false, "perf_hooks": false},```- These entries tell your bundler to ignore these imports. The spec being used is even linked to from [the esbuild docs](https://esbuild.github.io/getting-started/#bundling-for-the-browser) (see the [browser field ](https://github.com/defunctzombie/package-browser-field-spec)link in the last paragragh). Its possible there is a bug in the bundler causing those 404 requests.> This is because dist/index.js still uses a bundled dist/miniprogram/index.js which has the silly header with excessive requires!I\'m not entirely sure what this means but I don\'t think its accurate. [This is the content of `dist/index.js`](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js) and there isn\'t a path from that to loading the contents of `dist/miniprogram/index.js`.I really think this is an issue with your bundler or how you are configuring it/your build.=====', "yes, `miniprogram` is a a red herring, sorry about that, it's just a copy of minified cpu backend that is internally used by everyone.`build-npm.sh:cp dist/tf-backend-cpu.min.js dist/miniprogram/index.js`and lets assume `import { setWasmPaths } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm',` fails because bundler is too aggresive with tree shaking. i'll handle that on the bundler side.so there are no issues with `import { setWasmPaths } from '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/index.js',`but what is the purpose of: `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.js` and `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js`?every other part of tfjs can be imported from such bundles, but `wasm` must be imported from `dist/index.js`?also, why is `wasm` rebuild process trying to rebuild `*.wasm` binaries using `bazel` every time? no other part of tfjs does that!e.g., `tfjs-node` *downloads* binary tensorflow during build, it does not try to rebuild it each time.=====", "`@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.js` and `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/tf-backend-wasm.es2017.js` are UMD bundles that provide unminified code using ES5 and ES2017 syntax (note: just the syntax changes, not the module format) this allows people to opt into browser bundles that use modern es6+ code (e.g. async await) even if they do not yet have support for es6 modules. We do this for all our packages. > also, why is wasm rebuild process trying to rebuild *.wasm binaries using bazel every time? no other part of tfjs does that!No other part of tfjs has a bunch of c++ code that needs to be compiled. You can use `yarn build-fast` to skip the wasm bundle compilation if you have already compiled them once (or if you want to try something that doesn't actually require the wasm binaries to exist).=====", " No other part of tfjs has a bunch of c++ code that needs to be compiled.`tfjs-node` is based on `tensorflow.so` which is downloaded istead of being compiled, so that doesn't really hold. You can use yarn build-fast to skip the wasm bundle compilation`build-fast` doesn't work unless full build has been completed first as it requires `tfjs-backend-wasm-*.worker.js` which are dynamically generated. yes, i can run a `bazel` build, but it should not be necessary - it's about 50x slower than the rest of tfjs build altogether (when i was building a toolchain just to get `summarize_graph` it took hours).but we're getting sidetracked here. i don't like how `tfjs-backend-wasm` is handled very differently than the rest of `tfjs` from dependency point of view (fs, path, perf_hooks should not be there at all since this is **not** a nodejs module, it shouldn't be up to bundler to figure it out).please consider removing unnecessary dependencies from browser packages.=====", 'closing this issue due to changes in packaging of tfjs 3.0.0=====', 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: Implement native tf.browser.fromPixels() for WASM backend
body: Currently `tf.browser.fromPixels()` has native implementation for WebGL backend while WASM falls back to default `canvas.getContext('2d').getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height).data,`This means it will:a) Fail if input already has a different context     e.g., canvas with `webgl` context because user performed some image pre-processingb) It is really slowOn FullHD input, WebGL native implementation executes in near 0ms while `getImageData()` takes ~20ms  This significantly impacts overall performance of WASM backend in general.Example, if model execution takes 33ms in both WebGL and WASM, frame rate in WebGL will be 30 FPS, but in WASM it will be 1000/(20+33) = 18 FPS - that is 36% performance difference just because of lack of native implementation to get image data.
comments: ["UPDATE: as an alternative, would it be possible to use WebGL implementation of `tf.browser.fromPixels()` and then continuing with WASM model. I don't mind mixing backends like this, but actually changing active backend on the fly is a no-go.=====", "Closer look, it's even worse - `browser.ts:fromPixels_()` will create extra canvas if it cannot get `2d` context.So not only there is a missing native implementation, but fallback one is really bad.```js    if (fromPixels2DContext == null) {      fromPixels2DContext = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d'),    }```Plus it uses DOM (`document.createElement`), so it cannot be executed in Web Worker (if you *have to* create additional canvas, should try `OffsreenCanvas` first and use DOM as fallback).If you can't use your accelerated webgl implemenation, why not test for canvas `webgl` context first and then rely on GL context `ctx.readPixels()` which is >2x faster than `ctx.getImagedata()`.And then there is a loop to remove alpha channel instead of placing RGBA in a tensor and using tensor operations to remove one dimension!```js    for (let i = 0, i < numPixels, i++) {      for (let channel = 0, channel < numChannels, ++channel) {        values[i * numChannels + channel] = vals[i * 4 + channel],      }    }```No wonder `fromPixels()` is really bad on anything but `WebGL` backend!=====", 'When having a canvas with `2d` context, despite using `webgl` as the `tfjs` backend, the `fromPixels` method still takes 25ms+.I could not find a way to perhaps copy my canvas with existing context to a new canvas in order to have a `webgl` context.=====', "@AmitMY in my tests, only first call to `fromPixels` takes ~25ms when using `WebGL` backend as GLSL needs to be initialized  if doing 1000 calls using `HTMLVideoElement` as input (webcam in full-hd), it takes <2ms per each frame  btw, I've tried mixing GL and CPU or WASM backends (it can be done in a weird way), but the issue is that with GL `fromPixels` all ops and data happen on GPU and tensor is actually not available for usage outside of GL - title: [wasm] Optimization of tf.browser.fromPixels.
body: I noticed that [tf.browser.fromPixels](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-core/src/ops/browser.ts#L145-L151) can be very slow when it spends time in this loop:```js    const numPixels = width * height,    values = new Int32Array(numPixels * numChannels),    for (let i = 0, i < numPixels, i++) {      for (let channel = 0, channel < numChannels, ++channel) {        values[i * numChannels + channel] = vals[i * 4 + channel],      }    }```(Also reported by #4218)I was able to get significantly better performance with my application by calling this function instead:```jsfunction convertArrayBufferRGBAToUInt8RGB(buffer) {  // create view of ArrayBuffer  const x = new Uint8Array(buffer),  const n = x.length,  let i = 0,  let j = 0,  // loop through all pixels and shift them over to remove alpha  while (i < n) {    x[j] = x[i], i++, j++,    x[j] = x[i], i++, j++,    x[j] = x[i], i++, j++,    i++,  }  // return a subset of the original  return x.slice(0, j),}```And then calling it like sort of like this:```jsconst fromPixels2DContext = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d'), // only call this oncefunction fromPixelsFast(inputElt, width, height) {  return tf.tidy(() => {    fromPixels2DContext.canvas.width = width,    fromPixels2DContext.canvas.height = height,    fromPixels2DContext.drawImage(inputElt, 0, 0, width, height),    const buffer = fromPixels2DContext.getImageData(0, 0, width, height).data.buffer,    const UInt8RGB = convertArrayBufferRGBAToUInt8RGB(inputArray),    return tf.tensor3d(UInt8RGB, [height, width, 3]),  }),}```I think the thing that makes it faster is connected to:1. Using Uint8Array instead of UInt32Array (small effect)2. The unrolled loop is better optimized by the browser. (medium effect)3. It is more efficient to shuffle data in one array than between two arrays due to cache effects. (big effect)(But I have not done rigorous testing)It might even be possible to get a little more speed from `.subarray` instead of `.slice` to avoid making the copy.A complete example using this function with blazeface and a custom model on a webcam inside a webworker is available [in this repo](https://github.com/kylemcdonald/tfjs-expression-recognition/tree/webworker).
comments: ["I'm looking at the other report over in #4218 and the nature of that bug along with an examination of the source lead me to believe this path is primarily triggered for WASM, right? The other backends register their own implementations, I think. Can you confirm?=====", "@kylemcdonald This is very much inline in what I'm suggesting in #4218  Two suggestions that can enhance your code:Try OffscreenCanvas before DOM, it's slightly faster and works inside web workers. But it's not supported on Firefox yet.```jsconst fromPixelsCanvas (typeof OffscreenCanvas !== 'undefined') ? new OffscreenCanvas(width, height) : document.createElement('canvas'),```Try GL `readPixels` method first as its quite a bit faster.  And fallback to 2D context and `getImageData` if cannot get GL context.  ```jsconst fromPixelsGLContext  = fromPixelsCanvas.getContext('webgl'),const buffer = new Uint8Array(fromPixelsCanvas.width * fromPixelsCanvas.height * 4),fromPixelsGLContext.readPixels(0, 0, fromPixelsCanvas.width, fromPixelsCanvas.height, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, buffer),```But...one issue here would be that `getImageData` returns data starting top/left and `readPixels` returns data starting bottom/left, so processing loop needs to be inverted.Of course, best method would be to implement `fromPixels` directly in WASM backend just like it's implemented in WebGL backend.=====", '@vladmandic could you explain more what you mean by "best method would be to implement `fromPixels` directly in WASM backend"? I\'m new to WASM and I don\'t understand what this means. Are you talking about a different way of getting the pixels that is neither `readPixels` nor `getImageData`? Or are you just saying where the code should be located?@wingman-jr-addon I can confirm that this is designed to target the WASM backend. This is most relevant in the situation where WebGL is unavailable.=====', "@kylemcdonald - yes, that's exactly what I'm saying - it's possible for a WASM module to work directly with canvas, so it could implement it's own function to get pixel data from canvas instead of relying on either GL `readPixels()` or 2D `getImageData()` which are both relatively slow, especially since additional postprocessing is needed to drop alpha channel.But in the lack of such native implementation, any gain over existing method is welcome!=====", "Thanks for reporting this @kylemcdonald ! I'm going to close this as a duplicate of https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4218 - which was created 1 day earlier :)Thanks for the greaat discussion on this issue - this will be a really helpful reference for us!====="]

title: sideEffects annotation in package.json may be out of date
body: I'm working on [a bug](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/458) filed by a user of this library against [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild), a bundler I work on. It looks to me like this library uses the [sideEffects](https://webpack.js.org/guides/tree-shaking/#mark-the-file-as-side-effect-free) annotation in `package.json` to indicate that most files in the package do not have side effects. However, they do actually have side effects and this annotation causes the resulting bundle to be broken.**System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): no- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): macOS 10.15.7- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device: N/A- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): ?- Browser version: Chrome 80- Tensorflow.js Converter Version: N/A**Describe the current behavior**I tested this by bundling [this example code](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/b85f40d419a30f2c64305bd606974aaf47bcf88b/tfjs-backend-wasm/README.md#via-npm) from your readme:```js// Import @tensorflow/tfjs or @tensorflow/tfjs-coreimport * as tf from '@tensorflow/tfjs',// Adds the WASM backend to the global backend registry.import '@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm',// Set the backend to WASM and wait for the module to be ready.tf.setBackend('wasm').then(() => main()),function main() { console.log('works') }```Bundling that with `webpack ./example.js` (Webpack version 5.4.0, the current one) and running the bundle in the browser with a script tag throws `Error: Backend name 'wasm' not found in registry`.**Describe the expected behavior**I expect `works` to be printed to the console.**Suggested fix**The easiest way to fix this is to remove the [`sideEffects` field](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/b85f40d419a30f2c64305bd606974aaf47bcf88b/tfjs-backend-wasm/package.json#L83-L88) from your `package.json` files. This should make sure the library remains correct when bundled.A harder way to fix this would be to go through all of your files and figure out which ones have side effects, and then include them in that list. For example, at least the file `dist/backend_wasm.js` should be in there because it contains a call to `registerBackend('wasm')`. This is harder because you will have subtle correctness issues if you later on change your files (introduce new ones, move code between files, etc.) and forget to update the `sideEffects` field correctly.**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**Additional files used:* `package.json`    ```json    {      "scripts": {        "build": "webpack ./index.js"      },      "dependencies": {        "@tensorflow/tfjs": "2.7.0",        "@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm": "2.7.0",        "@tensorflow/tfjs-core": "2.7.0",        "webpack": "5.4.0",        "webpack-cli": "4.2.0"      }    }    ```* `index.html`    ```html    <script src="dist/main.js"></script>    ```
comments: ["Thanks for reporting this, I'll take a look. We initally set this up to work with webpack 4 but can check on the behaviour in webpack 5. At least at that point we needed to have the explicit sideEffects list present to get the behaviour we want.=====", 'Thanks for taking a look! I\'m sorry about this class of problems being an issue. Ideally `sideEffects` would have been specified as opt-in instead of opt-out because that would have been much less error-prone, but that ship has unfortunately sailed already.One more thing to point out is that it\'s not just the `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm` package. For example, here\'s a warning that esbuild generates when bundling the `@tensorflow/tfjs-core` package:``` > node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/flags.js: warning: Ignoring this import because "node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/engine.js" was marked as having no side effects 17 │ import \'./engine\', ╵ ~~~~~~~~~~ node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/package.json: note: It was excluded from the "sideEffects" array in the enclosing "package.json" file 121 │ "sideEffects": [ ╵ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~```Presumably the `import \'./engine\'` statement is trying to import that file just for its side effects, but then `package.json` instructs the bundler to treat the file as if it has no side effects when all of the imports are unused.=====', "Thanks for the detailed report @evanw, We missed a few files in our sideEffects listing. I've made a PR to address this and unblock this issue, and will be testing out webpacks [new ability to do without the sideEffects field](https://webpack.js.org/blog/2020-10-10-webpack-5-release/#side-effect-analysis) more extensively. It would be great if we don't have to track this manually, but will have to make the call as to whether we need to support webpack 4. =====", 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: The package "@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm" is not minifier-safe
body: I'm working on [a bug](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/538) filed by a user of this library against [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild), a bundler I work on. The `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm` package breaks when bundled and minified. This problem is not specific to esbuild, it happens with a normal Webpack production build too with all default options. However, this is a problem that needs to be solved in the library itself instead of by the bundler, so I figured I should file an issue here about this.**System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): no- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): macOS 10.15.7- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device: N/A- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): ?- Browser version: Chrome 80- Tensorflow.js Converter Version: N/A**Describe the current behavior**The `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm` package sometimes breaks when minified. This is the case with Webpack and other bundlers.The specific reason for the breakage is described here: https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/538#issuecomment-729199631. At a high level, this library converts a function to a string and then converts that string back to a function. This essentially "rips" it out of its local scope and injects it into another scope and then re-binds all identifiers. That function accesses a local variable called `_scriptDir` and expects that variable to keep the same name in the function source code.Some ways of fixing this:* This could be fixed by placing the code that should not be minified inside a string instead of using a function expression to contain the code. This will ensure that the minifier will not transform it in any way.* This could be fixed by not using the name of the variable to implement this binding. It would be best to pass the value of this variable as an additional parameter to the function so the function doesn't reach for anything outside of its scope.* There is an alternative hack using direct `eval` if doing this is not possible. This hack is also described in https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/538#issuecomment-729199631. Using direct `eval` is an anti-pattern so I'd only do this if other options don't work.**Describe the expected behavior**The `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm` package should not behave differently when minified.**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**There is a full reproduction case here: https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/538#issuecomment-728939332. Note that to hit the issue, you need to have both `WebAssembly SIMD support` and `WebAssembly threads support` enabled in `chrome://flags/`.

title: Will TF.JS survive WebAssembly? Is TF.JS going to die?
body: If we have [WebAssembly](https://webassembly.org/) tool that enables us to run C/C++,RUST, Python, Go... code in Browser at **native speed**  what is reason of using TF.JS in future?WebAssembly(supports WebGL) and guarantee consistent performance across a spectrum of browsers while JS must be optimized per se. Also as there is no need for multiple run of JS as interpreter and code can be complied which would save time.. (WebAssembly and JavaScript both have the same peak performance. But… JavaScript can easily fall off the “fast path” while WebAssembly will not.)--------------------------------------------**| .js         -> Ignition  ->/<-    TubroFan |** - _js input_  Ignition: Interprets the JS text and runs it. While running, collects analytics data about how the code is behaving before   TurboFan kicks in.  TurboFan: The optimizing compiler.**| .wasm ->  LiftOff       ->       TubroFan |**- _wasm input_  Liftoff: The streaming WebAssembly compiler which generates machine code.  TurboFan: The optimizing compiler which generates optimized code.                                                             |--------------------------------------------[IMAGE https://itenium.be/assets/blog-images/webassembly-v8-js-vs-wasm.png]Will this means future decline of TFJS in next years as overlapping is so huge? (as ML dev don't prefer JS and would rather use Python)P.S.I'm aware it's early days of WebAssembly but as its supported by https://www.w3.org/ it's here to stay.
comments: ['@aelich You have raised a good point, WASM has been on a rise recently. TensorFlow.js being an ML platform for the web/javascript developers, we are tech stack neutral. Our goal is to utilized all web technologies to provide our users the best performance, that includes WASM, webGL, webGPU, and the future WebNN standard. WASM has already been used in our tfjs-backend-wasm package. We are also actively investing more into WASM, you will see more news coming out in the near future.=====', 'As an anecdote, I\'m probably one of those "ML devs" who "don\'t prefer JS". However, for me the big story with any ML model is to make it useful by deploying it - deploying an ML model in any meaningful way often means a different language, model optimization, potentially learning new frameworks etc. For me - and I suspect many others - Tensorflow.js usage is focused primarily on the use case of inference of pretrained models.In most deployments, there are (at least) two parts: glue code and performance-critical code. Glue code has business logic and performance-critical code does the heavy lifting for the model. As such, the performance for glue code often doesn\'t matter that much as long as the interfacing is done well to the performance-critical code. In this way, Tensorflow.js using JS with optimized backends (including WASM) is not really that different from say Python with Tensorflow bindings to a GPU backend.So what am I getting at? For the glue code, I think the requirements tend to be "fast enough", "as fast as possible to write", and "easy to maintain". JS checks all those boxes for me, right now WASM does not. I\'m not saying tooling won\'t get better in the future, etc., but I do think that in many cases you still have to either 1) interface with HTML/CSS or 2) something else that wants JS at some point. JS has utility precisely because it provides a tradeoff in simplicity and tooling without sacrificing (much) speed where it counts. I suspect WASM without any JS will definitely have a certain use case too, but so far we also haven\'t seen (for example) C# apps converted to WASM magically displace JS - quite the opposite. So I think that essentially we have "JS bindings" for "WASM backend" and I\'d be surprised if either one went away just based on the patterns that seem to pop up on other systems. However, web tech is not my primary focus, so maybe I\'m missing something here, it\'d be interesting to see what others think on this front.=====', 'This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. It will be closed in 7 days if no further activity occurs. Thank you.=====', 'Closing as stale. Please @mention us if this needs more attention.=====']

title: Inconsistent creation of tensor6d with nested Uint8Arrays
body: **System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js):n/a- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04):Windows 10, Version 1909 (OS Build 18363.1198)- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device:n/a- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link):npm- TensorFlow.js version:2.7.0- Browser version:n/a- Tensorflow.js Converter Version:unknown**Describe the current behavior**TLDR: It appears the type definitions for tensor1-5d and tensor6d have inconsistent nested Uint8Array bracket counts. Please see the source at the bottom of this bug.Full Story:When creating tensors from nested Uint8Arrays, the results are not consistent across every supported rank (1-6). Specifically, rank 6 does not act like ranks 1-5._Regarding depth, I will consider Uint8Array[] as one-dimensional in this write-up, as I would with boolean[] or number[]. It's confusing with typed arrays._- If you pass a 6d array of Uint8Array into tensor6d(), an error is thrown.- If you pass the same 6d array into the generic tensor(), a rank 7 tensor is returned.- If you pass a 5d array into tensor6d(), a rank 6 tensor is returned.These cases may be perfectly valid (although they seem inconsistent). However, the behavior of the third case changes when applied to lower ranks.- If you attempt to pass a 4d array into tensor5d(), a TypeScript error is produced, showing that 'Uint8Array[][][][] not assignable to TensorLike5D'.It appears that one of these problems exists:- The type for 6d Uint8Array is missing a pair of brackets.OR- The types for 1-5d Uint8Array each have an extra pair of brackets._NOTE: I'd be happy to fix this one, but I'm not certain which behavior is preferred. Should tensor5() accept 4d or 5d arrays of Uint8Array? Should the generic tensor() ever produce a rank 7, or should that throw?_**Describe the expected behavior**The generic call tensor() and the specific calls tensor<1-6>d() should return properly ranked tensors given identical Uint8Array input, and there should be no TypeScript errors.**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**```import * as TF from '@tensorflow/tfjs-node',const UI8_4: Uint8Array[][][][]     = [[[[new Uint8Array(3)]]]],const UI8_5: Uint8Array[][][][][]   = [[[[[new Uint8Array(3)]]]]],const UI8_6: Uint8Array[][][][][][] = [[[[[[new Uint8Array(3)]]]]]],try {	// using title: WebGL backend should include an environment variable to toggle failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat value.
body: I've run into an interesting situation.Recently, when Firefox upgraded from 82 to 83, performance on [my addon](https://github.com/wingman-jr-addon/wingman_jr) dropped sharply for myself and some other users as well. I traced the issue to the WebGL backend failing to load due to `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` exhibiting a change in behavior between the two versions. As this was negatively affecting my users, I quickly added in the WASM backend as an option. However, while this was [faster for some users](https://github.com/wingman-jr-addon/wingman_jr/issues/75#issuecomment-734822117) - thank you TF.js team for your awesome work! - for others like myself it seems to still be a blocking issue.When I [did a bisection and filed a bug with Mozilla](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1679671), their initial response is that it is likely that `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` had a bug in FF 82 but that has now been fixed, and that the context creation *should* be failing by the spec.So this puts me in an interesting spot. With the evidence I have so far, I believe there are a significant number of users that would still benefit from the WebGL backend - even with "major performance caveats" - over the WASM backend. Unfortunately, it appears that the `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` is [hardcoded](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/c537c813ba8234a909d1e0849abfd95998a8fb5b/tfjs-backend-webgl/src/canvas_util.ts#L27) rather than relying on say an environment variable or something I can tweak to allow for a different user experience.So, I have a couple followup questions:1. Is the use of `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` solely about performance for the end user, or is there a correctness concern as well?2. If it is solely about performance, would the TF.js team consider making this controllable via, say, an environment variable?Maybe I'm missing something about the overall situation, but I've been battling this for about a week and a half now and I'm curious your perspective on the matter.Thanks!
comments: ['@wingman-jr-addon I believe you can create your own webgl backend using your own gl context.similar to how we register webgl backend for wechat mini program ([link](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-wechat/blob/master/src/plugin/utils/wechat_platform.ts#L127))You can set the failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat to false if you prefer.=====', '@pyu10055 Thanks for the tip - as per my first question, do you know if there are any correctness concerns if I do that?=====', "Hi @wingman-jr-addon - I don't believe there would be correctness concerns with creating your own WebGL backend. Per the [Khronos documentation](http://www.khronos.org/registry/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#5.2) of this attribute, it should only be relevant to performance.I think it would be reasonable to add a WebGL environment variable to toggle this value - thanks for the suggestion! I've renamed this issue to reflect.=====", 'Thanks @annxingyuan - and that was also a good link to the spec, I learned a few things about some of the additional flags, too!=====', '@annxingyuan and @pyu10055 I think you may be interested to see the direction Firefox has taken now regarding this flag in the linked bugs [1684475](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1684475) and [1678652](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1678652). =====']

When using high level APIs like Canned Estimators it is not easy to ensure for all integer ops to be of `DT_INT32` so that we can load and use the model in tfjs-node. Therefore, it would be nice if tfjs-node can handle this conversion automatically if possible or not execute that part of computation subgraph unless needed / invoked, at least in the context of canned estimators. Check https://repl.it/@NitinPasumarthy/Serialized-Model-Input-In-TFJS#index.js to see this live. comments: ['@HarshalRohit please give a reproduction code or codepen example ?=====', 'Hi, Please guide me on creating a reproducible code.I am currently working on tfjs and react-native, and dont have any idea on creating reproducible code for react-native.=====', "Hi thanks for reporting. I am able to reproduce the behavior and can explain where it is coming from. This behavior is coming from imprecision in float32 representations for numbers (which are used throughout tfjs). You can reproduce this in pure javascript with the following line `Math.log(new Float32Array([Math.E])[0])`. Putting Math.E in a Float32Array will change the representation of the number and add some imprecision. This isn't something we can avoid.What problems is this causing in you application/project? Because of this imprecision, if you are using float32 tensors and want to do comparisons you shouldn't use exact comparison, you should instead check that the numbers are close to each other within some range of tolerance (we often use `1e-7` for float 32 comparisons).=====", "Hi Thanks for the explanation. I suspected the issue but wanted to have clarification on it.My project involves writing a js implementation of converting .wav audio files to spectrogram representation using tfjs ops. I am using [this](https://towardsdatascience.com/understanding-audio-data-fourier-transform-fft-spectrogram-and-speech-recognition-a4072d228520) as the reference implementation and also for comparison purposes. To compare them I calculating _sum of squared differences_, which ranges between 10^-1 to 10^-4. This range isn't very good, I guess. Hence, I was looking for mistakes in my implementation and found the raised issue.=====", "No problem. Looks like you got the info you needed so I'll close this for now. Good luck on the project!=====", 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: Implement SeparableConv1D as a convolutional layer
body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): tfjs@2.8.0- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): No, not at this time**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**While tfjs currently supports [SeparableConv2D](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#layers.separableConv2d), it does not include [SeparableConv1D](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/layers/SeparableConv1D). The [Python implementation of SeparableConv1D](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/582c8d236cb079023657287c318ff26adb239002/tensorflow/python/keras/layers/convolutional.py#L1891-L2065) can presumably be used as a reference, and [the existing js SeparableConv2D implentation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/b94940d3b5c9c2645b039f056120378a9a439c5a/tfjs-layers/src/layers/convolutional.ts#L1054) could be a starting point for implementation [since it already has a note about not supporting SeparableConv1D yet](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/b94940d3b5c9c2645b039f056120378a9a439c5a/tfjs-layers/src/layers/convolutional.ts#L1005).**Will this change the current api? How?**It will add an additional layer in tf.layers (next to the [other convolutional layers](https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/#Layers-Convolutional)).**Who will benefit with this feature?**Among other uses, it will allow 1D [SepCNN](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.02357.pdf) to be implemented in tfjs ([as in this example for Python](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/text-classification/step-4)), and Tensorflow models that use it can be converted to js.**Any Other info.**

title: tfjs 2.8.0 is broken and introduces regressions in tf.image.cropAndResize
body: As subject line says, TFJS 2.8.0 unfortunately seems like a broken version.First, default parameter in `cropAndResize` was unintentionally removed (and apparently just re-added via #4407) which causes quite a lot of errors in existing appsSecond, even when specifying resize method as `bilinear`, `cropAndResize` FAILS on `WebGL` baclend:```Uncaught (in promise) Error: Failed to compile fragment shader.    at createFragmentShader (webgl_util.ts:103)    at GPGPUContext.createProgram (gpgpu_context.ts:280)    at compileProgram (gpgpu_math.ts:93)    at backend_webgl.ts:858    at MathBackendWebGL.getAndSaveBinary (backend_webgl.ts:902)    at MathBackendWebGL.runWebGLProgram (backend_webgl.ts:857)    at Object.cropAndResize3 [as kernelFunc] (CropAndResize.ts:35)    at kernelFunc3 (engine.ts:590)    at engine.ts:660    at Engine.scopedRun (engine.ts:453)```With WebGL code dump highlighting error in```204 setOutput(float(undefined)),```IMO, this is is blocking bug - once fixed, TFJS packages should be republished!(and I'm not sure how this passed any level of testing?)Btw, same code confirmed working after downgrade to tfjs 2.7.0.
comments: ['cc @annxingyuan @lina128 for visibility - sorry for spam, but this is bad=====', 'cc @tafsiri =====', "Hi @vladmandic - thanks for reporting this issue - just wanted to let you know that you can avoid the fragment shader compile error by passing both `method` and `extrapolationValue` into `cropAndResize`, e.g.: `tf.image.cropAndResize(image, boxes, boxInd, [5,5], 'bilinear', 0 /* extrapolation value */) // note the last argument` =====", "@annxingyuan thanks for that - but I have `cropAndResize` all over my code, I'll just wait until this is fixed and tfjs is republished - in the meantime i'm sticking with tfjs 2.7.0.=====", 'Hi @vladmandic, we are going to release the fix in 2.8.1 very soon.=====', "Since `2.8.0` is tagged as `latest`, the whole package looks deprecated now, see:https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tensorflow/tfjsI'd recommend to tag `2.7.0` as `latest` until you have a fixed version to remove the warning from the package npm page:```npm dist-tag add @tensorflow/tfjs@2.7.0 latest```=====", "Thanks for the tip @mgol! We've tagged 2.7.0 as the latest npm version for all packages that were in the 2.8.0 release. =====", '2.8.1 is released. It should fix the bug.=====', 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====', 'tfjs 2.8.1 fixes this issue, but exposes another issue in #4429=====']

title: [TypeError: img.toFloat is not a function] When passing an image from decodeJpeg (tfjs-react-native) into model.classify (tfjs-auto-ml)
body: Please make sure that this is a bug. As per our[GitHub Policy](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/ISSUES.md),we only address code/doc bugs, performance issues, feature requests andbuild/installation issues on GitHub. tag:bug_template**System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): Yes- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device: All mobile devices- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): 2.7.0- tfjs-react-native 0.5.0- tfjs-automl: 1.0.0**Describe the current behavior**I can get the image from the react native file system (using expo-file-system), convert it from base64 to array buffer, decode it (with tfjs-react-native), but once I pass it to my `ImageClassificationModel` from tfjs-automl, it gives me the error. It seems like the object returned from decodeJpeg (tfjs-rn) doesn't have a method `toFloat` that `ImageClassificationModel.classify` expects it to have for preprocessing.**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**Provide a reproducible test case that is the bare minimum necessary to generatethe problem. If possible, please share a link to Colab/CodePen/any notebook.``` const base64 = await ExpoFileSystem.readAsStringAsync(imageUri, { encoding: 'base64' }) const raw = Uint8Array.from(toByteArray(base64)) // toByteArray is from npm package 'base64-js' const imageTensor = decodeJpeg(raw) // decodeJpeg is from tfjs-rn const predictions = await model.classify(imageTensor) // ImageClassificationModel from tfjs-automl```Here's how I create my `ImageClassificationModel`, if it's relevant. I'm using expo to grab the asset txt as a string, then I pass it along with my asset ids for my model.json and my model_weights.bin. I'm using metro bundler properly to make sure that the extensions .txt. and .bin are bundled.```async function loadModel(dictId: number, modelJsonId: any, weightsId: number) { const [dictAsset] = await Asset.loadAsync(dictId) const dictRaw = await ExpoFileSystem.readAsStringAsync(dictAsset.localUri) const dict = dictRaw.trim().split('\n') const model = await loadGraphModel(bundleResourceIO(modelJsonId, weightsId)) return new ImageClassificationModel(model, dict)}```Here's what I get when I log the `imageTensor` object. This is supposed to be of type `Tensor`.`{"dataId": {}, "dtype": "int32", "id": 324, "isDisposedInternal": false, "kept": false, "rankType": "3", "shape": [224, 126, 3], "size": 84672, "strides": [378, 3]}`I can definitely see why this is crashing. `ImageClassificationModel` from automl wants to call `toFloat()` on this `Tensor` as part of preprocessing before classification.

title: tfjs-react-native: Any way to make models load faster? (outside of Metro)
body: I load three graph models when my app boots. On my new Galaxy S20+, this takes ~3 seconds with Metro (served over HTTP right?) and ~9 seconds with a release bundle (loaded with react-native-fs I believe). These numbers are fine (although I'd be interested to know why it takes 3x as long when the file is already on-device _edit: I realize now this is because over HTTP we use fetch as binary, whereas with fs we cycle between bytes/base64 multiple times_ ), but now that my app is getting ready for release, I'm seeing load times of 30 seconds or more on some older devices. This is really pushing the limit of what I'm comfortable with.Is there any recourse here? Each of my models is a tfjs model with 6 or 7 weights shards, 4mb each. ~75mb total on file.
comments: ["I think I know what's going on here.I found this in react-native-fs:```InputStream inputStream = getInputStream(filepath),byte[] inputData = getInputStreamBytes(inputStream),String base64Content = Base64.encodeToString(inputData, Base64.NO_WRAP),promise.resolve(base64Content),```And this in BundleResourceHandler:```base64Weights = await RNFS.readFileRes(fileName)...const weightData = util.encodeString(base64Weights, 'base64').buffer```So the flow is:RNFS reads bytes > RNFS converts to base64 > TFJS receives base64 > TFJS converts to bytesIt looks like this is a package out there that can fix this cycle:https://www.npmjs.com/package/rn-fetch-blobSpecifically the `readStream` method: https://github.com/joltup/rn-fetch-blob/wiki/File-System-Access-API#readstreampath-encoding-buffersize-interval-promisernfbreadstream=====", "@tafsiri Check this out! I think I'm on to something here. I know this code is pretty raw (mixing Expo FS and RNFS...) but it actually works! And I can use this exact same code to load buffers in Metro or in release.I was able to reduce my shards load time from 9-12 seconds to 3-3.5 seconds!Flow:1. Get asset uris from expo-asset2. Copy files from cache into document directory3. use react-native-static-server to serve doc directory over HTTP4. use axios to grab the .bin files from the serverI also think it's definitely possible to skip the cache>docDir copies, but it's late and I will try tomorrow...```async function loadAllShards() {  const t1 = Date.now()  const [family, genus, species] = await Asset.loadAsync([    require('../../assets/family_shards.bin'),    require('../../assets/genus_shards.bin'),    require('../../assets/species_shards.bin')  ])  console.log('loaded assets in', Date.now() - t1, 'ms')  if (!family.localUri || !genus.localUri || !species.localUri) {    throw new Error('shards file is missing a localUri')  }  await FileSystem.copyAsync({    from: family.localUri,    to: FileSystem.documentDirectory + 'family_shards.bin'  })  await FileSystem.copyAsync({    from: genus.localUri,    to: FileSystem.documentDirectory + 'genus_shards.bin'  })  await FileSystem.copyAsync({    from: species.localUri,    to: FileSystem.documentDirectory + 'species_shards.bin'  })  console.log('starting server', RNFS.DocumentDirectoryPath, Date.now() - t1)  const server = new StaticServer(0, RNFS.DocumentDirectoryPath)  const baseURL = await server.start()  console.log('serving at', baseURL, Date.now() - t1)  const axios = Axios.create({    baseURL  })  const buffers = await Promise.all(    ['family_shards.bin', 'genus_shards.bin', 'species_shards.bin'].map(      async file => {        const response = await axios.get<ArrayBuffer>(file, {          responseType: 'arraybuffer'        })        return response.data      }    )  )  console.log('got all buffers in', Date.now() - t1, 'ms')}```=====", 'Ran into the same issue when loading a single model with four weight shards, totalling to ~13MB. The tf.loadGraphModel method resolves reasonably quickly on iOS (iPhone7: 3s when developing locally, 9s when installed from testflight) but the load times on Android devices running built release apk are **much slower** leaving the app UI completely unresponsive in the meantime 😕 loadGraphModel taking: 24s on Redmi 7, 60s on nexus 5x, 78s on samsung a10 😖 @zholmes1  Could you elaborate on how you ended up using the _buffers_ array? I don’t see them used in any wayin the posted code and wanted to attempt try your version of the code. Running it I’m also running into an issue where axios returns undefined for response.data if "arraybuffer" responseType is specified.=====']

Thanks for your answer. I was getting the same "GPGPUProgram does not support complex64 input" but it was my bad, I wasn\'t converting the model properly.Now, after changing the implementation of tf.abs for the other one mentioned above I still getting an error:```tensor_list.js:219 Uncaught (in promise) Error: Invalid data types, op elements complex64, but list elements null at TensorList.setItem (tensor_list.js:219) at _callee2$ (control_executor.js:241) at tryCatch (runtime.js:45) at Generator.invoke [as _invoke] (runtime.js:274) at Generator.prototype. [as next] (runtime.js:97) at asyncGeneratorStep (runtime.js:728) at _next (runtime.js:728) at runtime.js:728 at new Promise () at runtime.js:728setItem @ tensor_list.js:218_callee2$ @ control_executor.js:28tryCatch @ runtime.js:45invoke @ runtime.js:272prototype. @ runtime.js:96asyncGeneratorStep @ runtime.js:728_next @ runtime.js:728(anonymous) @ runtime.js:728(anonymous) @ runtime.js:728executeOp @ control_executor.js:28(anonymous) @ operation_executor.js:64executeOp$h @ operation_executor.js:57_loop @ graph_executor.js:491processStack @ graph_executor.js:477_callee4$ @ graph_executor.js:404tryCatch @ runtime.js:45invoke @ runtime.js:272prototype. @ runtime.js:96asyncGeneratorStep @ runtime.js:728_next @ runtime.js:728```The fact is that I\'m trying to convert a Keras model with custom layers to a tf_saved_model using ```tf.saved_model.save``` (this part works well even when I load the pb model in Python) in order to avoid the implementation of the custom layers in TFJS. I don\'t know if it could cause any additional issue.You can get the TFJS model causing the issue here: [model-tfjs-with-custom-complex64-abs-implementation.zip](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/files/5879682/model-tfjs-with-custom-complex64-abs-implementation.zip)Thanks for your help!=====', '@JPery Looks like there are still complex64 type in the model, especially used on TensorList ops. i.e. ("StatefulPartitionedCall/sequential/melspectrogram/stft/stft_tf.signal.stft/map/TensorArrayV2Stack/TensorListStack")It seems to be related to melspectrogram/stft layer or method?=====', 'Hi!I finally found my error. title: Regresssion: WASM fails to load due to _scriptDir not defined
body: This is a regression in `tfjs` 2.8.4 compared to 2.8.3  Setting backend to `wasm` on the main thread results in error:```worker.js onmessage() captured an uncaught exception: ReferenceError: _scriptDir is not defined  threadPrintErr @ e67a52fd-9fdd-4d80-87b0-5a39d7cd567d:1  onmessage @ e67a52fd-9fdd-4d80-87b0-5a39d7cd567d:1ReferenceError: _scriptDir is not defined  WasmBackendModuleThreadedSimd (a0196e5e-0cae-4d78-90e3-7f0714096dfc:1)  onmessage (e67a52fd-9fdd-4d80-87b0-5a39d7cd567d:1)```No issues running TFJS 2.8.3 or older.This is likely related to pull request #4528
comments: ['Hi Vladimir, Thanks for reporting! This is a little bit strange because we did test it in 2.8.4. See this codepin: https://codepen.io/jing-jin/pen/BaLqJoE. If you click "Settings", you can see that the program is loading tfjs core and wasm backend @ 2.8.4.Could you please provide more context/sample code about this issue? Thanks!=====', "Ok, this is related to both #4392 and #4528. Originally `tfjs-backend-wasm` was not fully minification safe when running through a bundler - minify whitespace and minify syntax were ok, but minify identifiers was not. Then #4392 fixed it and everything was fine for a while.Now #4528 (i assume its this one since i don't see other differences) broke it once more and it's even worse since not even minify syntax works anymore. If I disable minification completely, then yes `wasm` works in 2.8.4 - but that is not realistic for production code.So yes, it's a regression. If you want to see a simple project, it's at and bundler runs via `server/build.js`=====", 'closing as fixed in tfjs 2.8.5. thank you!=====', 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====']

title: tf.grad() returns matrix of zeros
body: I trained a CNN on an MNIST dataset, and planned to use it for inference with tf.js.However, when checking the model's gradients with respect to one of the test images, I notice I keep getting a zero matrix. Does anybody know why this issue occur?```function getGradient(img, yTrue) {    yTrue = tf.oneHot(tf.tensor1d([yTrue], 'int32'), 10),    function f(x) {        return tf.metrics.categoricalCrossentropy(yTrue, model.predict(x)),        }    var g = tf.grad(f),    var grad = g(img),    return grad,}```The Python equivalent allowed me to succesfully compute the gradient.```loss_object = tf.keras.losses.CategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True)//already used one-hot encoding to convert the input_labeldef getGradient(input_image, input_label):  with tf.GradientTape() as tape:    tape.watch(input_image)    prediction = model(input_image)    loss = loss_object(input_label, prediction)  gradient = tape.gradient(loss, input_image)  return gradient```

body: **System information**- Have I written custom code (as opposed to using a stock example script provided in TensorFlow.js): yes- OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04): Windows 10- Mobile device (e.g. iPhone 8, Pixel 2, Samsung Galaxy) if the issue happens on mobile device: N/A- TensorFlow.js installed from (npm or script link): npm i @tensorflow/tf-node- TensorFlow.js version (use command below): 2.8.5, but master branch is affected as well- Browser version: N/A- Tensorflow.js Converter Version: N/A**Describe the current behavior**The tf.signal.stft function takes a 1D tensor, and calculates the FFT over a sliding window. The expected result is a 2D Tensor where all the strides contain the FFT according to the input parameters. I believe there's a performance bottleneck in the stft.ts implementation, in the stft_ function: the input (and processed) tensor is sliced into 1D tensors, and rfft is called in a loop. The output is aggregated into an output buffer, which is concatenated and then returned. **Describe the expected behavior**The called tf.spectra.rfft function is batch-aware. There's no reason to slice the processed tensor in stft_, you can pass windowedSignal to the rfft function, still get the same result. The benefit is, that there's no extra memory and processing required to slice/concat the results. Also, in rfft (where fft is called, which is a kernel function) gets a boost (may the backend be in node-cpu / -gpu / webgl / etc) from the calls working on larger set of data. My measurements show at least 3-fold performance increase (see example) using tf-node-cpu.Please consider reviewing the sfft_ function.**Standalone code to reproduce the title: Unknown op: BroadcastArgs
body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): 3.0.0- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): No, but can if told what to change and where**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**BroadcastArgs are not supported. [tf.linspace](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/linspace) changed implementations between TF versions 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 to use BroadcatsArgs and now models using linspace cannot be converted to TFJS.An example model:```import tensorflow as tftf.keras.Sequential([tf.keras.Input(shape=(4,)), tf.keras.layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.linspace(0, 1024, 1))])```If a model like this is run through the tfjs converter the following error is returned:```Unsupported Ops in the model before optimizationBroadcastArgs```**Will this change the current api? How?**No**Who will benefit with this feature?**People who use functions that use BroadcastArgs such as linspace**Any Other info.**

The layer is defined in Python, in which case it needs to be ported to TensorFlow.js or your JavaScript code.Please tell me:do you need to add this class to tfjs?or am I doing something wrong?

title: Build Custom non-trainable Layers using `tf.layers.fn`
body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using):- I'm willing to contribute, just want to make sure this makes sense for someone else, and/or maybe there is already some work in progress related to this**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**## ActualOn my current understanding, building a simple custom layer (like a sum layer) is made by creating a CustomLayer Class```jsconst tf = require('../tf'),class SumLayer extends tf.layers.Layer {	constructor(config) {		super(config),		this.axis = config.axis,		this.keepDims = config.keepDims,	}	/**	* Call() contains the actual numerical computation of the layer.	*	* It is "tensor-in-tensor-out". I.e., it receives one or more	* tensors as the input and should produce one or more tensors as	* the return value.	*	* Be sure to use tidy() to avoid WebGL memory leak.	*/	call(input) {		return tf.tidy(() => {			return tf.sum(input, this.axis, this.keepDims),		}),	}	/**	* GetConfig() generates the JSON object that is used	* when saving and loading the custom layer object.	*/	getConfig() {		const config = super.getConfig(),		Object.assign(config, {axis: this.axis}),		return config,	}	/**	* The static className getter is required by the	* registration step (see below).	*/	static get className() {		return 'SumLayer',	}}/** * Regsiter the custom layer, so TensorFlow.js knows what class constructor * to call when deserializing an saved instance of the custom layer. */tf.serialization.registerClass(SumLayer),```## ExpectedMaybe we could directly create a custom layer like : ```jsconst axis = 2,const keepDims = false,const layer = tf.layers.fn((a) => tf.sum(a, axis, keepDims))```**Will this change the current api? How?**I do not feel it will change anything to current api**Who will benefit with this feature?**Faster prototyping, less code.

title: face-landmarks-detection model caching bounding boxes from previous predictions
body: First I want to thank you for the wonderful work you do.I am using the [face-landmarks-detection model](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/blob/master/face-landmarks-detection). The model is fast and accurate and it works well when using it on a page via a webcam.The problem I am experiencing is because I am not using a webcam but single images with different sizes that are feeded to the model. From what I've seen my issue is similar to this issue: [facelandmarks-detection wrong when image dimensions change](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4131). As it is stated by @yann86 on the referenced issue a solution will be to:```model.pipeline.regionsOfInterest = []```But that can't be done because `pipeline` is marked as private on `FaceMesh` class (same with `regionsOfInterest` on `Pipeline` class).https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/blob/a206fe1fdc1465000a5579db8960e85c7bb032ef/face-landmarks-detection/src/mediapipe-facemesh/index.ts#L250-L251```class FaceMesh implements MediaPipeFaceMesh {  private pipeline: Pipeline,```So after a bit of researching I think a better solution will be to set the configuration parameter `maxContinuousChecks` to `0` at the moment of loading the model. https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/blob/a206fe1fdc1465000a5579db8960e85c7bb032ef/face-landmarks-detection/src/index.ts#L34-L55```/** * Load face-landmarks-detection. ... * @param config - a configuration object with the following properties: *  - `maxContinuousChecks` How many frames to go without running the bounding * box detector. Only relevant if maxFaces > 1. Defaults to 5. ... */export async function load(``` As it is stated on the comment this parameter set the number of "frames to go without running the bounding box detector", after reviewing the code that updates these ROIs it should work.https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/blob/a206fe1fdc1465000a5579db8960e85c7bb032ef/facemesh/src/pipeline.ts#L266-L276```  shouldUpdateRegionsOfInterest(): boolean {    const roisCount = this.regionsOfInterest.length,    ...    return roisCount !== this.maxFaces &&        this.runsWithoutFaceDetector >= this.maxContinuousChecks,  }```But the issue is still there and I think that is because in the function `updateRegionsOfInterest` the new bounding boxes aren't updated because old ones are overlapped (IOU rate is less than 0.25). How?** The only change will be a new transformation for people to use.**Who will benefit with this feature?**I am using this function in my TF model to multiply a tensor from my training batch against a transformation matrix (not dissimilar from a [DFT matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFT_matrix)). My transformation matrix happens to be very sparse (full of 0s in my case) and is suitable to be converted to a sparse tensor. However, I would not get the speed boost (I would get the memory boost) that comes with a sparse tensor unless I use a function like sparse_dense_matmul or sparse matmul.Functionality like this is very useful in signal processing, particularly audio processing (my use case) where transformation matrices like this exist.**Any Other info.**

title: Support use in Worklets, specifically AudioWorklets
body: Please make sure that this is a feature request. As per our [GitHub Policy](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/ISSUES.md), we only address code/doc bugs, performance issues, feature requests and build/installation issues on GitHub. tag:feature_template**System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): 3.0.0- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): would if I could, but the scope's a bit beyond me right now**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**A version of tfjs that works within `WorkletGlobalScope` (for my use case, `AudioWorkletGlobalScope`) would be ideal for processing data off the main thread. Network requests [are disabled](https://github.com/WebAudio/web-audio-api/issues/1439) in this scope, and the global object (`self`) is undefined. The latter prevents a tfjs distribution from even being imported in this scope, and the former would prevent functions like `loadGraphModel` from working, as they rely on fetching data over the network.In addition, TensorFlow and models can't be loaded on the main thread and transferred to an existing `WorkletNode` via `MessagePort` since the objects of course contain functions and hence can't be cloned.**Will this change the current api? How?**Yes, in that model loading functions will need to be altered/added so that they accept prefetched data. I'm unclear on how much altering the use of `self` would change the API, or even how feasible that is.**Who will benefit with this feature?**Anyone looking to process data off the main thread in a `Worklet`. In my case, I'd like to do realtime audio processing using TensorFlow models in an [`AudioWorklet`](https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2017/12/audio-worklet).**Any Other info.**

body: **System information**- TensorFlow.js version (you are using): 2.8.6- Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No): Yes**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state.**Currently the [tf.node.encodeJpeg()](https://js.tensorflow.org/api_node/3.1.0/#node.encodeJpeg) method only accepts Uint8 Tensor3D as input. This is incovenient as many of the tensors generated by images or the [ react-native HOC](https://js.tensorflow.org/api_react_native/0.5.0/#cameraWithTensors) are in dtype: Int32. This makes converting generated tensors back to jpg/png difficult as there isn't any methods for converting Int32 to uint8.**Will this change the current api? How?**This will allow additional input the the encodeJpeg method to allow a broader range of inputs. In addition, this will add more consistency as decodeJpeg() generates an Int32 tensor, but it can't be converted back to the original jpeg with encodeJpeg().**Who will benefit with this feature?**React native users and other users who deal with Tensor3D in Int32 format.**Any Other info.**Example: Tensor3D generated from the [react-native HOC](https://js.tensorflow.org/api_react_native/0.5.0/#cameraWithTensors) , the dtype is Int32 and therefore the original image can't be accessed for OCR, image processing etc.

title: arraySync gets tripped up by complex numbers
body: **System information**Using Tensorflow JS 3.2.0 in NodeJS v15.5.0, MacOS 10.15.7 (19H512)**Describe the current behavior**Running the below code produces the error:```Error: [32,1025] does not match the input size 65600.```**Describe the expected behavior**The code should return a 2-dimensional array of size 32800.**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**```javascriptlet tf = require('@tensorflow/tfjs')let samples = new Float32Array(18048),let res = tf.signal.stft(tf.tensor(samples), 2048, 512, 2048),console.log(res.arraySync()),```**Other info / logs**Tensor info after running stft:```Tensor {  kept: false,  isDisposedInternal: false,  shape: [ 32, 1025 ],  dtype: 'complex64',  size: 32800,  strides: [ 1025 ],  dataId: { id: 3014054 },  id: 453,  rankType: '2',  scopeId: 0}```
comments: ["Ok I think I see what's going on, it's having trouble with the real and imaginary parts of the complex number right?=====", 'Well, in my case I can solve this because I need to run `abs()` on my Tensor anyways which gets rid of the imaginary part.=====', "Ok so, after reading a bit more I'll summarize:When complex64 was added (https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/565), it was decided that dataSync should return both parts of the complex number. That's why the array returned by dataSync is twice as big. However, when arraySync was added this wasn't taken into account, which is why it prints an error. It's trying to fit the bigger array into the same shape.So dataSync is working correctly, but arraySync is not. A potential fix for arraySync would be to change it's shape to return an array where each element is a pair of real/imaginary parts of the complex number, to mirror the behavior of dataSync.I assume the above also applies to the non-sync'd version of arraySync.=====", 'Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue?YesNo=====', 'Thanks for the report Joonatan! =====']

body: I've converted Places365 from Caffe model (GoogleNet variation) to TF saved model using MMDNN and then to TFJS graph model using tensorflowjs_convert  (if needed, I can post actual conversion code or the model itself)  Resulting graph model works fine with tfjs-node (fully tested) and `wasm`, but fails in browser using `webgl` backend:error occurs during call to `predict()`:```logwebgl_util.js:82 Uncaught (in promise) Error: Failed to compile fragment shader.    at createFragmentShader (webgl_util.js:82)    at GPGPUContext.createProgram (gpgpu_context.js:199)    at compileProgram (gpgpu_math.js:44)    at backend_webgl.js:694    at MathBackendWebGL.getAndSaveBinary (backend_webgl.js:731)    at MathBackendWebGL.runWebGLProgram (backend_webgl.js:693)    at Object.padV2$1 [as kernelFunc] (PadV2.js:27)    at kernelFunc (engine.js:463)    at engine.js:524    at Engine.scopedRun (engine.js:337)```with actual error being:```logERROR: 0:178: 'Infinity' : undeclared identifier```and generated GLSL code in question is:```glslvoid main() {  ivec4 outputLoc = getOutputCoords(),  vec4 result = vec4(0.),  ivec4 rc = outputLoc,  if (any(lessThan(rc, start)) || any(greaterThanEqual(rc, end))) {    result[0] = float(-Infinity), // <-- ERROR 'Infinity' : undeclared identifier  } else {    ivec4 source = rc - start,    result[0] = getChannel(getX(source.x,source.y,source.z,source.w), vec2(source.z,source.w)),  }  ...```Which comes from `tfjs-backend-webgl/mirror_pad_packed_gpu.ts` `class PadPackedProgram`:```glsl  result[${i}] = float(${constantValue}),```Where `constantValue` is set in attributes of PadV2 in the model itself.Per OpenGL specs, there are no pre-defined constants, so this is bound to fail unless constant is either converted to value or set by TFJS itself.Or another way would be to address this in the converter itself so `Infinity` is translated to numeric value during conversion?Environment: tfjs 3.2.0 on chrome 88 on ubuntu 20.10```tensorflowjs_converter --versiontensorflowjs 3.2.0Dependency versions:  keras 2.4.0  tensorflow 2.4.1```

title: No easy way to change the input shapes for a built model for transfer learning
body: #### TensorFlow.js version0.11.7#### Browser versionN/A#### Describe the problem or feature requestIf I load a pretrained TFJS model, there is no easy way to change the input shapes it takes in.For instance, if I load [`Mobilenet`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-examples/tree/master/mobilenet), and I want to perform transfer learning on it, I have no easy way to get the model to take different shapes (even if the model is fully convolutional).#### Code to reproduce the bug / link to feature request```js  const model = await tf.loadModel('https://storage.googleapis.com/tfjs-models/tfjs/mobilenet_v1_0.25_224/model.json')    const test = tf.zeros([1, 512, 512, 3])  const preds = model.predict(test) ```#### Expected output:`preds` is a tensor of the output of the model#### Actual output: ```jsError: Error when checking : expected input_1 to have shape [null,224,224,3] but got array with shape [1,512,512,3].```This is especially needed when you need to transfer some layers of a loaded model into another:```jsconst someLayers = tf.sequential({layers: model.layers.slice(0, 5)})someLayers.predict(test)```It would be good if there was some way to `unbuild` a layer, or if there was some easy way to clone a layer (keeping everything but the shapes & topology), potentially like:```jsconst convLayers = model.layers.slice(0, 5).map(l => l.unbuilt()) // or l.clone(), l.clone({withoutShape: true}), etcconst someLayers = tf.sequential({layers: convLayers})```WDYT? I would be happy to author a PR for it unless someone else is working on something similar.

It seems to me more straightforward to use one of the two following approaches:1) Before you feed your new image to the model, resample it to the required shape. This can probably be done with some sort of HTML5 canvas tricks.2) Add a "image resampling" layer type to tensorflow.js and/or Keras, and create a new sequential model with the resampling layer as the first layer and the original model as the second layer (note that sequential models can be nested.) Keras doesn\'t have such a layer AFAIK. The closest is UpSampling2D, which allows you to change the size of the image only by positive integer factors.=====', "Essentially what I'm looking for is a way to get a copy of the layer that has the same weights but no input/output shape information (i.e, before the layer was put into a model), as it was before it was built, such that I could use the layer in an other model.=====", "@aman-tiwari I still don't quite understand your proposal.
