The above would certainly be good but would just require changing the API and having it return float values.=====", '> The above would certainly be good but would just require changing the API and having it return float values.Yes i think we can add a flag in the BodyPix function call to let a user determine the output type he or she wants to have. e.g. `use_float_segmentation=True (default False)`. This way it can be a bit more flexible in terms of the API return type. What do you think? I have a feeling that combining soft alpha mask/segmenation and the edge blur you have implemented would give us the optimal bokeh effect.=====', "@tylerzhu-github It's best to avoid having a flag that changes the return type because that may add confusion for people and it adds more to document.   I'm wondering if just returning the float values from the API makes sense - and not doing the segmentation threshold in the api.  Since users are going to be calling methods that convert the output to a mask, using the method `toMaskImageData` (see the documentation [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/blob/a045fd58a464c1bb89e645e7b2ecc17b27d7916f/body-pix/src/output_rendering_util.ts#L145)), and that already iterates through all the pixels, we could actually just apply the threshold there.  So the high level suggestion is:* for `estimatePersonSegmentation` - the api returns float values for each pixel.* in `toMaskImageData` - add an argument for `segmentationThreshold` - it is optional.  When it is set it converts to a binary mask image and uses that threshold.  When not set returns grayscale ImageData with the original float values.Some downsides to this:*  it is inconsistent with the `estimateBodyPartSegmentation` return because that returns integer values in the array, as there the segmentation threshold is applied to the output to crop the body parts.  * Threshold is performed on CPU, but performance hit is negligent as the user would be using `toMaskImageData` anyways.* Have to re-do a bit of work and documentation.As it is currently:```javascriptconst outputStride = 16,const flipHorizontal = false,const segmentationThreshold = 0.5,// segmentation contains a BinaryArrayconst segmentation = await net.estimatePersonSegmentation(imageElement, flipHorizontal, outputStride, segmentationThreshold),// creates an ImageData by iterating through the array.const mask = bodyPix.toMaskImageData(personSegmentation, invert),bodyPix.drawImageWithMask(    canvas, imageElement, mask, opacity, edgeBlurAmount, flipHorizontal),```With above changes it looks like:```javascript// segmentation contains a Float arrayconst segmentation = await net.estimatePersonSegmentation(imageElement, flipHorizontal, outputStride,// creates a binary ImageData by iterating through the array and checking if value matches segmentation threshold.const mask = bodyPix.toMaskImageData(personSegmentation, invert, segmentationThreshold),bodyPix.drawImageWithMask(    canvas, imageElement, mask, opacity, edgeBlurAmount, flipHorizontal),```What do you think @dsmilkov @nsthorat ?=====", 'Thanks for the explanations Dan! Will let Daniel and Nikhil make the final call.Your suggested API changes (returning float type instance mask and moving binary thresholding to `toMaskImageData` function) makes sense. In terms of the inconsistency between instance mask and body part masks after this change, we could  leave it as is or return each body part mask as a separate instance mask. More specifically body part masks will be an array of 24 elements and each element is a float type 2D mask similar to the person instance mask. =====']

title: tf.norm and tf.abs(_: complex64) are not underflow-safe.
body: To get help from the community, check out our [Google group](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs).#### TensorFlow.js versionv0.13.8#### Browser versionAny#### Describe the problem or feature requestOne of the most important norm properties is the positive definiteness:`|x|=0 <=> x=0`The current implementation of `tf.abs(_: complex64)` and `tf.norm` do not satisfy that property for some fringe cases where underflow becomes an issue. `Math.fround(1e-23**2)` rounds down to `0` and therefore the norm would become zero. This can cause issues, e.g. when normalizing a complex number or a vector, or when trying to determine convergence of an optimization.An underflow-safe implementation can be found [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Math/hypot). In WebGL there is a [length](https://www.khronos.org/files/opengles_shading_language.pdf#page=74) function that can be used both for `tf.abs` as well for `tf.norm` as binary reduction operator.#### Code to reproduce the bug / link to feature request```tsconst x = tf.tensor1d([1e-23,0]),x.norm().print(),// Output://   Tensor//       0```
comments: ['Closing this as the related PR has been merged, thank you.=====', "PR#1391 fixes underflow in `tf.abs` but *not* in `tf.norm`, I'm afraid. The latter is fixable with one or two lines of code but it will at least double the memory and computation overhead of the operation. I can file a PR for that as soon as I get to implement it.The performance and memory overhead could be avoided by adding an addtional reduction operation to the backend which should be even faster than the current `tf.norm`. That would however require bigger changes. ====="]

comments: ['This is my attempt to fix some problems.My view may be incorrect, but I believe that resultUV from the vertex shader ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, so the boundary pixel may get 1.0, output coordinates should be adjusted as so.On the other hand, the sampler should not use maximum value of 1.0.[https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Rectangle_Texture](https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Rectangle_Texture)> When using rectangle samplers, all texture lookup functions automatically use non-normalized texture coordinates. This means that the values of the texture coordinates refer specifically to texels in texel space. The value 12.5 is halfway between the thirteenth and fourteenth texel (remember: 0-base indices).Therefore, I believe halfCR is not required and I added adjuv() to adjust the value.=====', 'After reading [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7272579/iphone-opengl-es-2-0-pixel-perfect-textures/7272871#7272871](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7272579/iphone-opengl-es-2-0-pixel-perfect-textures/7272871#7272871), I think that I was wrong."halfCR" should be used. =====', 'Based on the results of previous tests, I think my previous view may not be totally incorrect.I think there are actually two kinds of WebGL implementations.One is assuming texture pixel centers being integers, and the other assuming pixel centers being halfway between integers.Therefore, I updated the code to use vec2(0.25) to adjust instead.=====', "@xianreb is there an issue that this is fixing or can you explain what you're seeing that this resolves?=====", '@nsthorat Originally, I found the GPU backend accuracy/performance was not matching CPU backend on my computer. I started analyzing the tfjs-core code and found there may be some potential problems and tried to fix that. I am not sure whether these changes are actually fixing these potential problems or not, but the new code did pass the tests. Maybe some of them are unnecessary or totally irrelevant.Later, I found that the main cause was the max texture size as mentioned in [https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/510](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/510). Either the GPU reported the wrong max texture size, or it did not work correctly when max texture size was used.=====']

title: Add aarch64 support for tfjs-node
body: Modify the install.js to support external binaries while installingnpm package. It reads the `custom-binary.json` configuration file toget URLs for the following resources:- 'tf-lib': libtensorflow and libtensorflow_framework shared libraries. Its value is a URL that points to a `tar.gz` or `zip` and contains the shared libaries and header files.- 'addon': pre-compiled node binding. Its value is a object contains three values: `host`, `remote_path` and `package_name`. These three values are concatenated into a URL that points to the pre-compiled node binding.If you only provide `tf-lib` and no `addon`. It compiles the nodebinding while installing the npm package.Signed-off-by: Yihong Wang To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2513)

title: [webgpu] Add numBytesAllocated
body: Tensor.dispose will not free the GPU's video memory but push the buffer into a freeBuffers Map.The freeBuffers is TFJS's free buffer. But to the GPU, it is allocated buffer (Suppose it isvirtual memory).If not call Tensor.dispose in a loop, the freeBuffers will grow bigger as the size of the loopgets bigger. And finally, the GPU runs out of memory. At the same time, numBytesInGPU keeps growing.If call Tensor.dispose in a loop, numBytesInGPU is very small(4194304), and remains unchanged duringall trials. However, the allocated memory may be much bigger(847249424) than numBytesInGPU. The application may run out of memory when the numBytesInGPU keeps small.So numBytesInGPU is not a good indicator for GPU memory usage. This CL introduced numBytesAllocatedInGPU. numBytesAllocatedInGPU is an indicator to measure how much memory is allocated from GPU's video memory.It differs from numBytesInGPU in that:numBytesInGPU indicates how much memory is used by Tensors.numBytesAllocatedInGPU indicates the TFJS application has allocated how much memory. Some of the memory are used by Tensors, some are just kept in the freeBuffers pool. For the OOM case, it is a better indicator.numBytesInGPU = memory of accquireBuffer - memory of releaseBuffer.numBytesAllocatedInGPU = memory of GPUDevice.createBuffer - memory of GPUBuffer.destroyHints for how to use benchmark's time function: choose trials and reps carefully, too big trials andreps may lead to unstable performance data or OOM.How to test, add log after trial's dispose:```for (let t = 0, t < trials, ++t) { const start = tf.util.now(), await trial(), times.push(tf.util.now() - start), if (disposeAfterEachTrial) { dispose(), } console.log("numBytesInGPU = " + (tf.memory() as WebGPUMemoryInfo).numBytesInGPU + ", numBytesAllocatedInGPU = " + (tf.memory() as WebGPUMemoryInfo). numBytesAllocatedInGPU)}```Test result:1. Not call dispose in loop, disposeAfterEachTrial === falseTest case:``` it('transpose', async () => { const x = tf.randomNormal([1024, 1024]), await time(() => tf.transpose(x, [1, 0]), null, false, 10, 200), }),```Memory usage data:numBytesInGPU=838860800, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=1673527296, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=1681915920numBytesInGPU=2508193792, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=2516582416numBytesInGPU=3342860288, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=3351248912numBytesInGPU=4177526784, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=4185915408numBytesInGPU=5012193280, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=5020581904numBytesInGPU=5846859776, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=5855248400numBytesInGPU=6681526272, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=6689914896numBytesInGPU=7516192768, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=7524581392numBytesInGPU=8350859264, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=83592478882. Call dispose in loop, disposeAfterEachTrial===trueTest case:``` it('transpose', async () => { const x = tf.randomNormal([1024, 1024]), await time(() => tf.transpose(x, [1, 0]), null, true, 10, 200), }),```Memory usage data:numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424numBytesInGPU=4194304, numBytesAllocatedInGPU=847249424---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2526)

title: Split NonMaxSuppressionV3 and NonMaxSuppresionV5 to two APIs
body: Because in the C implementation, the V3 has 1 output but the V5 has 3 outputs, we have to define different APIs for them. Otherwise, models that uses NonMaxSuppressionV5 may break because subsequent Op may need to access the second or the third output.Changes made:1. Add one more API for V5 in backend.ts2. Add one more API for V5 in image_op.ts3. Add corresponding implementations for CPU and GPU.4. Add corresponding tests.Note: 1. @kangyizhang identified this issue, because the Node test break, expecting different output shape. After this change, tested Node code locally and it passed.2. Python API also splits into two APIs (non_max_suppression and non_max_suppression_with_score). tfjs naming follows the Python API naming found here: https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/image/non_max_suppression3. This implementation naturally includes V4. Will add V4 API in another PR. V4 will also require a different API because the output is also different.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2557)

comments: ['@annxingyuan @kainino0x Please take a look.The main reason that the previous method is slow is because that we fetch the data as [channel, height, width] sequence not [height, width, channel]. But the data is stored as [height, width, channel] in memory. That results the data fetching is not continuous in memory which is time-consuming.You can see this change in https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/2620/commits/b2860297d50ad0e9499f890e1b4c70c7602c5fa6#diff-d0f5478de3197c2a9075a8a33e7e8905L120  (the calculation of WRow, WCol, channel) to get more details.=====', "> Just to make sure I understand your comment on #2568 - are you saying that with this change, running the im2Col shader separately is always slower?Sorry, I missed this one. Theoretically, the time used by these two methods are very close.  However, in my test, im2col is good for Intel GPU, not that friendly for AMD GPU. The change in this method can benefit both. But I can't say im2col is not needed anymore. I find in some situations, im2col is better than the current method for Intel GPU. I need more time to analysis it and understand the hardware. Also it's hard for me to only apply some changes to a specific GPU due to web's limit.====="]

title: [tfjs-react-native] Add functions for streaming camera data into tensors.
body: Adds functions for converting camera data to tensors for realtime use in model predictions.### MotivationPrimary goal of this PR is to enable real time use of camera data with models like posenet/bodypix etc. This is achieved by using the `createCameraTextureAsync` of expo-gl to get a reference to a texture that will be updated by the underlying OS with the preview contents of an expo.Camera component.Because: 1) Texture objects are not shareable between WebGL contexts 2) There is a fair amount of distinct global GL state between the tfjs WebGL context and that provided by expo-gl 3) The expo webgl context is being used in two distinct true threads without a means to synchronize operations to it.The approach is to download texture values to the CPU and then construct a tensor from there. ### ApproachTo make this practical for high resolution camera views and convenient for users to pass into models which typically accept smaller images with no alpha channel. This PR provides functionality to _resize images_ and in some cases _drop the alpha channel data_ __before__ data is downloaded to CPU (i.e. on the expo-gl context that originated the camera texture). This is helpful in mitigating serialization costs between the native and JS threads.This PR introduces the base functionality for this as well as a demo with PoseNet. A future PR will provide sugar in form of a react component that users can just mount and pass callbacks to.### StructureThe core functionality is found in camera/camera.ts and includes: - `fromTexture`: a function that converts an image tensor to a tensor, optionally doing a resize and alpha channel drop along the way - `toTexture`: a function that converts a tensor to a texture that can be displayed in the expo-gl context (which can be controlled by the end user). This can be used to render the resized image. - `renderToGLView`: A helper function to draw a texture to the screen (using the expo-gl context).These are supported by a number of helper/utility functions and shader programs.There is also a new screen in the integration test app that demos this with a realtime posenet demo.### TestsThis PR also has a number of tests that run on device and introduces a mechanism to run unit tests specific to tfjs-react-native on device. A future PR will migrate all the tests that are currently run in the browser with shims to run on device.---------------------To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2657)

title: [WIP] Disable shader key and shader cache
body: FIXWhat happens:Run case one by one (yarn test --grep=), pass. But when run several together. Some case may fail.Example case:Case may be failed due to cache reasons(div/Arithmetic_test.ts):'gradient: Tensor1D with int32', // Actual != expected.'gradient: Tensor2D', // Actual != expected.'gradient: Tensor2D / Tensor2D w/ broadcast', // Actual != expected.Root cause:This problem is introduced by two reasons:1), makeShaderKey called before the real shader generated(compileProgram and makeShader).Which means, two different shaders may possibly share the same shader key.2), The shader key optimization(https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/2451), which useseveral key properties of the shader instead of the full shader source as shader key.For most case, especially all properties are self-contained in the shader`s WebGPUProgramfile, this works. But when some properties are originated from the shader_preprocessor.ts,two different shader may be collided with the same shader key.Currently the fix is to disable the shader key and shader cache first.The follow up todo is: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/2669.Also add square and neg operators.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2670)

title: [tfjs-core] Modularize squaredDiff
body: This PR modularizes squaredDifference in a manner that is non-breaking but consistent with our future plans for modularization. A few takeaways I got from this:- We should defer modularizing tfjs-node kernels until we can do a release of core that exports `kernel_names.ts` - We need to keep using runKernelFunc to not break backends outside of core that do not use the registry (e.g. webgpu).- tfjs-node can continue to co-locate kernel registration with kernel definition as we have no need to bundle size reduction in that context (as there is no bundle).- Its nice having kernel_names.ts be the single source of truth for kernel names, input specs and attr specs. The latter two could be moved into another file, but i don't think we need to do that. To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2775)

Short term solution is to apply the same strategy that WASM package use to use script to change back to symlink. Cons is, (1) people need to remember run test at least once before submit the PR, because CI won't do the link. (2) it's possible people may develop against pinned version if they don't run the test first.Long term solution (hopefully will come soon), always keep symlink in development code and master branch. body: The cases included in this PR may fail when dilation and padding (padding is fixed in another PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/2993) are no properly applied. Currently there is only one (fused)conv2d test case, "throws when both stride and dilation are greater than 1", whose strides are [2, 1], and filter size is 2x2, with valid padding. And this case can not capture the dilation and padding misuse very well.This PR adds stride [2,2] and filter 3x3, with same padding. The pattern is originated from handpose model (https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/tree/master/handpose). body: Add necessary commands for linking and building dependency packages. p.s. it explicitly build dependencies including the nested dependencies. This is because, if we rely on transitive dependency building, which means the union package, tfjs's, build-ci has to include build-layers-ci, build-data-ci, etc, which will result in these packages built twice, one from cloudbuild.yml, and one from build. This adds too much hidden processes and is error-prone. To make things simple, packages that have nested dependencies, currently only tfjs-node, should take care of building all the dependencies it needs. This is the same behavior if we use yalc link/publish, which doesn't take care of nested dependency either.p.p.s. Need to remove 'scripts' from tfjs-converter's tsconfig file, and also change the main entry and type in the package.json file. Otherwise, typescript can't find modules symlinked. This issue is reported in typescript's repo, solution is to change from dist/src/index.js to dist/index.js: https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/23502We shouldn't be too worried, because after the change, tfjs-converter's tsconfig and main/type entry will be exactly same as data and layers, which should have been the same in the first place.This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2854)

title: Release and diffing change.
body: Preparing for release process change. This PR includes below changes:(1) Make diffing logic more generic. It introduces baseBranch, so the script no longer assume diff against master, it will diff against whatever baseBranch cloud build send. This information is ultimately from GitHub.(2) Add a step in release script, asking which release branch to send the PR to.(3) Generate a unique local branch for the PR each time. The branches need to be deleted afterwards.(4) Automate pull-request to send the PR to the release branch, not master.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2885)

title: Remove link-master. Refactor test steps.
body: This PR is mainly clean-up, it touches these packages: layers, converter, data, union package, node, and node-gpu.It has below changes:1. Remove link-master in package.json, and deleted link-master.js and link-core-master.js from top level scripts folder. Since the new release process is in place, master's dependency structure will be stable. Remove the short term solution. 2. Refactor package.json and cloudbuild.yml. Make sure for both test and test-ci, it build dependency packages and then build itself and then lint and then test. The differences between test and test-ci are (1) test-ci use the ci version of build for the dependency packages instead of regular build, (2) test-ci also has lint and build, whereas test doesn't to make it lightweight for local development.p.s. We have to put the build dependencies step in test-ci, not in cloudbuild.yml, because integration test also needs to call test-ci, but will not use the same cloudbuild.yml. Put build dependencies in test-ci makes sure it will always have all the things it needs for testing no matter where test-ci is called.p.p.s. We made the decision for each package's build, only build itself, build-deps shouldn't be included. This is because include it will cause some common packages to be rebuilt many many times in a transitive build process.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2913)

title: modularize broadcastTo op
body: Modularizes the broadCastTo op without updating kernels. (as previously discussed with Ann and Na)A few things emerged while doing this.- Since the forward mode of broadcastTo currently just uses the `tile` op but the backward mode is a different computation than the one of tile. This requires declaring a new kernel for broadcastTo that backends will have to implement (that they use tile is an implementation detail internal to them). Right now that kernel does not exist.- The grad func of broadCastTo requires attrs, so this has been added to the gradFunc interface and to the tape mechanism for computing gradients.- broadcastTo was not a chained op, nor in the backend interface, so I added it as a chained op for consistency.- Added a place to test that chained ops exist on tensor instances.- There is some temporary casting from to and from the unknown type because NamedTensorMap and NamedTensorInfoMap do not overlap. Once we switch to runKernel in future both the ops and kernels will likely be using NamedTensorInfoMap and we can reduce the type mismatch. To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2919)

title: Create publish-npm.ts
body: Automate publish npm for new release process. Changes in this PR:1. Created an interactive script for publishing packages to npm. It is based on the ./scripts/publish-npm.sh, with below differences in terms of logic: 1.a. Takes two parameters, package (e.g. tfjs-core) and release branch (e.g. tfjs_1.7.1). Note, release branch will be inferred if not the first package in the release unit, otherwise need user input. 1.b. The new script doesn't run ./scripts/make-version.js. This is already ran in release.ts, so I think no need to make-version again during publish. However, I realized that the version bump in package.json's version field and version.ts will only get updated in each release branch, master won't get updated anymore. We should update master in release.ts script. 1.c. publish-npm.ts will create temporary dir, and checkout the release branch, and publish from there. Whereas publish-npm.sh just uses master in local branch. So this should be an improvement. 1.d. Overall flow for publish-npm.sh is: Ask release unit -> Ask phase -> Infer release branch and Ask to correct if needed -> Publish for all the packages in the phase from the release branch.2. Extract some utils used by both release.ts and publish-npm.ts to a util file.3. Added `yarn publish-npm`4. In release.ts, added logic to update package.json and version.ts of master branch.5. Set yarn to use npm registry as a one-off when publish. Some background, shell changes to Yarn's scope and Yarn uses a different registry. So when we do 'npm publish' in the same shell, it will throw "npm ERR! code ENEEDAUTH". We need to set yarn to use npm's registry. There are three ways to do it, (1) set env YARN_REGISTRY to point to npm as a one off in the current shell, and run yarn publish. (2) add a .yarnrc file in the project root directory with a line 'registry https://registry.npmjs.org/'. We adopt (1), because (2) may be a bigger change, involving regenerating yarn.lock files. See discussions of this issue: https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/issues/2935---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2928)

title: modularise clone op
body: Strawman PR for discussion:This PR modularises the clone op. But does so differently to how most ops will be modularised. There are three distinct things here:1. The kernel and gradient registration is done within the op file and the kernel name and interface __are not__ in kernel_names.ts. This is done under the _assumption_ that we don't expect backends to need to implement `clone` (and thus do not list it in the kernel_names file). It is also done under the assumption that we always want clone available in tfjs/tfjs-core.2. It does not add a chained op augmentor for clone. This is under a hunch that we will want some subset of ops to always be on tensor. To my eye this includes things like cast, reshape, buffer, as2D, as3D, asType, etc (but we can make a list if we agree with this hunch with the goal of keeping it as small as possible). These would remain on the backend interface / opHandler mechanism. This is primarily with an eye to developer ergonomics (including internal code).3. It registers a backend agnostic kernels.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2935)

title: Remove master branch version update.
body: This PR has following changes:1. Remove master branch version update in release.ts script. Context: If we also have to update master branch every time releasing every package, 2 PRs need to be approved instead of 1, for each package. Also it runs tests redundantly, draining the CI resources too much. The version update in master is informational anyway, because the real version to be published will be in corresponding release branch. We will have other ways to provide version information, probably add a badge for npm version in readme.2. Change package.json version field and version.ts to 0.0.0 for each package. Context: Instead of deleting the field and the version.ts file altogether, we decided to keep change minimal.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2958)

title: [webgpu] Add modularized nonMaxSuppression kernel
body: FIX https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/2361nonMaxSuppression is implemented by CPU. When running in WebGL backend, WebGL supports readSync. If passing any tensors reside in GPU to it, nonMaxSuppression can automatically read back GPU data to CPU.When running in WebGPU backend, WebGPU doesn't support readSync. If passing any tensors reside in GPU to it directly, nonMaxSuppression may complains "WebGPU readSync is only available for CPU-resident tensors". So before this, call await first to gurantee the tensors are in CPU.The related issue for this: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/2976.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/2963)

title: [core]Modularize addN.
body: Changes in this PR include:(1) Split AddN out from binary_ops.(2) Split AddN's gradient out to a separate file.(3) Add logic to engine to handle array of inputs to save.Context for (3), the gradient modularization requires a gradConfig for each gradient function in their separate file. This gradConfig has a inputsToSave field, currently the logic is that inputsToSave field will specify tensors to save: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L669. But it couldn't handle the case that the inputs have dynamic length of Tensors to save. To deal with this, we can introduce a flag saveAllInputs to gradConfig, which indicates to engine that simply save all the inputs.An alternative is to change the inputsToSave type from Tensor[] to Array, but this generates more issues than desired, for example, a lot of the places (logging, profiling, backward functions, etc.) expect the simple form Tensor[], and has logic to access each array element and their shape or dtype, etc. Changing will cause to add more logic to evaluate whether it is an array or a tensor. See this PR for the places to change, and this PR still fails with 10 more places to fix, at which point, I gave up on this solution: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/compare/master...lina128:addn_try?expand=1 I think the first solution is much simpler and elegant.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3002)

We just need to introduce a flag to gradConfig to handle the case where inputs has a dynamic number of elements to save and we just want to save all inputs. The second solution (in another PR, link in this PR's description) requires logic change in many places, need to understand from Daniel and Nikhil whether this is needed. And what's the original thoughts to handle array of Tensors as object of Tensors with array index as key.====="]

title: Move cpu backend out of tfjs-core
body: Moves the CPU backend out of tfjs-core into its own package/top level folder.- tfjs-backend-cpu is a devDependency of core to enable tests that depend on CPU specifically or more generally on having some backend present. This does create a circular dep between packages with respect to test running. But there are some workarounds to make the two libs build (using require over import in some places).- tfjs-backend-cpu is a now a devDependency of most of the other packages as they relied on CPU backend for running tests.- This PR allows re-registration of a kernel for a given backend (overwriting the prev kernel config). This is because WebGL backend is still in core and registers kernels as a side effect and core is a dependency of tfjs-backend-cpu. Thus in tests some double registration happens. Once WebGL is out of core the old behaviour could be restored. - As far as dependency structure for testing, this PR tries to mirror the status quo. We can tune stuff around when tests get called for what in future.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3008)

title: [cpu] Fix build and deps.
body: This PR fixes several things:1. `build` should never have transitive build, it can cause several problems. So in Core, its build should only build itself, never add dependency build here, it should be in build-deps.2. `build-deps` should build all the dependencies including the transitive deps. So for Core, it means cpu and itself (dependency through cpu). For cpu, it means core and itself (dependency through core). This will not cause infinite loop because build only build the package itself, which is the key.For more context on why we need to do it this way, I'm copying the explanation in my design doc:"`build-deps` - Builds the dependency packages. Note for existing and new packages, if there are nested dependencies, this cmd should directly build all dependencies including transitive ones. To illustrate why we need to do it this way, if we spell out the dependency graph in Fig. 2 for Node, it looks like this: tfjs-backend-node -> [tfjs] -> [tfjs-data, tfjs-converter, tfjs-core, tfjs-layers] -> [tfjs-converter, tfjs-core, tfjs-layers]. If we want to rely on transitive build, then any package’s build also needs to build the dependencies, this will result in some packages rebuild many many times unnecessarily. For example, if tfjs doesn’t only build itself, but also build the other four packages it depends on. Then data also doesn’t only build itself, but also build the other two packages it depends on. Core will be rebuilt many times, as do layers and converter. So to avoid that, each package should only build itself. The build-deps should take care of building all the dependencies needed. For Node, this will be tfjs, tfjs-data, tfjs-converter, tfjs-core, and tfjs-layers."---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3064)

title: Update packages to compile to ESM modules by default
body: **Switch default compile (tsc) options from CommonJS (modules) + ES5 (javascript target version) to ESM (modulex) + ES2017 (javascript target version).** This PR also turns the union package into something releasable (with backend-cpu and backend-webgl.**Rollup**Rollup is used to produce a number of new bundles across the packages: - tf-[package-name].node.js — a CommonJS+ES5 bundle for node that package.main points to. - tf-[package-name].js — a UMD+ES5 bundle for use in browsers/script tags. package.jsdeliver, package.browser & package.unpkg should point to this. - tf-[package-name].min.js — same as above but minified - tf-[package-name].es2017.js — a UMD+ES217 bundle for use in browsers/script tags. - tf-[package-name].es2017.min.js — same as above but minifiedNote that because **package.main** now points to **tf-[package-name].node.js**. Rollup must be run before that package can be imported by other packages in node.js (i.e. all of our scripts and infra).**dist/**`dist/` (excluding the files listed above) contains the output from tsc, which is now ESM+ES2017 code. This means that any toolchain that does a “dist import” needs to be able to handle ESM+ES2017.This has been enabled in the build and test scripts using two optionsIn environments that require commonjs+es5 (i.e. node) we use **tsc with a different tsconfig (tsconfig.test.json)** to compile the javascript down to the level expected by that tool. In karma driven test runs we use karma-typescript-es6-transform to transpile ES2017 to ES5, babel polyfills are included as well since that is required by the output of the transform.You will notice many references to tsconfig.test.json or more local tsconfigs geared towards running scripts and tests rather than the main tsconfig, which is geared towards producing ESM.This PR also includes some general unification/updating of rollup configs, karma configs and related dependencies. We now get a bundle visualization for every package.**Package.module**package.module now points to dist/index.js (ESM+ES2017). This means any consumer (including end users) that uses the module entry needs to be able to handle that format. We definitely need ESM but can be more flexible on what javascript version we target. I chose 2017 for this PR to lay the groundwork for what we want to do in 3.x. But _we can choose_ any version between ES5 and ES2017+ and the setup in this PR should just work. **Tree shaking**The primary motivation for this is to enable tree-shaking. An example of that is pulling a single function from another package. The graph below shows the bundle visualization for **tfjs-backend-webgl**, which imports a function `transposeImpl` from tfjs-backend-cpu. Notice the tiny sliver at the top of the image that represents that single function being pulled in.**Bundle Size**One motivation for pushing on enabling ES2017 now is bundle size due to less transpilation. Right off the bat we see savings: - Union package bundle today (tf.min.js v1.7.2) — 921.5 kB - Union package bundle with ES2017 (tf.2017.min.js) — 810.7kB (12% size reduction)**Other changes**The ES5 bundle for the union package now includes polyfills, so it will work in IE11.**Other notes** - This hasn’t gone through the nightly tests, so there will likely be a few more scripts that need the new tsconfig. If you are aware of something else that would be affected by this but you don’t see covered please let me know. This is particularly relevant if you are using a “dist import” somewhere that I didn’t catch. - I was hitting browserstack limits so I took tfjs-vis out of the test matrix (after getting it passing on CI) to make it easier for the build to run to completion. I will restore it after this gets merged. Usage docs have not been updated (e.g. using core needs a backend). I plan on doing this after doing 2.x pre-release and testing these packages through some of our other code (examples, models, etc).--------To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3112)

title: Fix webgl bundling and test invocation
body: This fixes 2 things:1. The webgl bundle was not correctly including the transposeImpl import from CPU (it was treating it as an external). This fixes that and restores the tree-shaking ability in spite of the side effects in index.ts of tfjs-backend-cpu.2. Adds `--skip-ignore` to some ts-node invocations. This resolves an issue that is only visible during release PRs. By default ts-node will always exclude files that are in node_modules (even if your code imports them and regardless of your tsconfig). This is not an issue during development or regular PRs because we use symlinks, thus when loading something like jasmine_util, the final path is not in node_modules. However when you build a packaged with pinned versions downloaded from npm, these files are in node_modules. Adding this flag allows them to be resolved and should allow CI to pass on release PRs.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3225)

title: Start moving integration tests to top level folder. Introduce a tag mechanism for smoke and regression tests.
body: This PR does the following:1. Create a top level e2e folder and a package.json to manage all the integration tests.2. Use test-ci.sh to control which tests to run.3. Introduce a tag mechanism to filter tests by tags, smoke, regression, etc.4. Name integration tests by CUJ.5. Moved integration tests in Layers folder to e2e. 6. Expand test scope to test for each backend instead of just one backend. Note, in this PR only cpu and webgl are listed as backends for testing. Will add Node and WASM in a followup PR.Note: Layers integration tests used to run for every Layers' related PR and nightly. After this change, those tests will only run in nightly. It's up to us to decide whether we want to keep the integration tests for PR too. For that, we just need to introduce a LAYERS tag, and set it up in test-ci.sh.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3285)

title: float16 quantization + granular quantization
body: As discussed in #3221 this enables support for quantizing to float16 over the wire. Some models perform better with float16 quantization versus the current integer-based affine scaling method.I also needed the ability so support a form of granular quantization where I want to quantize only certain values. This PR also includes these changes to the converter, no changes are required to the core in order to support this.To recap the major changes are:## Converter`--quantization_bytes` is no longer a flag in the converter. It didn't make sense as we support two methods for 2 bytes. I added three new flags: `--quantize_float16`, `--quantize_uint8`, `--quantize_uint16`. These flags can be supplied on their own or you can specify specific weight names or groups of weights using a wildcard expansion. For example,```--quantize_float16=conv/*/weights--quantize_uint16=conv/*/biases--quantize_uint8```Would quantize weights that match the prefix `conv/` to float16, all biases with the prefix `conv/` using 2 byte affine quantization, and all remaining weights with 1 byte affine quantization.## Weight DecodingThe only other addition revolves around decoding the float16 values in Javascript to float32 values. JS doesn't support any form of `Float16Array` at this time so I manually decode the weights using a table-based lookup method that is referenced from http://www.fox-toolkit.org/ftp/fasthalffloatconversion.pdf ## TestingI tested this myself with my own models and was able to deterministically reproduce my own results from Python TF. I wrote some tests for the float16 decoding edge cases and a couple of basic decoding test cases.All the converter test cases are passing and I wrote a couple more tests for the new quantization scheme.I haven't really tested the converter wizard yet, it doesn't run locally for me (`tf.app` is not supported?) and I haven't gotten around to building the pip package to test it out. I think the wizard quantization flow is kind of weird and will probably require some modifications.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3340)
comments: ["Hi @pyu10055,Thanks for taking a look, I resolved most of the issues you outlined. I need to resolve a couple more things before it's ready to be looked at again. More specifically, I need a better way of resolving the case where you want to catch all other weights with a specific quantization value, i.e., ```--quantize_float16=conv/*/weights--quantize_uint16=conv/*/biases--quantize_uint8```won't catch all remaining variables and quantize to `uint8`. I do want to support this though. The way I invasion this is if you supply two patterns that resolve to the same weight it will fail. But if you supply a pattern that matches a weight __and__ you supply a fallthrough like `--quantize_uint8` (without any pattern supplied) it won't fail and will quantize all remaining weights with affine `uint8`.It won't take much work but I do want to provide sufficient tests for this mapping scheme. I'll let you know when it's ready to be looked at again.=====", 'Thanks for the careful reviews @pyu10055. Do you have any idea what the timeframe for a new release will look like?=====']

comments: ["@kainino0x Not sure if these warnings will affect the performance. So I prefer to fix these warnings.But there is still one warning left:GPUBuffer.setSubData is deprecated: use createBufferMapped(with copyBufferToBuffer if needed)(but note the design/spec of this API is still in flux).It's a little complicated to use createBufferMapped in currrent design. In TFJS, it uses `BufferManager` to manage all allocated buffers. When we want to use a buffer, we need to call `bufferManager.acquireBuffer` to get a buffer (It can re-use allocated buffer). However, if we change it to createBufferMapped, it will return `[GPUBuffer, ArrayBuffer]`. Should we save `[GPUBuffer, ArrayBuffer]` for BufferManager? Except of setSubData,  getBufferData also uses acquireBuffer. But it   uses copyBufferToBuffer to copy data from a storage buffer to a readback buffer.  Any idea for this warning?=====", "The warnings don't affect performance, but it is necessary to fix them. We will be removing the deprecated items from Chrome in the next few days.An alternative to setSubData has landed in the spec: writeBuffer. I don't think we've implemented that yet so I'll try to remember we need to not remove setSubData yet.=====", "@kainino0x Thanks. I think we can wait `writeBuffer`. I don't have permission to land PR. Feel free to land it if you can.Or add @annxingyuan to do it.====="]

title: fix file:// URLs on Windows
body: BUG In Node.js on Windows, file: URLs have three slashes before thedrive letter. For example: file:///c:/Users/strager/[snip]/nsfwjs/model.jsonWhen converting a file: URL to a file path, NodeFileSystem's routerincorrectly preserves one leading slash. This results in adrive-relative path, which refers to a different file than intended.This leads to errors down the road: Error: Path C:\C:\Users\strager\[snip]\nsfwjs\model.json does not exist: loading failed at C:\Users\strager\[snip]\node_modules\@tensorflow\tfjs-node\dist\io\file_system.js:67:23Use Node.js' built-in functions for dealing with file: URLs instead ofhackily parsing them ourselves.On POSIX systems, this commit should not change behavior.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3436)

title: Move all the remaining chaining api outside of tensor.ts
body: To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3538)
comments: ["This is a large scale change that moves all the the remaining chaining api ops out of tensor.ts. Primarily done using code gen with hand editing after. Its a lot of files but very uniform type of change. I went down this path (automation) for a couple of reasons: 1. Speed up modularization workflow (3 less steps!) 2. Make OpHandler and Tensor as slim as possible with respect to ops as we look ahead towards the work in the backends. In parallel i'm trying to define what precisely we want to keep as part of the tensor type which will have implications on the backend interface and possibly the TensorInfo object backends use. So moving these out is a step in clarifying what we want those interfaces to be. More to come on this in a doc after the holidays. 3. I realized I wanted to move things like the strict* versions of ops out of tensor.ts so that it can be refactor independent of the actual removal of those functions from public api.====="]

title: Add DEBUG_QUERY flag
body: Fix: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/3551This DEBUG_QUERY flag is used for getting performance data of each operators, so no read back and numerical error check.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3552)
comments: ['@annxingyuan, PTAL=====', "Thanks @axinging ! However I don't think this addresses the root cause of https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/3551. Also I think it's necessary to wait for `data()` in order to get accurate profiling information. Without calling `data()` on the output of a GPU program, we can't know that it has finished executing. However it's possible that checking the output for errors distorts the profile - have you observed this? =====", '@annxingyuan  @kainino0x ### Instructions about reproducing how WEBGLQuery distort the profiling:1.  Merge the change in this PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/35522.  Put below file inside tfjs\\tfjs-backend-webgl\\src\\benchmark_models_test.ts, set DEBUG_QUERY(Only WebGLQuery and logs) and DEBUG(WEBGLQuery , ErrorCheck, logs) properly(Do not turn both as true).3.  tfjs-backend-webgl/package.json, add a line:  "benchmark": "karma start --grep=benchmark",4.  and run "yarn benchmark --grep=resnet50 --no-single-run"Expectation: the time logged by console.log(times) should be similar when DEBUG_QUERY is on or off.```// tfjs\\tfjs-backend-webgl\\src\\benchmark_models_test.tsimport * as tfc from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-converter\',import * as tf from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-core\',import {ALL_ENVS, describeWithFlags} from \'@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/jasmine_util\',import * as profiler from \'./profiler\',describeWithFlags(\'Models benchmarks\', ALL_ENVS, () => {  beforeAll(() => {    jasmine.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_INTERVAL = 1000000,  }),  async function benchmark(      benchmarkFn: () => tf.Tensor | tf.Tensor[] |          {[name: string]: tf.Tensor}): Promise<number> {    const start = performance.now(),    let oldLog: any,    let kernels: any = [],    const logOutside = false,    if (logOutside) oldLog = console.log,    if (logOutside) profiler.startLog(kernels, oldLog),    const result = benchmarkFn(),    if (result instanceof Array) {      await result[0].data(),    } else if (result instanceof tf.Tensor) {      const tmp = result,      await result.data(),      tmp.dispose(),    } else {      await result,    }    if (logOutside) await profiler.logKernelTime(kernels, oldLog),    return performance.now() - start,  }  it(\'resnet50\', async () => {    const input = tf.randomNormal([1, 224, 224, 3]),    const url =        \'https://storage.googleapis.com/tfjs-models/savedmodel/posenet/resnet50/quant2/model-stride32.json\',    const model = await tfc.loadGraphModel(url),    const bench = () => model.predict(input),    await benchmark(bench),    input.dispose(),    const times = [],    const trials = 50,    // tf.ENV.set(\'DEBUG_QUERY\', true),    // tf.ENV.set(\'DEBUG\', false),    for (let t = 0, t < trials, ++t) {      const input = tf.randomNormal([1, 224, 224, 3]),      const bench = () => model.predict(input),      const time = await benchmark(bench),      input.dispose(),      times.push(time),    }    console.log(times),    const mean = times.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / trials,    const min = Math.min(...times),    const fmt = (n: number) => n.toFixed(3),    console.log(`Mean time: ${fmt(mean)} ms -> ${fmt(mean / 1)} / rep`),    console.log(`Min time: ${fmt(min)} ms -> ${fmt(min / 1)} / rep`),  }),}),```=====', "@kenrussell We discussed this issue at the Intel/TF.js meeting, with disjoint timer query (or maybe some timing code in TF.js) causing significant slowness as measured from the CPU side. Something we'll probably want to discuss at tomorrow's meeting.====="]

title: Add HashTableV2, LookupTableV2Find
body: Followed api:HashTableV2: https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/HashTableV2LookupTableV2Find: https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/LookupTableFindV2Notes:1. I'm debating the implementation of the table handle. The c++ version has a logic of using shared_name | node.name as the table handle, this is also part of the parameter list of HashTable api. I only partially implement this logic to use a string tensor as the handle. The real benefit of using string tensor though, is to allow the `HashTableMap` to be able to find the `HashTable` by if the key is "equal" to the handle. In tf, "equal" is same value, not shallow equal in Javascript. The use case of this is to allow models to take shared_name as model input, but this use case is only hypothetical. So to fully support using tf.equal to lookup resource, I need to revise the current implementation. Instead of using the Map.get() method, which does a shallow equal, I need to use the tf.equal and download the result of equal to check value. A better solution, however, is to use the tf.while_loop, but this is a much bigger change of how we implement context. I'm leaning toward not supporting the string handle because of all the architecture difference. If the hypothetical use case mentioned above does have a real requirement, we can implement the intermediate solution of just use tf.equal. For future, we can keep in mind to refactor context to something similar to resource manager.2. There will be a separate PR or PRs to support string tensors in multiple ops, slice, unstack, and equal. Until then, the HashTable and LookupTableV2 ops can only support numeric tensors. Given that the LookupTable may be used quite often in language models, we will need to support string tensors.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3576)

title: Modularize fused ops
body: This splits out fused ops into their own files.It doesn't make them modular because they use a pattern that doesn't fit in with how other kernels are implemented and will need some offline discussion. However I wanted to at least save state on moving the code around. To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3597)
comments: ["The underlying issue was that these kernels have an optional input tensor (bias) that is sometimes null. They also use a non-ideal way to pass tensors from forward to backward pass, they close over the reference rather than call save([]) as you can't pass null to save. This is also not compatible with new modular gradients, and in my opinion isn't something we should generally do (nullable parameters). In the backward pass an extra result would be added with bias is not null.Talked with @annxingyuan offline and here are two options I see for this:1. _Split the fused kernels into two versions_, one that takes a bias and one that doesn't. The op can still take an optional bias argument, but it will use that to decide which kernel to call (which will have a fixed/non-variable interface). 2. _Do not support gradients for these kernels_. My understanding from talking to Ann is that these fused op calls are generated by the converter for fast inference. We also only support gradients for fused ops using the linear activation (1 of 5 options). We also don't document these ops publicly so they shouldn't appear in arbitrary code that is used for training. If we go down this route we can still keep the optional input tensor in the kernel definition (though this is still exceptional compared to other kernels) as we don't need to worry about keeping a potentially nullable argument for the backward pass. If we don't really see a need for gradients for fused ops this is a simple approach that allows for more dynamic kernels in future.Thoughts?=====", "Update: After discussion offline, I tried out option 2, but found out we do used the gradients for these in layers. So went back to the custom op approach and ultimately found an approach that worked (and that doesn't require actually changing customGrad or engine. The summary of the approach is to return different customOps depending on which params are passed in. Notes for future consideration: Because CustomGradFunc expects a comma separate list of inputs and then a saveFunc at the end, optional parameters cannot be added (because the last param is non optional). Future refactor should consider separating input tensors into an array argument separate, but that changes the api of customOp.=====", 'One final important note, I had to add a dy.reshape inside the grad func for fused matMul due to the reshape it does at the end of the custom op. But this is now ready for review @annxingyuan =====']

title: Setup release e2e infra.
body: * How to trigger a release e2e flow in CI Any PR that has a release file in the top level directory is a 'release' PR, which will trigger the release e2e flow rather than the regular unit test flow or nightly build flow. The release.ts script that prepares release version will generate such a release file. So PRs to release branches will all go through release e2e flow.* Changes related to Release e2e flow:1. In run-build.sh, only e2e directory will run test, all unit tests in other directories will be ignored. The RELEASE flag is passed to child build.2. e2e's cloudbuild.yml will pass the RELEASE flag to the first step to decide whether prepare for release.3. The first step will run start-verdaccio.sh script. If RELEASE=true, it will publish tfjs packages to local verdaccio registry, and then change e2e's package.json tfjs dependencies to use the locally published version.4. title: custom bundle tool
body: Introduces a CLI tool in the tfjs package, tfjs-custom-bundle that can be used to create entry files (modules) that can be tree shaken by a bundler as part of whole program optimization. The tool isn't complete but this is the first part and in order to keep PRs smaller I figured we could review it piece by piece. Currently it only supports tree shaking programs that only use tfjs-core.It takes a config file as input: [example1](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/core_only/forward_mode_config.json), [example2](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/core_only/training_config.json)And produces an ES module as output that replaces the `import * as tf from ...` statements in a program: [example1](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/core_only/forward_mode_tfjs.js), [example2](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/core_only/training_custom_tfjs.js).Note: eventually the examples in that repo linked above would become e2e tests in this repo. But it is sufficiently experimental at this stage that I want to keep them outside.You can see the results of tree shaking via rollup: [example1](https://ghcdn.rawgit.org/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/master/core_only/dist/forward_mode/forward_mode_rollup_bundle.js.html), (for example 2 not all those kernels have been modularized in those backends, so while the properly tree shake bundle is created it is incomplete and can't run). In particular look at the "kernels" subfolder of each backend, only the modular kernels specified in the config file are included. To achieve this we also need to tell bundlers like rollup and webpack which files are sideffect free. This involves some file reorganization and importantly of a list of files in package.json for files that do have global side effects. Please review these and point out if there any missing (anything that sets up a registry or auto registers anything would be included).FYI running this does require some manual steps as we can't yet remove register_all_chained_ops from core without breaking api. This is planned for 3.x but we will work around this in the mean time.As a note the user uses this tool by installing the @tensorflow/tfjs package and then running`npx tfjs-custom-bundle --config path_to_config.json` the rest is as described in the design doc.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3692)

title: [wasm] Use single Emscripten JS module.
body: This change generates WASM binaries in standalone mode which moves work out of the emscripten-generated JS modules into the binary. In standalone mode, the JS modules for vanilla and SIMD are the same, so we can remove the SIMD module.Here is how the file sizes compare:`master`:tfjs-backend-wasm.js: 27kbtfjs-backend-wasm-simd.js: 27kbtfjs-backend-wasm.wasm: 155kbtfjs-backend-wasm-simd.wasm: 213kb`wasm_standalone`:tfjs-backend-wasm.js: 27kbtfjs-backend-wasm.wasm: 156kbtfjs-backend-wasm-simd.wasm: 214kbThis means we save 27kb in the JS bundle, but the binaries are significantly larger. Performance is unaffected.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3694)

In the case of SIMD, generating with emscripten's `STANDALONE=1` option is enough to remove the differences in the JS modules. title: [tfjs-react-native] Fixed model loading after applying CodePush update
body: [react-native-code-push](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-code-push) allows update js bundle and assets without publishing new version of app package.After applying CodePush update, Asset returns uri in file:// URL form instead of file path. which is okay in most use but since tfjs-react-native uses react-native-fs for loading bundled weights, converting URL to path must be done.This pull request implements file URL detection and converting for solving this problem.and here's quick workaround for before this request accepted:```javascriptimport * as tf from '@tensorflow/tfjs',import {bundleResourceIO} from '@tensorflow/tfjs-react-native',import {Image} from 'react-native',const myModelJson = require('../assets/my_model.json'),const myModelWeights = require('../assets/my_model_weights.bin'),class LocalFileHandler { constructor(modelJson, modelWeightsId) { this.modelJson = modelJson, this.modelWeightsId = modelWeightsId, } async load() { const localFilePath = unescape( Image.resolveAssetSource(this.modelWeightsId).uri.substr( 'file://'.length, ), ), const base64Weights = await RNFS.readFile(localFilePath, 'base64'), const weightData = tf.util.encodeString(base64Weights, 'base64').buffer, const modelArtifacts = Object.assign({}, this.modelJson), modelArtifacts.weightSpecs = this.modelJson.weightsManifest[0].weights, delete modelArtifacts.weightManifest, modelArtifacts.weightData = weightData, return modelArtifacts, }}let resourceIO = bundleResourceIO( myModelJson, myModelWeights,),if ( Image.resolveAssetSource(myModelWeights).uri.match('^file://')) { resourceIO = new LocalFileHandler( myModelJson, myModelWeights, ),}const model = await tf.loadGraphModel(resourceIO),```---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3703)

title: Add TF-Op to tfjs-op mapper to converter
body: This PR introduces a tool to map from TF-Ops (aka TF-kernels) used in the converter/model.json to the corresponding tfjs op the converter calls. It does this by parsing the executor code.All TF-ops that do not map into a tfjs-op are listed in a test file to check that only those ops have empty mappings. This includes ones we expect (like TensorListGetItem) as well as a few that should map to ops but don't currently because they used chained ops (e.g. Placeholder). A followup PR will remove chained op calls from converter (similar to #3706). With that the list of unmapped ops will shrink.This tool is run on build/test and the result is checked into the repo (metadata/kernel2op.json) so that we can have a mapping specific to each commit (and more importantly each release) of tfjs.We need this mapping to generate custom op imports for the converter based on a specific model.json.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3726)

title: make flags dependency in io namespace explicit
body: - Make dependencies on IS_BROWSER flag being registered explicit. - Also move registration of `BrowserLocalStorage.URL_SCHEME` and `BrowserIndexedDB.URL_SCHEME` from the top-level of thier corresponding IO handlers to the platform_browser file. This co-locates side effects that happen in a browser environment and removes global side effects from the IO handler files themselves.This fixes a bug we say in syncing to g3 where sometimes flags.ts would get loaded after io/indexed_db.ts (for examples). Since the dependency between the two is implicit rather than explicit. This makes that link explicit which imo is a good pattern and makes it easier to move around other imports as we separate side-effectful code from non side-effectful code.cc @dsmilkov (this externalizes (and makes more complete) the fix in my last sync cl).A bigger question is whether we want to replicate this pattern in all modules that depend on some flag being evaluatable. In many cases we have been able to rely on load order as defined in our imports. And once all the side effects and registries have been disentangled from code that we want to tree shake, relying on load order might be sufficient. But I suspect making the dependency explicit is beneficial for documentation/debugging) purposes, and arguably more correct.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3848)
comments: ['@pyu10055 for http it does call fetch through a method (`env().platform.fetch()`) rather than the flag mechanism, so I think that is sufficiently explicit for resolution/specifying load order. There would also be a clear exception if not platform is registered. The flags issue caused a very subtle problem where our tests would pass because by the time they run the flag has been registered but the code might throw an exception at load time depending on how the files got loaded. =====']

title: model.json support in custom bundle tool & converter
body: This PR adds support for creating custom bundles of tfjs that use tfjs-converter to execute a model. There are a lot of files in the diff but many are a change of pattern repeated across different files. I'll try and give high level context of the problem and solution here. But you can see how this is used in [this sample application using blazeface](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/tree/master/blazeface). ### Primary challenge:We need to determine which ops the converter will call for a given model and make sure only those ops get added to the final bundle. However the converter imports many more ops as part of the op executors that drive model inference.### High level solution:In the converter's [op executors](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/tree/master/tfjs-converter/src/operations/executors), rather than doing:```jsimport * as tfc from '@tensorflow/tfjs-core',tfc.max(...),```We do```jsimport * as tfOps from '@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/ops/ops_for_converter',tfOps.max(...)```By default tfOps exports all ops in core. But in a custom build a bundler can [alias that module](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/blazeface/rollup.config.js#L27) to a [generated module containing only the ops](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/blazeface/blazeface_tfjs/custom_ops_for_converter.js) used by the model. Thus tfOps becomes smaller and the final bundle is smaller.Other symbols can still be imported from `@tensorflow/tfjs-core` and will go through the regular tree-shaking done by bundlers.Pretty much everything else is in support of this and other aspects of supporting model.json in custom builds.### Aliasing modulesThis change also fleshes out the workflow creating custom builds on the user end and in particular is geared towards support module aliasing features in bundlers. This allows users to switch from regular to custom builds by changing their build files rather than their source code. For example the aliasing defined in this [rollup file](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/blazeface/rollup.config.js) allow [this source file](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/blazeface/blazeface_demo.js) to keep importing from `@tensorflow/tfjs` but automatically get re-routed to custom build files. This will generally be a better developer experience as it makes switching from full to custom builds easily as feature development is done (a user could even build full and slim bundles and even test them in the same setup).### Breakdown of changes- **[tfjs-converter]** Convert `import * as tfc from '@tensorflow/tfjs-core',` -> `import * as tfOps from '@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/ops/ops_for_converter',` in all executors and their corresponding tests. Rollup file has also been updated to correctly create a script tag bundle.- **[tfjs-core]** add `src/ops/ops_for_converter.ts` that exports everything from ops.- **[tfjs-core]** Move namespaced ops like `image.resizeBilinear` from `src/ops/resize_bilinear` to `src/ops/image/resize_bilinear`. i.e. We make the namespace match the path. This allows us to easily map from a call like tfOps.image.resizeBilinear to a path on disk in order to generate a [custom ops_for_converter](https://github.com/tafsiri/tfjs-treeshake/blob/master/blazeface/blazeface_tfjs/custom_ops_for_converter.js) that correctly recreates the namespace. The diffs for these files come purely from updating import paths that they reference and that reference them. Fused op op files have been renamed to match the path/naming convention. No public exports have changed.- **[tfjs] cli tool** Add support for parsing model.json files and generating a custom ops_for_converter.js files.- **[tfjs] cli tool** Generate a custom 'tfjs-core' module in addition to the previously generated custom 'tfjs' module. This avoids circular dependencies after aliasing because our libraries internally import @tensorflow/tfjs-core- **[tfjs, e2e]** karma.conf files have been updated to match webgl and layers karma.conf files.- **[tfjs-wasm]** name of exported function from DepthwiseConv2dNativeConfig changed to correctly match the kernel name (2D => 2d).To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3854)

title: [converter]Support table initializer in converter.
body: **Background:**For saved model graphs that have hashtable or lookuptable operations, the underlying hashtable needs to be initialized before being used. From graph architecture, the initialization subgraph is detached from the inference subgraph, so that initialization doesn't happen in every inference. To support hashtable ops in TF.js, we made below changes: 1. Extract the initialization subgraph and store its topology in `modelInitializer` field in model.json. See this PR. 2. Load the initialization subgraph and execute it during model load. See https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3975 3. Add hashtable ops implementation and add hashtableMap in model. Only dispose the hashtables when model is disposed. (To resume this PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3576)**Changes in this PR:**1. Get `table_initializer` from `meta_graph` `collection_def['table_initializer']`.2. Use the nodes in `table_initializer` as outputs to extract a initializer subgraph and freeze the graph using `convert_variables_to_constants.py` and grappler.3. Extract the Const ops' values in the initialization graph to weights file.4. Created a `modelInitializer` field in model.json. Store the initialization graph's topology in the `topology` subfield. Store the outputs in the `outputs` subfield.**Notes: ** 1. This implementation only handles table initializer. We intentionally don't generalize to other initializers until we know the use case. 2. This solution only solves saved model in 1.x style. For 2.x style, we need more investigation how to support table initializer.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3958)

title: Log error caught when creating WebGL context
body: My day today: I spent a _long_ time debugging the error `Initialization of backend webgl failed` on a particular machine. Ultimately, the cause was really obscure: Chrome was returning `null` from `canvas.getContext` when passed [this `failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat` flag](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/c823c1f944fcf97c8070fd75036da8f4bf14c660/tfjs-backend-webgl/src/canvas_util.ts#L27). Another line in TensorFlow assumes that `getContext` cannot return null, and so throws an error `TypeError: Cannot read property 'isContextLost' of null`. This is another bug. But that error was then silently swallowed at the line here.On restarting the machine, Chrome mysteriously stopped behaving this way. But that underlying issue is a story for another time.The point is, silently swallowing all thrown errors is a pretty bad practice. title: [converter] Add table initializer to graph execution.
body: **Background:**For saved model graphs that have hashtable or lookuptable operations, the underlying hashtable needs to be initialized before being used. From graph architecture, the initialization subgraph is detached from the inference subgraph, so that initialization doesn't happen in every inference. To support hashtable ops in TF.js, we made below changes: 1. Extract the initialization subgraph and store its topology in `modelInitializer` field in model.json. See PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3958 2. Load the initialization subgraph and execute it during model load. See this PR. 3. Add hashtable ops implementation and add hashtableMap in model. Only dispose the hashtables when model is disposed. (To resume this PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3576)**Changes in this PR:**1. Add modelInitializer to the model and graph representations.2. In `load` method last step `loadSync`, load the initialization subgraph into memory through method `transformInitializer`, and then execute the subgraph.3. Refactored `GraphExecutor`'s execute method into private method `_execute` and two public methods `execute` and `initialize`, which will use the private method to execute the graph. The shared logic in `_execute` can run a graph given an ordered node list. The original `execute` method takes care of user provided inputs and outputs. The `initialize` method doesn't have inputs tensors, so it just calculates the ordered list and call `_execute`.4. Added a method to calculate ordered list for initialization subgraph which is basically consist of Const ops and other ops, no input tensors.**Notes:** 1. This implementation only handles table initializer. We intentionally don't generalize to other initializers until we know the use case.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/3975)
