title: Avoid keeping pointer to temporary strings
body: substr() creates a temporary string which will be deallocated, leaving the c_str() pointer pointing to garbage.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4016)
comments: ['> > _[Reviewable](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4016)_ status: 0 of 1 approvals obtained (waiting on @estyrke)> > _[tfjs-node/binding/tfjs_backend.cc, line 1142 at r1](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4016#-MItdRwS3gm9HOLWcn4G:-MItdRwS3gm9HOLWcn4H:b8a0tqh) ([raw file](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/6177e7174b688a93fcbd74e09b52e3ce546f7346/tfjs-node/binding/tfjs_backend.cc#L1142)):_> > > ```c++> >       input_tensor_index = 0,> >     } else {> >       input_tensor_index = atoi(input_op_index.c_str()),> > ```> > Is the concern that the temporary string was not disposed? If so here the temporary string is created?Not exactly. The problem is on this line: ```c++const char *input_op_index = name.substr(index + 1).c_str(),```The expression `name.substr(index + 1)` creates a temporary variable whose scope ends at the end of the "full-expression" (essentially the end of this line). The `c_str()` call then takes the address of the string pointed to by this temporary variable. Thus, after this line, the pointer in `input_op_index` points to an already deallocated memory area. When the pointer is then used on the line you pointed out, the result is undefined. In most cases, the memory contents may still be there and no problem is observed. But if the deallocated memory area has already been cleared or reused, the atoi (or the strlen before it) will fail. This is what we observed on our compiler (VS 2019) - the strlen returns 0 and the output_tensor_index (in our case) will always be zero no matter which output we try to select.In general, it is risky to hold on to the value returned by c_str, since it is an unmanged C pointer which will be undefined if used after its backing std::string has been deallocated - It is better to only call it "temporarily" when it is needed, such as within the atoi call here.=====', "VC2019 prints a warning to this effect, unfortunately I don't have a windows computer at hand now so I can't quote it.====="]

title: Python converter bugfix
body: ## MotivationThe Python converter code supports writing boolean weights, but not reading them. This causes problems when reading TFJS models from Python.Furthermore, the Python converter fails to read scalar string weights. Numeric scalar weights are read just fine, but string scalars cause an error.## Implementation`np.bool` has been added to the list of supported input dtypes.The deserialization code for string arrays has been fixed so the size calculation always returns a valid `int`.## DetailsScalars are stored in the weight manifest with an empty shape ([]), which is technically correct to reflect the nature of a scalar.The string deserialization uses `np.prod()` to calculate the total number of items. Unfortunately, `np.prod()` returns `1.0` when given an empty iterable (see [numpy docs](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.prod.html) under _Notes_).This value cannot be used with `range()` later, which leads to an error in situations where a weight manifest contains string scalars (e.g. model [SSD OpenImages v4](https://tfhub.dev/google/openimages_v4/ssd/mobilenet_v2/1)).---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4037)

title: Implement HashTable ops
body: **Background:**For saved model graphs that have hashtable or lookuptable operations, the underlying hashtable needs to be initialized before being used. From graph architecture, the initialization subgraph is detached from the inference subgraph, so that initialization doesn't happen in every inference. To support hashtable ops in TF.js, we made below changes: 1. Extract the initialization subgraph and store its topology in `modelInitializer` field in model.json. See PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3958 2. Load the initialization subgraph and execute it during model load. See PR: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3975. 3. Add hashtable ops implementation. See this PR.**Changes in this PR:**1. Add ResourceManager class, used to share model resources, such as HashTables. Currently, the resourceManager only stores hashTable maps, but it is easy to extend to store other resources. For the hashtable, there are two maps, hashTableNameToHandle and hashTableMap. hashTableNameToHandle is used to get the hashTable handle from node name. node name is used as inputs for a node, if any node needs hashTable as input, the name of the hashTable name will be in the inputs list. The step happens when an executor getParams for a node. hashTableMap is used to get the actual hashTable from the handle's id. This step happens when after getParams, a handle is found. 2. Add HashTable class, which contains operations on hashTables, such as import and find.3. The HashTable receives keys and values as tensors, but will transform keys to primitive value to store. This allows O(1) lookup time. As a comparison, if keys are stored as tensors, lookup time is O(N), N = # of elements in the table. This is because Javascript doesn't have a mechanism to override hashing and equal operator. The downside of this approach is the key tensor values need to be read out, but the time cost should be minimal.4. Also fixes an error in e2e suite, graph_models => graph_model, to allow tests actually run in the convert_predict.ts file.5. Because of above fix, actually found a memory leak in loading graph with complex64 data, that is also fixed in this PR.6. Added a e2e test for a model that takes a key tensor, initializes a hashtable, and lookup the key tensor in the hashtable and outputs the result.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4060)

title: Use versioned CDN URL in readme example
body: Is there a backward compatibility guarantee with the `@tensorflow/tfjs/dist/tf.min.js` file? If so, please close this pull request.If there is no backwards compatibility guarantee, then it seems like a bad idea to have a non-versioned URL in the examples, since users often copy-and-paste without realising that they need to add a version to ensure their code doesn't break when breaking changes are introduced to the library. [This page](https://publicwww.com/websites/%22tfjs%2Fdist%2Ftf.min.js%22+depth%3Aall/) shows 79 web pages without a version, and this search is very likely non-exhaustive (sites must reach some threshold to popularity to be indexed by that search engine). If v3 has breaking changes, there could be hundreds of sites that break.The only disadvantage here is that the readme will need to be updated with each new release. This could be avoided by adding a comment above the script tag saying "change 2.6.0 to the latest version", or something like that, and then only updating the version number in the readme every now and then.Assuming there is no backwards compatibility guarantee, I hope you'll consider merging this - mainly to help newbies who don't realise the trouble with non-versioned CDN urls :)---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4123)

title: Fix gradient for min and max
body: Closes #4135 Adds a regression test to guard against #4130 (which seems to be fixed at HEAD at the time of that issue being reported).To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4136)
comments: ["Good question. There were a few things I noticed. - The grad function would itself try and transpose the output if permutedAxes was not null. However the gradForMinAndMax helper function would also do this as part of the helper function, effectively nullifying each other (though the outer transpose was called without permutedAxes which just seemed odd).- The min and max grad functions seemed to be written against the eariler definition of the kernel in the forward func. For example looking at how the code [was at 1.7.4](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/tfjs_1.7.4/tfjs-core/src/ops/reduction_ops.ts#L384), you can see that that op would sometimes to an internal transpose before passing the input to the backend implementation, however the original input is what gets passed to the gradient. So I believe the gradient was trying to match the shape of what gets passed to backend.max internally. However in new modular kernels there is no op level transformation and thus no transpose to account for (any internal transposition done within the forward kernel are completely hidden). So the extra 'transposition handling' code becomes unnecessary. =====", 'Ah, makes sense!=====']

title: Run CI on a single machine by generating cloudbuild files.
body: Instead of running each CI test on a separate Google Cloud machine, generate a cloudbuild.yml file to test all affected packages on a single machine. The benifits of this strategy include the following:* Fewer machines are required for a single test (2 instead of up to 12), so queuing should happen much less often.* Packages only need to be built once, instead of once per machine.* Multithreaded steps have access to more cores.When CI is run, the root cloudbuild.yml is launched on Google Cloud. This file has only three steps: Install yarn dependencies, run `yarn generate-cloudbuild-for-packages`, and run `run-build.sh`. The second step finds what packages were affected by the change and combines their cloudbuild.yml files into a single `cloudbuild_generated.yml` file, and the third step launches the generated build on Google Cloud. The steps in the generated build are set to `waitFor` each other according to the dependency tree `scripts/package_dependencies.json`, and each package's `build-deps` step is removed in favor of waiting for its dependencies to be built.Each package's cloudbuild file still works as expected, and there are two new yarn commands at the root: * `yarn test-packages` tests all packages affected by a change. It performs the same steps as CI.* `yarn generate-cloudbuild-for-packages [PACKAGE]...` generates the cloudbuild file to test each `PACKAGE` and packages it might affect. If given no packages, it detects what packages have been changed in the current PR.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4147)

Release 2.3.1

Bug Fixes and Other Changes

  • Fixes an undefined behavior causing a segfault in tf.raw_ops.Switch (CVE-2020-15190)
  • Fixes three vulnerabilities in conversion to DLPack format (CVE-2020-15191, CVE-2020-15192, CVE-2020-15193)

  • Fixes segfault raised by calling session-only ops in eager mode (CVE-2020-15204)

  • Fixes segfaults caused by incomplete SavedModel validation (CVE-2020-15206)

TensorFlow 2.3.0

Release 2.3.0

Major Features and Improvements

  • tf.data adds two new mechanisms to solve input pipeline bottlenecks and save resources:
    • snapshot
    • tf.data service.

In addition checkout the detailed guide for analyzing input pipeline performance with TF Profiler.

  • tf.distribute.TPUStrategy is now a stable API and no longer considered experimental for TensorFlow. (earlier tf.distribute.experimental.TPUStrategy).

  • TF Profiler introduces two new tools: a memory profiler to visualize your model’s memory usage over time and a python tracer which allows you to trace python function calls in your model. Usability improvements include better diagnostic messages and profile options to customize the host and device trace verbosity level.

  • Introduces experimental support for Keras Preprocessing Layers API (tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.*) to handle data preprocessing operations, with support for composite tensor inputs. Please see below for additional details on these layers.

  • TFLite now properly supports dynamic shapes during conversion and inference. We’ve also added opt-in support on Android and iOS for XNNPACK, a highly optimized set of CPU kernels, as well as opt-in support for executing quantized models on the GPU.

  • Libtensorflow packages are available in GCS starting this release. We have also started to release a nightly version of these packages.

  • The experimental Python API tf.debugging.experimental.enable_dump_debug_info() now allows you to instrument a TensorFlow program and dump debugging information to a directory on the file system. The directory can be read and visualized by a new interactive dashboard in TensorBoard 2.3 called Debugger V2, which reveals the details of the TensorFlow program including graph structures, history of op executions at the Python (eager) and intra-graph levels, the runtime dtype, shape, and numerical composistion of tensors, as well as their code locations.

title: Bug fixes for local benchmark tool
body:
- Correctly show WASM_HAS_MULTITHREAD_SUPPORT flag value, and make it "tunable". Also sort all flags to make them easier to read. Before: https://screenshot.googleplex.com/5iyTQriVUfeGjAg After: https://screenshot.googleplex.com/A57sSAuoBvxogJs- Currently, when benchmarking a built-in model, it will first ask users to replace "-1" in the input tensor (https://screenshot.googleplex.com/5eTX73hkUBW7YNT). Then if user clicks "run benchmark" button *again*, it will start the benchmark. This is kind of broken, because users cannot actually edit the input tensor field for built-in models. This PR fixes this logic by only prompting about replacing "-1" in input tensor when benchmarking a **custom model**. It will also make benchmark to run after user clicks the button the first time.- The following steps are broken in the current tool. 1. After page is loaded, start a benchmark with WASM backend with simd checked. 1. After benchmark is done, uncheck the simd option, and run benchmark again. 1. An error message is shown: https://screenshot.googleplex.com/ArQe6p97n3aAGyq (This also happens in webgl backend when users toggle flags in different runs)

The root cause is: the model loading logic only happens when users change the model, NOT when users change flags. In the example above, when user unchecks the simd option, a new WASM backend will be registered, but the tensors allocated during tf.loadGraphModel (when model was loaded) will still [point to](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L1136) the *old* WASM backend which is now disposed (and the wasm field is [set to null](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-backend-wasm/src/backend_wasm.ts#L130)). This PR fixes this by re-loading the model when the flags are changed. After the fix: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTc1NjUzOTkyNTE2ODEyOHw0Njc1ZmQyMi0yMg ---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4275)

title: Quantization fix
body: ## MotivationThe Python converter's de-quantisation function doesn't match the tfjs converter and causes data loss:```pythonimport tensorflowjs as tfjsimport numpy as npd = np.array([-0.2345, 0.0468, 0.3456, 0.], dtype=np.float32)q, metadata = tfjs.quantization.quantize_weights(d, np.uint16)de_q = tfjs.quantization.dequantize_weights(q, metadata)np.testing.assert_array_almost_equal(de_q, d) # this will fail```The tfjs de-quantisation works properly and the problem only exists with the python converter.## ExplanationThe de-quantisation rounds the weights to integers before converting them to the target `dtype` (e.g. `float32`), see [quantization.py line 160](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/17d79c13b7784409623b75f7bdcfb499a8e6ffd0/tfjs-converter/python/tensorflowjs/quantization.py#L160).This is not only inconsistent with the behaviour of the TS version (see [tfjs-core io_utils.ts line 155](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/479b02311cc9930619e8e068dce211f8315f5372/tfjs-core/src/io/io_utils.ts#L158)), but also causes data loss, this primarily affects normalised FP weights (e.g. values in the range [0,1] or [-1,1] resp.).## Proposed FixThe changes test whether the de-quantisation should result in `float32` values and doesn't round values after scaling if that is the case. The behaviour of integer case (e.g. de-quantisation to `int32`) remains unchanged.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4285)

Release notes

TensorFlow 2.4.0

Release 2.4.0

Major Features and Improvements

  • tf.distribute introduces experimental support for asynchronous training of models via the tf.distribute.experimental.ParameterServerStrategy API. Please see the tutorial to learn more.

  • MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy is now a stable API and is no longer considered experimental. Some of the major improvements involve handling peer failure and many bug fixes. Please check out the detailed tutorial on Multi-worker training with Keras.

  • Introduces experimental support for a new module named tf.experimental.numpy which is a NumPy-compatible API for writing TF programs. See the detailed guide to learn more. Additional details below.

  • Adds Support forTensorFloat-32 on Ampere based GPUs. TensorFloat-32, or TF32 for short, is a math mode for NVIDIA Ampere based GPUs and is enabled by default.

  • A major refactoring of the internals of the Keras Functional API has been completed, that should improve the reliability, stability, and performance of constructing Functional models.

  • Keras mixed precision API tf.keras.mixed_precision is no longer experimental and allows the use of 16-bit floating point formats during training, improving performance by up to 3x on GPUs and 60% on TPUs. Please see below for additional details.

  • TensorFlow Profiler now supports profiling MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy and tracing multiple workers using the sampling mode API.

  • TFLite Profiler for Android is available. See the detailed guide to learn more.

  • TensorFlow pip packages are now built with CUDA11 and cuDNN 8.0.2.

Breaking Changes

  • TF Core:

    • Certain float32 ops run in lower precsion on Ampere based GPUs, including matmuls and convolutions, due to the use of TensorFloat-32. Specifically, inputs to such ops are rounded from 23 bits of precision to 10bits of precision. This is unlikely to cause issues in practice for deep learning models. In some cases, TensorFloat-32 is also used for complex64 ops.TensorFloat-32 can be disabled by running tf.config.experimental.enable_tensor_float_32_execution(False).
    • The byte layout for string tensors across the C-API has been updated to match TF Core/C++, i.e., a contiguous array of tensorflow::tstring/TF_TStrings.
    • C-API functions TF_StringDecode, TF_StringEncode, and TF_StringEncodedSize are no longer relevant and have been removed, see core/platform/ctstring.h for string access/modification in C.
    • tensorflow.python, tensorflow.core and tensorflow.compiler modules are now hidden. These modules are not part of TensorFlow public API.
    • tf.raw_ops.Max and tf.raw_ops.Min no longer accept inputs of type tf.complex64 or tf.complex128, because the behavior of these ops is not well defined for complex types.
    • XLA:CPU and XLA:GPU devices are no longer registered by default. Use TF_XLA_FLAGS=--tf_xla_enable_xla_devices if you really need them, but this flag will eventually be removed in subsequent releases.

  • tf.keras:

    • The steps_per_execution argument in model.compile() is no longer experimental, if you were passing experimental_steps_per_execution, rename it to steps_per_execution in your code. This argument controls the number of batches to run during each tf.function call when calling model.fit(). Running multiple batches inside a single tf.function call can greatly improve performance on TPUs or small models with a large Python overhead.
    • A major refactoring of the internals of the Keras Functional API may affect code thatis relying on certain internal details:
      • Code that uses isinstance(x, tf.Tensor) instead of tf.is_tensor when checking Keras symbolic inputs/outputs should switch to using tf.is_tensor.

      • Code that uses tf.map_fn/tf.cond/tf.while_loop/control flow as op layers and happens to work before TF 2.4. These will explicitly be unsupported now. Converting these ops to Functional API op layers was unreliable before TF 2.4, and prone to erroring incomprehensibly or being silently buggy.
      • Code that directly asserts on a Keras symbolic value in cases where ops like tf.rank used to return a static or symbolic value depending on if the input had a fully static shape or not. Now these ops always return symbolic values.
      • Code already susceptible to leaking tensors outside of graphs becomes slightly more likely to do so now.
      • Code that tries directly getting gradients with respect to symbolic Keras inputs/outputs. Use GradientTape on the actual Tensors passed to the already-constructed model instead.
      • Code that requires very tricky shape manipulation via converted op layers in order to work, where the Keras symbolic shape inference proves insufficient.

title: remove default registration of chaining api [3.x_dev]
body: Removes the default addition of the chain api to tensors in tfjs-core.This ended up being a large PR because of a change that needed to be done to all the chain op augmentors. Apologies for the size of it, there isn't a straightforward way to split this up and get everything passing. The following pattern changed:`Tensor.prototype.opName = function()...` -> `getGlobalTensorClass().prototype.abs = function()`This is because of how node.js module resolution (gnd caching) works across package boundaries. Basically an `import {Tensor} from ...` can result in different `Tensor` being imported into the module based on the original path. Thus the augmentation of the Tensor prototype would not propagate outside of package that initiated it. This would result in behaviour where a tensor returned by a method in core could have a different prototype (and thus different methods) from a tensor created another package that imported a registerThis change uses the same mechanism we use for ENGINE and other things we need to be truly global across our packages (which have had a similar experience). We use getGlobal to store a single reference to the class/prototype we want to modify, this regardless of which package a tensor augmentation starts in, it always uses the right module reference.So all of the changes in tfjs-core/src/public/chained_ops/* are of the same nature. Then there are some other fixes to actually adapt the packages and test runs.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4413)

comments: ['@qjia7 @axinging @haoyunfeix @gyagp Please take a look, thank you.=====', 'I encountered the issue about how to introduce this feature to developers, in this patch,1. Introduced a "DRIVER_SUPPORT_FLOAT16" flag,2. Introduced a "enableFloat16Mode()" API.If developers want to use the float16 feature, they must be use "enableFloat16Mode()" to explicitly enable this feature. If developers does not enable this feature but use this feature, tfjs-core could throw errors.There is another way to introduce float16 feature. We could only introduce a "DRIVER_SUPPORT_FLOAT16" flag, and developers are responsible for their usages. If developers use the float16 but driver does not support float16, they would get error and undefined result.Which way is more reasonable？=====', 'Hi, @lina128 ,1. Move the flag to flags_webgpu.ts,2. It is not a universally better option. Float16 is a good option that users pay more attention to computation speed. But if users want high accuracy, I think it is better using float32.I also removed the "enableFloat16Mode" api here, I think that users does not need to explicitly enable float16 feature. Whether or not to use float16 feature depends on model\'s data type or input data type.=====', "> Can you add an annotation on how float16 is represented by Uint16Array?Sorry, I do not fully understand your question. Uint16Array is only the storage for float16, because the element size of Uint16Array and float16 are the same(16 bits), and float16 is not the standard data type on CPU side, so we save float16 into an Uint16Array object.float16's format is as https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-precision_floating-point_format, and we could convert a float to float16 according to http://www.fox-toolkit.org/ftp/fasthalffloatconversion.pdf algorithm. It is the same style as C++ code, we will use uint16_t to save float16 data on CPU side.=====", '@tafsiri @pyu10055 Please take a look, thank you.=====']

title: [webgl] Reference for WebGL stft memLeak fix.
body: Fix issue https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4378There are two issues related to STFT failure1. Complex components cannot be release if there are multiple references on the components and those reference are disposed before the complex tensor is disposed.2. STFT uses RFFT which uses a shallow_slice, there is a bug in shallow_slice that copied refCount and complexParentRefCount from the original tensor to the output tensor, which cause the tensors to have extra refCount and complexParentRefCount.Problem 1 is solved by sync engine ref count to backend, reset the output tensor ref counts in the shallow_slice fixed problem 2. To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4448)

title: add prioritizeBackend, expose getSortedBackends
body: I observed some backends are registered with the same priority, like [webgl](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-backend-webgl/src/base.ts#L25) and [wasm](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-backend-wasm/src/base.ts#L27), both with priority `2`. In this case, it is not trivial to predict which backend will be sorted with the highest priority, as per the [getSortedBackends](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L375) implementation.More generally, a consumer may wish to manage backend priorities on its own.This change proposes to include priorities in the array returned by `getSortedBackends`, and expose a new `prioritizeBackend`.Usage example:```jsconst backends = tf.getSortedBackends(),// [{name: 'wasm', priority: 2}, {name: 'webgl', priority: 2}, {name: 'cpu', priority: 1}]// favor webgl over wasmtf.prioritizeBackend('webgl', 3),// [{name: 'webgl', priority: 3}, {name: 'wasm', priority: 2}, {name: 'cpu', priority: 1}]await tf.ready(),```---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4491)

title: Avoid building tfjs-core twice in CI
body: tfjs-core's 'build-deps-always' cloudbuild rule runs 'yarn build-deps-ci', which, due to a circular dependency with tfjs-backend-cpu, first builds tfjs-core before building its dependencies. The 'build' cloudbuild rule then builds tfjs-core again right after tfjs-backend-cpu is built. Since tfjs-core imports tfjs-backend-cpu for testing only, and uses `require()` notation to do so, this rebuild is unnecessary. This commit removes the extra rebuild of tfjs-core.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4518)

title: Fix WASM JS script not working after minification
body: In my previous PR, I replaced ```if(_scriptDir)``` with ```if(typeof _scriptDir !== "undefined" && _scriptDir)``` in the emscripten-generated JS script. I did it in backend_wasm.ts where the script content is imported. But it doesn't really work when end users minify the code through a bundler, because "if(_scriptDir)" cannot be found anymore in the minified code.To make this work, the code replacement has to happen right after the code is generated, which is in build-wasm.sh. I added a node.js script to do the code replacement there.Another thing I had to do is that by default, terser (the plugin we use to minify code in rollup) will transform ```typeof _scriptDir == "undefined"``` into ```_scriptDir === void 0```, which will break our code (it will throw "_scriptDir is not defined" error). To prevent this, I need to turn off that option in terser in WASM's rollup.config.js. I also updated the README.md file to let users know they need to turn this option off if they want to minified the code by themselves. I tested this in various situations:- Use full script through script tag- Use our own minified script through script tag- Use bundler with minification (esbuild, the one used in https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4539)Because I based this fix on top of the version after Yannick's merge, so please ignore rollup.config.helpers.js (which was added in Yannick's PR). For the tfjs-backend-wasm/rollup.config.js file, please only look at line 124-129. The rest of the changes in that file came from Yannick's PR that makes rollup.config.helper.js work.Thanks!Fixed https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4539---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4562)

title: Fix memory leak for complex tensors
body: Fix issue #4378There are two issues related to STFT failureComplex components cannot be release if there are multiple references on the components and those reference are disposed before the complex tensor is disposed.STFT uses RFFT which uses a shallow_slice, there is a bug in shallow_slice that copied refCount and complexParentRefCount from the original tensor to the output tensor, which cause the tensors to have extra refCount and complexParentRefCount.Problem 1 is solved by sync engine ref count to backend, reset the output tensor ref counts in the shallow_slice fixed problem 2.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4563)

title: Engine/backend refCount refactoring
body: The PR aims to clean up the refCount mechanism in both engine and backends. This follows the [PR that fixed the complex tensor memory leak](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/4564), which caused by mismatch of refCount between engine and WebGL backend.Here are main changes in this PR:1. Removed the refCount from engine TensorInfo, engine only tracks the tensors and mapping between DataId and Backend.2. Backend disposeData method is called on the dataId of the tensor for every disposal and backend will determine if the dataId is ready to be disposed, it will return a boolean to indicated success of the disposal. Engine will only remove the DataId mapping when it is disposed successfully in the backend.3. When Engine calls makeTensor or makeTensorFromDataId from backend dataId, it would just track the mapping of dataId to backend, but makeVariable needs to increase backend refCount, since it is an extra reference from the variable to the dataId that exists only in the engine.4. Engine clone tensor for gradient would need to call backend Identity op to increase ref count in the backend to prevent disposal prematurely.5. Removed complexParentRefCount from WebGL, since complex components can be tracked sufficiently by backend refCount.6. Added refCount tracking to node and WASM backend.7. compileAndRun method in WebGL should return TensorInfo instead of Tensor, since it is used in the Backend ops, returning Tensor would add engine tracking to the DataId and cause unnecessary disposal by scope.8. When DataId is moved across backends, the source backend will force disposal, and the refCount is copied to the destination backend, this will ensure no premature disposal in the destination backend.This would affect WebGPU backend due to backend interface changes. @qjia7 To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4628)

title: Add broadcast args
body: As per the issue I raised #4624, I added support for [BroadcastArgs](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/BroadcastArgs?hl=ca) based on the XLA implementation in [tensorflow](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/dec8e0b11f4f87693b67e125e67dfbc68d26c205/tensorflow/compiler/tf2xla/kernels/bcast_ops.cc#L32) which eventually calls [Bcast](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/dec8e0b11f4f87693b67e125e67dfbc68d26c205/tensorflow/core/util/bcast.h#L135). The result should match to what Bcast sets as _output.To match the tensorflow documentation, this function takes two tensors and returns a tensor.The integration tests were based on me running the following in python:```import tensorflow as tftf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[1,1], s1=[1,1], name=None)tf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[1,1], s1=[4,2], name=None)tf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[1,6], s1=[3,1], name=None)tf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[1,6], s1=[3,1,1,1], name=None)tf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[1,6,-1], s1=[3,1,1,1], name=None)tf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[1,2], s1=[1,3], name=None)tf.raw_ops.BroadcastArgs(s0=[[1,1],[1,1]], s1=[[1,1],[1,1]], name=None)``` I have one performance concern that I'd like guidance on if possible. I'm making heavy use of `arraySync` inside this function which I fear may lead to stalls during runtime. Are there any recommendations to fix this issue?Thanks for the review.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4636)

title: Keep values on CPU
body: To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4753)
comments: ["@lina128 @pyu10055 take a look, thanks.Keeping values on CPU is 1) convenient for `moveData` when switching backends. For example, if we switch backend from webgl to wasm, when calling `readSync` in webgl, we don't need to read data back from gpu to cpu.2) convenient for WebGPU since it doesn't support read data back from gpu synchronously. Otherwise, when switching from webgpu to other backends, it will report `WebGPU readSync is only available for CPU-resident tensors.` error.Another option is totally to remove `readSync` and use `async read`. Then we need to change the current logic in tfjs-core.Cc @haoyunfeix @axinging @xhcao =====", "> I don't think it is a typical use case for user to switch from WebGL to WASM. For WebGPU this probably only helps constant tensors, that was originally on the CPU, not any output tensors, which do not have value field populated.> In current e2e benchmark framework, for the same model, we can try different backends. The error will happen when you switching from WebGPU to other backend. It's just a temporary workaround to make this situation work well for webgpu. Like you said, it can't resolve the situation that tensor doesn't have cpu values. For the latter, it may happen on hybrid mode. But it seems that there is no solution for WebGPU if we don't use the async read.I just modified the change only for webgpu to make it work for e2e benchmark when integrating webgpu. For future, we still hope tfjs-core can use async read everywhere. > I think the bigger issue is how to sync data when switching from WebGPU to other backend? The current codebase has many places uses readSync, it would be a really big change to remove the API.> Can WebGPU simulate sync read with a blocking poll?> As far as I know, WebGPU only support async read. It seems that there is no way to call an async read in a sync method.====="]

title: Use official emsdk bazel toolchain
body: Build tfjs-backend-wasm with the [official emsdk toolchain](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk/tree/master/bazel) open-sourced from google3.Using the official toolchain fixes the issue where normal, simd, and simd + threaded builds write their artifacts to the same output location, invalidating the build cache. With this change, outputs are created in separate folders, enabling build caching.Additionally, the emscripten toolchain is now automatically downloaded as a dependency within Bazel, so it no longer needs to be installed separately.A [minor edit](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/4769/commits/e9530cf79b0c6df79d80b4c5896ac79a74e5d711) to the official toolchain was needed to make simd work correctly with XNNPACK.This PR also enables remote build caching for the wasm backend on CI runs.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4769)
comments: ["Remote caching is not working in GCP yet, but is working with a locally run 'remote' cache. I'm sending this out for review now, but we might want to delay merging it until after the remote cache is working on GCP (which I'm pretty sure just requires some GCP config changes but might require some changes to this PR as well).=====", 'Note to reviewers: Everything in `emscripten_toolchain/` is from the [emsdk Bazel toolchain](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk/tree/master/bazel/emscripten_toolchain) with a [minor edit](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/4769/commits/e9530cf79b0c6df79d80b4c5896ac79a74e5d711). Also, the new toolchain required a few changes to the cc source files, mostly involving removing unused variables. These are detailed in [remove unused variables](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/4769/commits/2e719ca19ecaf19ca541b7bb25bac9a472eb4996).=====', "I tried this on my mac, and I think this PR may break support for compiling wasm on OSX and Windows. It looks like the build rules only ship with Linux binaries for emscripten. I'll check with the author.Edit: looks like there's an issue open for this: https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk/issues/650=====", "Support for operating systems other than linux has been [fixed](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk/pull/766) in emsdk, and the way the toolchain is loaded has been significantly simplified (it's now loaded as an external repository instead of copied into our workspace).I've tested this PR on my mac again, and it now compiles and passes the tests. I think it's ready to be merged, but PTAL again. Thanks!=====", 'Great work, thank you Matt!=====']

I'd like to get to the bottom of this. There must be a reason FFT behaves differently in this case. Thanks for your patience.=====", 'There was a typo using an important variable invoking rfft. title: [webgpu] Use uniform instead of constant for shape
body: This reverts https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/3647 and adds:1. support float/int uniform buffers, merge all uniforms into one uniform buffer.2. store shape strides and shape size in uniform buffer.3. turn shapes to shape lengths to save shader in makeShaderKey.These changes will save warmup time. For all e2e related model, this saves wamup time from 60% ~ 90%. And no obvious performance regression is found.TODO: remove all shapes from all shader key, such as ConcatProgram, CropAndResizeProgram, PadProgram.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4819)

However, the `size` and `strides` can also be computed in the shader, and the uniforms can be removed for `size` and `strides`.For memory bound, I think putting these calculation into shader is better.For compute bound, I think putting these calculation into cpu and uploading to uniform may be better. Per my understanding, most of kernels are memory bound. Maybe putting the calculation into shader is better? But I am not sure. So I want to hear all your opinions about this. @axinging If it's convenient for you, can you collect some data under these two situations? It's also possible that there is no big difference for these two.=====", "The key logic compute strides is as below, this sure can be done in GPU(shader) or CPU(This PR proposed):```export function computeStrides(shape: number[]): number[] {  const rank = shape.length,  if (rank < 2) {    return [],  }  const strides = new Array(rank - 1),  strides[rank - 2] = shape[rank - 1],  for (let i = rank - 3, i >= 0, --i) {    strides[i] = strides[i + 1] * shape[i + 1],  }  return strides,}``` If done in CPU, shader need to access this by uniform (For 4d, this will be three int32). And think about that we already have other data in the uniform buffer(such as in/out shapes), For most case, those uniform data can be fetched into one or two cache line(s), for example, when running yarn test, the uniform byte length ranges from 12-120. So, I think three int32(worst case) will not add too much memory IO.If done in GPU(shader), every thread instance will compute same computeStrides above, this will have bad influence on power. Anyway, during my test, I didn't found any obvious performance regression when compute stride in CPU, so I think current compute stride in CPU is not bad idea at perf and power side. comments: ['@axinging  @haoyunfeix @gyagp, PTAL=====', "I thought it's been designed in this way, to constrain users to only set tunable flags (the keys of `TUNABLE_FLAG_TYPE_MAP`). If this blocks we testing some new flags we could add flag to TUNABLE_FLAG_TYPE_MAP.=====", "> I agree with Yunfei, the idea is for benchmark tool, it will reset the flags to a fix state, so we are sure that what is being used for the benchmark, not trying to incremental change flags.> The issue is that webgpu is a real async implementation. So it will meet error if you use promise in a sync function in some situation, see #4303, #4492.  So to resolve that issue, we set `CHECK_COMPUTATION_FOR_ERRORS` to false for webgpu. However,  if we use `env().setFlags` in e2e, it will reset  `CHECK_COMPUTATION_FOR_ERRORS`  to true for webgpu and result in a lot of errors again.`CHECK_COMPUTATION_FOR_ERRORS` is a tunable value for other backends, but for webgpu, currently it must be false. So that's why I suggest use `set` instead of `setFlags` so that it doesn't affect other flags' value which are not in `TUNABLE_FLAG_VALUE_RANGE_MAP`.My understanding is that `TUNABLE_FLAG_VALUE_RANGE_MAP` just lists the flags that you can tune and the corresponding values that you can set in this benchmark. However, it shouldn't affect other flags that are not in this list.====="]

title: Build tfjs-core and tfjs-backend-cpu with Bazel
body: This PR adds Bazel BUILD targets for tfjs-core and tfjs-backend-cpu. The following commands can invoke the new Bazel targets. Yarn rules have not been added for them since Bazel not the default way to build yet.- `yarn bazel build //tfjs-core:tfjs-core_lib` compiles tfjs-core.- `yarn bazel test //tfjs-core:tfjs-core_test` tests tfjs-core with a headless browser.- `yarn bazel run //tfjs-core:tfjs-core_test` launches tfjs-core tests in a browser and waits for human interaction.- `yarn bazel test //tfjs-core:browserstack_tfjs-core_test` tests tfjs-core on BrowserStack. Only Chrome on MacOS is enabled at the moment. This test requires that `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME` and `BROWSERSTACK_KEY` are set in your environment.- `yarn bazel run //tfjs-core:browserstack_tfjs-core_test` (theoretically) launches tfjs-core tests in a BrowserStack session for debugging and waits for you to connect before running the tests. I haven't been able to test this yet since I can't seem to get an interactive session to start (probably due to network issues).Currently, these build targets use esbuild for bundling since it was the easiest to set up. We will probably use Rollup for some cases e.g. to support es5. Targets for publishing to npm (i.e. `pkg_npm`) are not yet written.This PR also sets up Bazel CI tests. CI tests use a Bazel query to find what targets should be tested, so any Bazel target with `tag = ["ci"]` will be tested in CI. Bazel remote caching is now working, so we run all the tests on every commit and let Bazel figure out what actually needs to be run.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4856)

comments: ['LGTM.@pyu10055 @lina128 @jinjingforever take a look, thanks.=====', "> > _[Reviewable](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4862)_ status: 0 of 1 approvals obtained (waiting on @qjia7 and @xhcao)> > _[tfjs-backend-webgpu/src/backend_webgpu.ts, line 404 at r3](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4862#-MWkKAtX2_qLQbIO29DT:-MWkKAtX2_qLQbIO29DU:bimfrlb) ([raw file](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/a3d7639d87ebbf159570a5480e71795c5cf688e3/tfjs-backend-webgpu/src/backend_webgpu.ts#L404)):_> > > ```> >     res['getExtraProfileInfo'] = () =>> >         kernelMs.map((d, i) => ({name: flattenedActiveTimerNames[i], ms: d}))> >             .map(d => `${d.name}: ${d.ms}`)> > ```> > When supportTimeQuery is false, d is likely null or d.ms is 0. Can you do something like in this PR? https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/pull/4640/files> > When the extension is not available, it times the gpu execution plus download to cpu time. Not ideal, but still informational.There is no `dataSync` method on webgpu backend, it only supports download to cpu asynchronously, if we follow webgl backend, it times the GPU execution, download to cpu time, plus system rescheduling time, and the rescheduling time is very large.=====", 'For example, if there are N operators in model, and the pairs of [s1, e1], [s2, e2], …, [sN, eN] are the beginning time stamp and the ending time stamp.On WebGL, https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/97cde443aebe04152f873c464a79436efab2bb67/tfjs-core/src/profiler.ts#L53, use `dataSync` to get result, the time axis is defined,  ‘ s1, e1, s2, e2, …, sN, eN’, so we could compute the correct spending time for operators, which are e1-s1, e2-s2, …, sN-eN.On WebGPU, we could only use the async method `getBufferData`, the time axis is undefined, It may be ‘s1, s2, …, sN, …, e1, e2, …, eN’, but e1-s1, e2-s2, …, eN-sN are not the correct spending time for operators.=====']

WhenWEBGPU_DEFERRED_SUBMIT_BATCH_SIZE is one, it will become to the oldimmediate mode.queue.submit has a fixed cpu overhead. So it's not efficient to call ittoo many times. Here we use an empirical value 15, which is observed over 5%performance improvement for mobilenet/resnet50 on different platforms.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4888)

title: Initial TFLite support
body: This PR adds the `tfjs-tflite` package. It adds the `TFLiteModel` class that implements `InferenceModel` (similar to saved model or graph model) and the corresponding `loadTFLiteModel` function. Under the hood, it uses the tfweb_model_runner from the tfweb WASM module and JS client downloaded from google storage. Please see README.md for the basic setup instructions.I also added a demo to show how this package can be used. I chose the cartoongan model which I think is more significant and fun than the mobilenet model. Also, the cartoongan model is not supported by current task libraries so it won't be duplicated with our future demos for task library support.[live demo](https://storage.googleapis.com/tfweb/demos/cartoonizer/index.html) to try it out.This is the first step. Some TODO items:- Integrate with CI.- Add types for task libraries.- Publish npm.- Add initial APIs in tfjs-model repo to support task libraries.Please take your time! title: Add essential types for all supported tflite task libraries
body: Also, the tfweb js client issue I mentioned should be solved. I realized that I shouldn't export types from d.ts file itself. This wouldn't work because d.ts file is basically a reference for the ts compiler and its content won't appear in the final binary. Instead, I extract the root type to a separate file, and export that file instead. Then, at the client side (e.g. from another package that uses this package), I can import the root type, and easily construct the js client there. In this way, the code duplication is kept to a minimum. The ground truth stays in this package.I created another PR (not finalized yet) in the tfjs-models repo for the tasks API: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/pull/639. You can see how the tfweb js client type is being used there. Also, please see how the task library types defined here are used in that PR to create the initial tasks API (please feel free to leave tasks API related comments there). Thanks!(Also, I needed to revert the commonjs plugin version to the older one, because the new version doesn't bundle the tfweb js client code for some reason. title: [wasm] Fix wasm backend not starting any threads
body: Without the linker option `PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE` set, the wasm backend does not create any webworkers and spins forever waiting for them to be created (crashing the browser). This PR sets `PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE` to `Math.min(4, Math.max(1, (navigator.hardwareConcurrency || 1) / 2))`, meaning it will use half of the logical cores available up to a max of 4 (or only 1 if `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` is not available). See [this comment](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/pull/10263#issuecomment-582010187) for details on why this works. This option apparently supersedes the value passed to [`pthreadpool_create` in `backend.cc`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/c9dfebddfa34f531d2f0c363b6ea574a9fe9745d/tfjs-backend-wasm/src/cc/backend.cc#L65-L66), but its current setting should match the value computed in the `.cc` file. Fixes #4932 This PR also fixes a bug where webworkers created by the wasm backend were not removed when `dispose` is called. Fixes #4796.Fixes #4934 as well.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/4957)
comments: ["The [thread count computed in `backend.cc`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/c9dfebddfa34f531d2f0c363b6ea574a9fe9745d/tfjs-backend-wasm/src/cc/backend.cc#L65-L66) could perhaps be removed and replaced with `pthreadpool *threadpool = pthreadpool_create(1),`, but that might make it create N webworkers but only use 1. I haven't tested this yet.=====", 'Fixes #4934:![Wasm Threaded Simd](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1474501/115773478-39b32c00-a365-11eb-8f7d-ef42c49f8f61.png)=====', '> Hi Jiajia, the flag you proposed is different than this one, #4942, right? For both flags, do you expect them to be tunable?Yes. #4942 is just a get method. I hope we can control the threads number or pool size. Do you know the relationship between the `PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE` and the thread number in `pthreadpool_create`? @lina128 @mattsoulanille =====', 'They should be same. From https://emscripten.org/docs/porting/pthreads.html:"Optionally, pass the linker flag -s PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=<integer> to specify a predefined pool of web workers to populate at page preRun time before application main() is called. This is important because if the workers do not already exist then we may need to wait for the next browser event iteration for certain things, see below.When pthread_create() is called, if we need to create a new Web Worker, then that requires returning the main event loop. That is, you cannot call pthread_create and then keep running code synchronously that expects the worker to start running - it will only run after you return to the event loop. This is a violation of POSIX behavior and will break common code which creates a thread and immediately joins it or otherwise synchronously waits to observe an effect such as a memory write. There are several solutions to this:Return to the main event loop (for example, use emscripten_set_main_loop, or Asyncify).Use the linker flag -s PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=<integer>. Using a pool creates the Web Workers before main is called, so they can just be used when pthread_create is called.Use the linker flag -s PROXY_TO_PTHREAD, which will run main() on a worker for you. When doing so, pthread_create is proxied to the main browser thread, where it can return to the main event loop as needed."=====']

title: [node] Add `SummaryFileWriter.histogram` TensorBoard logging
body: I'm opening this WIP PR, in which I have a partial implementation of a Node.js counterpart to [`tf.summary.histogram`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/summary/histogram). This PR is in WIP status, as I've hit a small blocker, and would like to ask how I can continue from here.To compare my implementation to a correct one, I first tried to generate a histogram of 10 normal distributions, each shifted by `i / 10` in Python. This gave me this result in TensorBoard:![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/990794/118531843-96c4b680-b746-11eb-9bef-16b7f518034a.png)Now, if I try to generate the same histogram using my Node.js implementation, I get the following result, which is obviously wrong:![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/990794/118531640-582efc00-b746-11eb-9661-4e88dca91445.png)I'm fairly confident that the values produced by my implementation of the `bucket` function are correct. The [Python implementation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorboard/blob/master/tensorboard/plugins/histogram/summary_v2.py) describes that the values should be as follows:```py"""A histogram summary stores a list of buckets. Each bucket is encoded asa triple `[left_edge, right_edge, count]`. Thus, a full histogram isencoded as a tensor of dimension `[k, 3]`.In general, the value of `k` (the number of buckets) will be a constant,like 30. There are two edge cases: if there is no data, then there areno buckets (the shape is `[0, 3]`), and if there is data but all pointshave the same value, then there is one bucket whose left and title: Make tfjs-node create a new TFJSBackend for each environment
body: This fixes issue #4947.`tfjs-node` assumes a single global `TFJSBackend` for all `napi_env`s. This assumption holds for most applications, but not when embedding node in C++ with multiple environments or when using web workers. The user observes typical non-deterministic behavior with random crashes and weird error messages.To resolve this, a map is created that holds a `TFJSBackend` for each `napi_env`.Cleanup wasn't handled by the previous global implementation, so it's also not handled by this implementation. This may be undesirable. I also did this quickly to fix an issue I was having with little regard for style, DRYness, or other considerations, so hope it's a useful starting point for a project developer at least.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5108)

title: Use Bazel and ts_library to build core and backend-cpu
body: This PR builds tfjs-core and tfjs-backend-cpu using Bazel and makes the build outputs available to the other packages in the monorepo.# New Bazel `tools` directoryThis PR adds a new `tools` directory that includes Bazel rules and macros for building TensorFlow.js## `tools/defaults.bzl`Defines default versions of `ts_library` and `esbuild` that are specific to the tfjs repo. * `ts_library` is set to use `es2017` and has its `tsconfig.json` file set to `tsconfig_ts_library.json`. * `esbuild` has the correct esbuild binary for the user's platform pre-selected. `esbuild` is used for tests since it is very fast.## `tools/tfjs_bundle.bzl``tfjs_bundle` is a macro to build bundles for tfjs. It defines several `rollup_bundle` targets and their minified variants: * `[name].es2017[.min].js`: A UMD es2017 bundle. * `[name][.min].js`: A UMD es5 bundle. * `[name].fesm[.min].js`: An es2017 flat es modules bundle. * `[name].node[.min].js`: A commonjs es5 node bundle. (Note: This may be removed) Rollup plugins and options are defined in the `rollup_template.config.js` file. ## `tools/tfjs_web_test.bzl``tfjs_web_test` is a macro that defines several `karma_web_test` targets, most of which are run on BrowserStack: * `[name]`: A local `karma_web_test` target that runs using chrome. * `browserstack_[browser_name]_[name]`: A `karma_web_test` that runs on BrowserStack using `[browser_name]`. * Browsers are defined in `tools/karma_template.conf.js` * The macro allows selecting which browsers to test with via the `browsers` keyword argument.## `tools/copy_to_dist``copy_to_dist` is a rule that creates symlinks for a given tree of files in another directory. It is used to copy the `ts_library` compilation results from `src` to `dist` to support creating an npm package with outputs in `dist`. It is also used to copy bundles from `tfjs_bundle` to `dist` (and any other files that need to be in `dist`).To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.# Building `tfjs-core` and `tfjs-backend-cpu` with BazelThere are several steps to building `tfjs-core`. While `tfjs-core` itself does not depend on a backend, its tests require `tfjs-backend-cpu`, so we build them separately to avoid a circular dependency.The following Bazel targets build `tfjs-core` without tests:* `//tfjs-core/src:tfjs-core_src_lib`: Builds all of `tfjs-core` excluding tests and the `index.ts` entrypoint. * Uses `module_name = "@tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist"` so that its files can be imported relative to that path. e.g. `import @tensorflow/tfjs-core/dist/public/chained_ops/register_all_chained_ops`.* `//tfjs-core/src:tfjs-core_lib`: Builds `index.ts` entrypoint and depends on `//tfjs-core/src:tfjs-core_src_lib`. * Uses `module_name = "@tensorflow/tfjs-core"` so it can be imported as `@tensorflow/tfjs-core`.After `tfjs-core` is built, `tfjs-backend-cpu` can be built by the following rules:* `//tfjs-backend-cpu/src:tfjs-backend-cpu_src_lib`: Like with core, builds all of `tfjs-backend-cpu` excluding tests and the `index.ts` entrypoint. Depends on `//tfjs-core/src/tfjs-core_lib`.* `//tfjs-backend-cpu/src:tfjs-backend-cpu_lib`: Like with core, builds the `index.ts` entrypoint. These steps are similarly separated so that `module_name` can be set differently for each.With `tfjs-backend-cpu` built, `tfjs-core` can be tested:* `//tfjs-core/src/tfjs-core_test_lib`: Builds all the test files.* `//tfjs-core:tfjs-core_node_test`: Runs `tfjs-core_test_lib` tests in node.* `//tfjs-core/src:tfjs-core_test_bundle`: Builds a browser bundle for tests.* `//tfjs-core:tfjs-core_test`: Runs web tests using the bundle.* There are several other tests, like snippets tests and async backends tests.With `tfjs-core` tests build, `tfjs-backend-cpu` can be tested:* `//tfjs-backend-cpu/src:tfjs-backend-cpu_test_lib`: Builds cpu tests.* `//tfjs-backend-cpu:tfjs-backend-cpu_test`: Runs cpu tests in node.# Creating NPM packagesThe `pkg_npm` rule is used to create an npm package for `tfjs-core`, but there are a few steps that need to be done first:* `//tfjs-core:tf-core`: Bundles `//tfjs-core/src:tfjs-core_lib` using `tfjs_bundle`.* `//tfjs-core:copy_bundles`: Copies bundles to `dist/` (in bazel's output folder).* `//tfjs-core:copy_src_to_dist`: Copies the compiled results of `//tfjs-core/src:tfjs-core[_src, _test]_lib` to `dist`.* There are a few other copy rules to copy things like the miniprogram files and test snippets code.Once bundles are built and everything is copied, the npm package can be created:* `//tfjs-core:tfjs-core_pkg`: Packages everything into an npm package.A similar process to the above is used to package `tfjs-backend-cpu`.# Inter-operating with existing packagesPackages in the monorepo that don't yet use Bazel are linked to each other via `link:../package-name` dependencies in their `package.json` files. These link dependencies expect the outputs of building a package to appear in the package's directory, but Bazel doesn't allow that. Instead, Bazel places build artifacts in a location completely separate from the source files. This output directory can change, but there is a symlink to it named `dist` for easy access. This means we can just change the `link:../` dependencies to point to `../dist/bin/tfjs-backend-cpu/tfjs-backend-cpu_pkg`, right? Unfortunately, we can't, because of how node resolve dependencies. Suppose we're building `tfjs-layers`, which depends on `tfjs-backend-cpu`. If we link to `../dist/bin/tfjs-backend-cpu/tfjs-backend-cpu_pkg`, then when `tfjs-backend-cpu` imports / requires `@tensorflow/tfjs-core`, it moves up the `dist/bin/tfjs-backend-cpu` directory tree and looks in the root `node_modules` of the `tfjs` repo. Due to some specifics of how `ts_library` works, this `node_modules` contains an incomplete copy of `@tensorflow/tfjs-core` that is created by Bazel for running node tests, so the import fails.We can't replace `link:../` with `file:../` because that would result in multiple imports of multiple copies of the same code, which creates several copies of things that are supposed to be singletons, like `io` handlers.To work around these issues, this PR creates a new top-level `link-package` that provides a place where bazel-built packages can be `link:../`ed from. Its `package.json` currently lists `@tensorflow/tfjs-core` and `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-cpu` as `file:../` dependencies copied from `../dist/bin/...`. With this new link package, `tfjs-layers` and others can now list `@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-cpu` as `link: ../link-package/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-cpu`. Now, when `tfjs-backend-cpu` looks for `tfjs-core`, it will find the correct `tfjs-core`, since the link package has both installed in its `node_modules`. The link package should never be published to npm, and will be removed once the monorepo fully builds with Bazel.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5133)

7.4.6

Bug fixes

  • Fixed a ReDoS vulnerability (00c425ec).

A specially crafted value of the Sec-Websocket-Protocol header could be usedto significantly slow down a ws server.

for (const length of [1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]) {  const value = 'b' + ' '.repeat(length) + 'x',  const start = process.hrtime.bigint(),
value.trim().split(/ *, */),
const end = process.hrtime.bigint(),
console.log('length = %d, time = %f ns', length, end - start),}

The vulnerability was responsibly disclosed along with a fix in private byRobert McLaughlin from University of California, Santa Barbara.

In vulnerable versions of ws, the issue can be mitigated by reducing the maximumallowed length of the request headers using the --max-http-header-size=sizeand/or the maxHeaderSize options.

Bumps [ws](https://github.com/websockets/ws) from 7.4.4 to 7.4.6.
Release notes

Sourced from ws's releases.

7.4.6

Bug fixes

  • Fixed a ReDoS vulnerability (00c425ec).

A specially crafted value of the Sec-Websocket-Protocol header could be usedto significantly slow down a ws server.

for (const length of [1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]) {  const value = 'b' + ' '.repeat(length) + 'x',  const start = process.hrtime.bigint(),
value.trim().split(/ *, */),
const end = process.hrtime.bigint(),
console.log('length = %d, time = %f ns', length, end - start),}

The vulnerability was responsibly disclosed along with a fix in private byRobert McLaughlin from University of California, Santa Barbara.

In vulnerable versions of ws, the issue can be mitigated by reducing the maximumallowed length of the request headers using the --max-http-header-size=sizeand/or the maxHeaderSize options.

7.4.5

Bug fixes

  • UTF-8 validation is now done even if utf-8-validate is not installed(23ba6b29).
  • Fixed an edge case where websocket.close() and websocket.terminate() didnot close the connection (67e25ff5).

title: Fix webgl backend memory leak in firefox
body: In #3319, users reported that there is significant memory leak in firefox when running the bodypix demo with the webgl backend. I tracked down the problem which was caused by calling `.data()` [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/blob/master/body-pix/src/body_pix_model.ts#L549). Looks like in the webgl backend's `read()` method, we created a WebGLBuffer to read data but we never deleted the buffer. This didn't cause issues in Chrome because (I guess) the buffer might get automatically deleted which is not the case in firefox.I added the deleteBuffer call and the memory leak was gone from my local testing. Will update the demo after this PR is merged.BTW, we also use `.data()` in some other places (like in blazepose with tfjs-webgl backend). It has [memory leak in firefox](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a8rJNMgkC0u2M21A4orlYihvV7buziLd/view?usp=sharing) too. This should also fix that. To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5193)

title: webgpu: Optimize depthwise conv2d
body: PERFTo see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5209)
comments: ["@kainino0x @lina128 @jinjingforever Please take a look, thanks.In our last meeting, I ever said that the perf of depthwiseConv2d was almost 2x slower than webgl on Intel GPU. With this change, the perf is close between webgpu and webgl.hand_detector:<!--StartFragment-->DepthwiseConv2dNative | 13.88-- | --<!--EndFragment-->becomes<!--StartFragment-->DepthwiseConv2dNative | 8.28-- | --<!--EndFragment-->This optimization is mainly for filter size 3x3 and stride size is 1x1. It's widely used for all of we tested models.For such kind of depthwise conv2d, due to the stride size is only 1x1, there will be many data are repeated access in each channel tile. If we only calculate one output data in one invocation, we need to access 3x3 data in `x` and 3x3 data in `filter`. So to get a 4x4 output data, we need (3x3+3x3)* (4x4) = 288 times memory access. However, if we calculate 4x4 data in one invocation, we only need to access (3x6)*4 data in `x` and (3x3)*4 data in `filter`. So it needs (3x6 + 3x3) * 4 = 108 times, which is only half of previous one.====="]

This surprised me, so I took a look at how we test tfjs-react-native.tfjs-react-native isn't part of the monorepo, so it doesn't use `link:../` dependencies to link to other TensorflowJS packages. It has a `link` command in its package.json, but its never used by CI. Instead, it builds against whatever versions are specified in its package.json. tfjs-react-native runs tests with an example app `integration_rn59`. It has several commands in its package.json to copy monorepo dependencies to `node_modules`, but it only copies the `dist` directory and not the whole package (this is likely a bug that by chance hasn't caused any issues yet). When react-native tests are run in CI, they copy the tfjs-react-native package into the test app but [don't actually copy any other dependencies](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/50a5932c0fc75d3c3888c484ce6e1362fad73152/tfjs-react-native/integration_rn59/scripts/test-ci.sh#L28-L31). title: Add the missing backend initialization in runKernel
body: This is related to #5237 **Background**Most of our kernels will create/convert tensors before calling `ENGINE.runKernel` ([example](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/fixrunkernel/tfjs-core/src/ops/greater.ts#L45-L46)). In those cases, `convertToTensor` will eventually call `ENGINE.makeTensor` where `this.backend` will be [referenced](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/fixrunkernel/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L808). `this.backend` has a side effect that will [initialize the backend](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/fixrunkernel/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L216). This design allows our backend to be lazily initialized. The similar lazy backend initialization also happens in `runKernelFunc`. See this [code block](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/fixrunkernel/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L607-L614).**The problem**Some kernels do **not** create/convert tensors before calling `ENGINE.runKernel`. For example, [linspace](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/fixrunkernel/tfjs-core/src/ops/linspace.ts#L41), [fill](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/fixrunkernel/tfjs-core/src/ops/fill.ts#L42), etc. As a result, when they call `ENGINE.runKernel`, an error will be thrown when calling `getKernel` [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-core/src/engine.ts#L538), because `this.backendName` is not set since the backend has not been initialized.**The fix**I copied the code block about lazily initializing backend from `runKernelFunc` to `runKernel` which should fix this problem (tested locally). This was probably missed during the kernel modularization process when we switched from `runKernelFunc` to `runKernel`. To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5251)

title: [webgl]Fix conv2d when width is odd.
body: Fix https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4844.Background:This bug is not recently introduced, it seems it has been existing since the beginning. The algorithm that special handle packed x with odd number of cols. The algorithm assumes xTexData.shape's height, width and inChannels are same as x.shape. However, they can be different, in which case, the texShape is wrong, so the result is wrong. Imagine the input image x has a shape [3, 3, 1]. When we call conv2D for the first time, it is not packed, so we use the algorithm in the if condition in `conv2dByMatMul`, x is reshaped to [1, 9, 1]. When the texture is uploaded to GPU, it is packed, xTexData.shape is [1, 9, 1] and xTexData.texShape is [10, 2]. When we call conv2D for the second time, x is packed, so we use the algorithm in the else condition. x is shallowly reshaped to [1, 12, 1], and xTexData.shape is shallowly mutated to [1, 10, 1], texShape is still [10, 2], which result in 2 data missing. Imagine a case where x is already packed. Its xTexData.shape will be [3, 3, 1] and xTexData.texShape will be [12, 2]. For the else condition, x is shallowly reshaped to [3, 4, 1], and xTexData.shape is shallowly mutated to [3, 4, 1], texShape is still [12, 2], no data is lost.Given that the algorithm in the else condition assumes shape match between x and xTexData, the fix is to check this assumption and only use the algorithm when shapes match.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5264)

title: Fix #5273: Refactor IOHandlers to use same JSON parsing
body: Fixes #5273.It seems that when #83 was fixed, the parsing and serialization of the new `trainingConfig` field wasn't implemented in all IOHandlers. Additionally, each IOHandler has its own custom logic for how to parse and serialize between `ModelArtifacts` and `ModelJSON`.This PR fixes this by adding two functions, which (almost) all IOHandlers can use instead of their custom logic.- `getModelArtifactsForJSON`, which parses a `ModelJSON` into a `ModelArtifacts`- `getModelJSONForModelArtifacts`, which serializes a `ModelArtifacts` into `ModelJSON`This PR also adds handling of the `trainingConfig` field to the above functions.I then refactored all IOHandlers (except `BrowserIndexedDB`) to use these methods. For IndexedDB, I could not do the same refactor, as `BrowserIndexedDB` saves `ModelArtifacts` directly to IndexedDB, without serializing to `ModelJSON` first.This thus fixes #5273 for all IOHandlers. I also added tests to ensure that they could all load and save artifacts containing a `trainingConfig`.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5274)

This function is called when there's a backend change, so the change here only makes sure the initial flag setting is false. What you probably want is to only allow false for webgpu backend. title: webgpu: optimize matmul with small output size
body: Current matmul algorithm dispatches logical threads based onoutput size, if output size is small and inner dimension sizeis large, there are few threads and every thread should handlelarge loads, so the performance is poor.This patch dispatches logical threads based on output size andinner dimension size, increases the logical threads, makes loadbalancing.This patches also introduces two shared memory buffers, somelogical threads could handle arithmetic operations and othershandle IO operations between barrier api, makes ALUs and load/storeunits work simultaneously, could improves the performance.To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5342)

title: [webgl]Fix PadV2 with empty size.
body: Fixes: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/4716 and https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/issues/5291It seems models trained with Google's ObjectDetection API can generate tensors with 0 in shape, such as [0, 4], which is the input to PadV2, this causes error in our WebGL backend when creating texture. title: [tfjs-data] Fix an issue caused by incorrectly cloning certain iterator
body: When concatenating one iterator to another (e.g. `tf.data.csv(...).concatenate(...)`), `tf.data` stores them in an `ArrayIterator`. When "running" those iterators, the `ArrayIterator` would deep clone them (see [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-data/src/iterators/lazy_iterator.ts#L504)). During the cloning process, it will recursively go through all the iterable objects (hence "deep"). The main purpose of doing the clone is for correctly cloning all the tensors.The function ([`isIterable`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/80b5a04d7a6a62f430816e190a1bf3ed7d340d4b/tfjs-data/src/util/deep_map.ts#L248)) to check whether an object is iterable or not has a bug. It will treat all `Promise` objects as iterable objects. This will cause issues for certain iterators that have fields that are `Promise`s. For example, in `SkipIterator` (used by `tf.data.csv`), there is a `lastRead` field ([here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/80b5a04d7a6a62f430816e190a1bf3ed7d340d4b/tfjs-data/src/iterators/lazy_iterator.ts#L561)) that is a `Promise`. The old `isIterable` function thinks it is iterable, so it will try to deep-clone it instead of just assigning its value to the cloned object. The end result is that the cloned `lastRead` object is no longer a `Promise`. It becomes a plain `Object`. That's why users saw the `TypeError: this.lastRead.then is not a function` error mentioned in #5375. The fix is to add a check to make sure `Promise` objects will not be treated as iterable objects. After adding this check, another bug was revealed: we also need to make sure all text decoder related objects are not treated as iterable objects as well, or [`Utf8Iterator`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs/blob/master/tfjs-data/src/iterators/byte_chunk_iterator.ts#L88) cannot be cloned correctly. I added two tests to cover these use cases. Fixes #5375 To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5444)

This PR simply remove the duplicate export statements.The duplication might cause following issue when bundling `tfjs` (for example, use `parcel-bundler`) into a webapp:![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10307875/128878496-4939d021-faa4-4a25-9629-3df409c7c649.png)I have created a simple repo to reproduce this issue, please check [here](https://github.com/whitedogg13/tfjs-pr-test-app)To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5450)

title: Make Bazel npm outputs match current packages
body: Make npm packages generated by Bazel match what we currently publish to npm.```tfjs-core/ package.json dist/ index.js # <-- ESModule format index.d.ts tf-core.node.js # <-- CommonJS node bundle ...```Also, add a webpack regression test to e2e that makes sure webpack can consume the npm packages we publish.Additionally, it fixes a bug in version tests that was caused by setting `package_name` of a js_library and `module_name` of a ts_library to the same value. [See this for more details.](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/4e73b8820acf7368ba874b09567547627573595f/tools/defaults.bzl#L206-L218)Fixes #5382To see the logs from the Cloud Build CI, please join either our [discussion](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs) or [announcement](https://groups.google.com/a/tensorflow.org/forum/#!forum/tfjs-announce) mailing list.---This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/tensorflow/tfjs/5451)
